name: fdps_map_actor_behavior_step
role: Advances one map actor by a single step according to the behavior mode stored in its record, then marks the actor dirty and redraws one frame.
plate_comment:
Advance a single map actor one behavior step.

Algorithm:
Resolves the actor record for the given index through the record accessor at 0002d210 (the same record is reachable as DAT_00069cd8 + index * 0x50, confirming a 0x50-byte stride). If bit 0 of record[5] is set the actor is inactive and the function returns immediately.

Otherwise it reads the behavior mode from the low nibble of record[0x34] and two byte parameters record[0x35] / record[0x36] (a destination pair), plus an event slot index in record[0x3d], and dispatches:
  mode 0, 1, 2, 9  -- try the movement handlers 00012c10 / 000126b0 / 000127c0 / 00012230 in a fixed order and fall back to 000120d0 when every attempt fails. Mode 9 first queries 0002dc20 for a target and, when one exists, walks toward it via 000119e0.
  mode 3           -- like mode 9, but keyed on 00012c10 succeeding first; on a resolved target it clears DAT_00069cd0.
  mode 4, 7        -- clear DAT_00069cd0 and walk toward the record[0x35]/record[0x36] destination via 000119e0. Mode 7, on arrival, plays the "Posion.saf" effect through 00026e00 when the terrain byte record[7] lies in 0x24..0x27, then sets bit 0 of record[5] to retire the actor.
  mode 5           -- event step: if the per-slot flag (&DAT_000640d8)[record[0x3d]] is still clear and 00013e10 yields a destination, walk there; on arrival read a 3-byte entry at DAT_0006013c + slot * 3 + 0x53, copy it into record[0x31]/record[0x32], call 00025d20 when the first byte is zero, set the slot flag, call 0002e910, switch the actor to mode 7 and play "Chess.wav" via 0002a1f0.
  mode 8           -- no action.
  mode 10, 11      -- the interactive/driven modes: 00013040 or 00013420, gated extra handlers 00027180 / 00013c90 when DAT_00063f8c / DAT_00063f88 reach 6, then 00012230, and finally 00012e50 or the 000126b0 / 000120d0 fallback depending on DAT_00063f78. Mode 11 additionally invokes 00010760 when the terrain byte record[7] is in 0x3c..0x3e.

After dispatch it re-reads the record, calls 0002e030 with the actor's current x/y and 1, sets bit 0x80 of record[5] to mark the actor for redraw, and calls fdps_render_view_frame.

Parameters:
  actor_index -- index into the actor record array at DAT_00069cd8 (0x50 bytes per record).
  context     -- second stack argument, passed unchanged to every movement handler.

Returns:
  Nothing.
evidence: Both arguments arrive on the stack ([EBP+0x14], [EBP+0x18]) and the function ends with a plain RET, so the caller cleans up: __cdecl, not the Watcom register default. The first argument is used both as an index (IMUL EAX,[EBP-0x48],0x50 added to DAT_00069cd8) and as the argument to 0002d210, which proves 0002d210 is the actor record accessor and the record stride is 0x50. The body is a flat if/else chain on (record[0x34] & 0xf) with values 0..0xb, each arm calling a different combination of the 00012xxx/00013xxx handler family with the same two arguments, which is the shape of a per-actor behavior dispatcher rather than any CRT or AIL routine. Terrain-keyed effects tie it to a tile map: record[7] in 0x24..0x27 triggers the "Posion.saf" effect string at 0006155c, and "Chess.wav" at 00061550 is played on event completion, both game-specific assets, so the pool is fdps. The tail (mark dirty bit 0x80, call fdps_render_view_frame) shows it runs one visible animation step. Callers are three unnamed map routines plus fdps_title_demo, consistent with the same actor stepping code driving the attract-mode demo.
open_question: Whether this map is the battle grid or a town/overworld map is not fully settled; "Chess.wav" and the terrain-damage tiles argue for battle, but the mode 5 event-slot machinery (&DAT_000640d8 flags, the 3-byte table at DAT_0006013c+0x53) could equally be scripted map events. The meaning of the second argument, and of the globals DAT_00063f78 / DAT_00063f88 / DAT_00063f8c compared against 6, were not determined.

name: fdps_move_path_trace
role: Walks the battle movement cost map held at DAT_00060144, either tracing a downhill step-by-step direction path between two tiles (mode 0 and 1) or reporting the unit of the requested side that sits on the lowest-cost reachable tile (mode 2).
plate_comment:
Traces the battle movement cost map and returns either a direction path or the nearest reachable unit.

Algorithm:
The global at DAT_00060144 points to a movement map header: word width, word height, then width*height cells of 2 bytes each. Byte 1 of a cell holds the flood-filled step cost, 0xff meaning unreachable. Cell stride is 2 and row stride is width*2; both are computed into locals up front.

mode == 2: scans the unit table (count in DAT_00060150, records fetched by index through FUN_0002d210). Units are filtered by side: when arg4 is zero only units with record byte 6 == 0 are considered, otherwise only units with byte 6 != 0. Units with bit 0 of record byte 5 set are skipped. For each surviving unit the cost cell at (unit.x, unit.y) is read and the minimum is tracked. If no unit was found the function returns -1, otherwise it stores the winning unit's x and y into out_path[0] and out_path[1] and returns the minimum cost.

mode == 0 or 1: starts at (arg4, arg5) and repeatedly steps to the neighbouring cell with the lowest cost, recording one direction code per step into a local buffer: 0 = y-1, 1 = x+1, 2 = y+1, 3 = x-1, 4 = no move. Edge neighbours are skipped at the map borders. If the starting cell is already 0xff the function returns -1 immediately. Mode 0 takes a neighbour only on a strictly lower cost, which makes runs of identical cost keep the current heading. Mode 1 also accepts an equal cost, but only when the previously recorded step used a different direction code, which makes ties alternate direction instead of running straight. The walk stops once the current tile equals (arg1, arg2). The recorded direction codes are then copied into out_path in reverse order and the step count is returned.

Parameters:
arg1 goal_x   - x of the tile at which the walk terminates (unused in mode 2)
arg2 goal_y   - y of the tile at which the walk terminates (unused in mode 2)
arg3 out_path - byte buffer receiving the reversed direction codes, or the found unit's x,y in mode 2
arg4 start_x  - x of the tile the walk starts from; in mode 2 this is the side filter instead
arg5 start_y  - y of the tile the walk starts from (unused in mode 2)
arg6 mode     - 0 straight-preferring trace, 1 turn-preferring trace, 2 nearest-unit query

Returns:
Number of direction codes written in modes 0 and 1, the minimum cost found in mode 2, or -1 when the start tile is unreachable or no unit matched.
prototype: int fdps_move_path_trace(int goal_x, int goal_y, unsigned char *out_path, int start_x, int start_y, int mode)
evidence: All six arguments are read from stack slots EBP+0x14 through EBP+0x28 after the PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP prologue, no argument register (EAX/EDX/EBX/ECX) is read on entry, and the function ends in a bare RET with no stack adjustment, so the caller cleans the arguments: this is the stack-based convention, not the Watcom register default. The body indexes a 2-byte-per-cell grid whose width and height come from the two words at the head of DAT_00060144, uses byte 1 of each cell as a cost with 0xff as the unreachable sentinel, and emits the four direction codes 0/1/2/3 for y-1/x+1/y+1/x-1 into a local buffer that is copied out reversed. Mode 2 walks the unit table (count DAT_00060150, records via FUN_0002d210, x at byte 0, y at byte 1, skip flag bit 0 of byte 5, side at byte 6). One of the three callers is already identified as fdps_battle_unit_turn, which places the function in the battle movement subsystem. No strings are referenced.
open_question: Which end of the trace is the unit and which is the chosen destination is not settled: the direction codes are recorded while walking downhill from (start_x, start_y) to (goal_x, goal_y) and are then reversed, but whether the callers flood the cost map from the unit tile or from the target tile was not checked, and the codes themselves are not inverted during the reversal. Also unconfirmed is why mode 1 prefers turning on ties, likely a cosmetic walk-animation variant.

name: fdps_battle_move_unit_toward
role: Moves one battle unit as close as its movement range allows to a requested destination tile, adjusting the destination when it is unreachable or occupied, and executes the resulting walk.
plate_comment:
Battle movement: walk a unit toward a requested destination tile.

Algorithm:
1. Resolve the unit record for unit_index via FUN_0002d210, and cache from it: field 0x00 = tile x, field 0x01 = tile y, field 0x20 = movement points, field 0x3b = a movement/terrain cost selector.
2. FUN_00018b70(move_points + 1) yields a per-unit movement context; malloc(100) is the step buffer (one direction code per step) and malloc(0x800) is the reachable-tile list (x,y byte pairs).
3. Build the movement/cost map (FUN_00010b90(map_mode) then FUN_00010de0(ctx, x, y, cost_selector)) and try to path from the unit to (dest_x, dest_y) with FUN_00011460(x, y, step_buf, dest_x, dest_y, 0). It returns the step count, or -1 when no path exists.
4. If that fails, retry the path with the relaxed flag 1. If the relaxed path exists, replay it step by step (direction code 0 = y+1, 1 = x-1, 2 = y-1, else x+1), probing each tile with FUN_0002ba00(x, y) and reading the occupancy result at 0x00069d0c. The last tile whose probe is not 0xff becomes the new destination, i.e. the request is retargeted to the furthest usable tile along the blocked route.
5. Rebuild the movement map, call FUN_000118f0(unit_index, map_mode) to flood the unit's reach, and FUN_00011da0(tile_buf) to collect the reachable tiles and their count.
6. Scan the reachable tiles and keep the one minimising Manhattan distance |tx - dest_x| + |ty - dest_y| to the destination, breaking ties on the smaller ||dx| - |dy|| (the more diagonal-balanced tile).
7. Path to that chosen tile with FUN_00011460(..., 0). If the step count is non-zero, FUN_0002d2d0(unit_index, step_buf, step_count) performs the actual move and the result is 1; otherwise 0.
8. Free both buffers and return.

Parameters:
  dest_x     [ebp+0x14] requested destination tile x; reassigned internally when the route is retargeted
  dest_y     [ebp+0x18] requested destination tile y; likewise reassigned
  unit_index [ebp+0x1c] index of the acting unit, resolved to its record by FUN_0002d210
  map_mode   [ebp+0x20] selector handed to the movement-map builder FUN_00010b90 and to FUN_000118f0

Returns:
  1 if a move of at least one step was executed, 0 if the unit stays where it is.
prototype: int fdps_battle_move_unit_toward(int dest_x, int dest_y, int unit_index, int map_mode)
evidence: All four arguments arrive on the stack at [EBP+0x14..0x20] after the PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP + MOV EBP,ESP prologue, and every call site inside cleans its own arguments with ADD ESP,n, so the function is stack-argument __cdecl rather than the project default __watcall. FUN_0003d375 / FUN_0003d478 / FUN_0003d364 are malloc / free / abs (sizes 100 and 0x800, and abs used to form |dx|+|dy|), placing them in the crt pool, while the function itself is game logic. The purpose is pinned by the step-buffer replay loop at 0x11b51: a byte per step decoded into the four cardinal directions y+1/x-1/y-1/x+1 is a movement path, and FUN_00011460 returning -1 for one flag value and succeeding for another is a pathfinder with a fallback mode. The tile-selection loop at 0x11c44 walks x,y byte pairs and minimises Manhattan distance to the destination with a diagonal-balance tie-break, which is the classic tactical-RPG 'get as close as you can' rule. The unit record fields (0x00 x, 0x01 y, 0x20 movement points, 0x3b cost selector) are consistent with the buffer sized move_points+1. Callers are battle-side: fdps_battle_system_menu at 00014ab0 plus four AI/command sites, five in total, so this is a per-action helper and not a startup routine.
open_question: The fourth argument (map_mode, [ebp+0x20]) is only forwarded to FUN_00010b90 and FUN_000118f0, so its meaning (team filter, terrain ruleset, or zone-of-control switch) is unresolved. Field 0x3b of the unit record is likewise only a pass-through to FUN_00010de0. The global byte at 0x00069d0c written by FUN_0002ba00 is read as an occupancy result where 0xff means empty, but that reading is inferred from usage, not from the producer.

name: fdps_draw_tilemap_layer
role: Draws one SAF tilemap (one animation layer) by walking its columns x rows grid and handing each cell's tile index to the per-cell tile drawer.
plate_comment:
Draws one SAF tilemap layer.

Algorithm:
Takes a 0x24-byte draw context whose field 0x14 holds the base address of a loaded SAF file and whose field 0x18 holds the tilemap index. Reads the section 1 (tilemap) descriptor from the SAF header: item count at 0x16, offset-table start at 0x18. Returns immediately if the index is negative or not less than the item count. Otherwise resolves the tilemap record via saf + *(u32 *)(saf + saf[0x18] + index * 4) and reads its i16 column count and i16 row count, then advances past the 4-byte tilemap header to the cell array. Copies the whole 0x24-byte context onto the stack as a working copy (memcpy at 0x3d514) and iterates rows outer, columns inner. At the start of each row the working copy's x (offset 0x0c) is reset from the caller's x; for each cell the signed i16 tile index is stored into the working copy's index field (offset 0x18), the per-cell tile drawer at 0x13ed0 is called with the working copy, x is advanced by the SAF cell width (header 0x07) and after the row y (offset 0x10) is advanced by the SAF cell height (header 0x09). Cell indices are read signed while the caller's tilemap index is unsigned; the per-cell drawer performs its own range check.

Parameters:
  ctx - pointer to the 0x24-byte SAF draw context: 0x0c = x, 0x10 = y, 0x14 = SAF base pointer, 0x18 = tilemap index on entry (reused as tile index for each cell).

Returns:
  Nothing. Draws nothing when the tilemap index is out of range.
evidence: Disassembly reads its single stack argument at [EBP+0x14] after PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP, and both calls (0x3d514 with three pushes, 0x13ed0 with one) are followed by ADD ESP, so the whole cluster is stack-based cdecl; Ghidra's __watcall and the unaff_EBX parameter in the decompilation are wrong. The header offsets it touches (0x07 cell width, 0x09 cell height, 0x16 section 1 item count, 0x18 section 1 offset table) match resource_info/saf.md exactly, where 0x13fd0 is already identified as the per-layer tilemap walker; the nested loop bounds come from the tilemap record's i16 columns/rows and the loop body advances x by cell width and y by cell height, which is that document's stated cell traversal. Its only caller is fdps_draw_composite_sprite (0x14140, the per-frame layer walker) and its only non-CRT callee is the per-cell drawer 0x13ed0, so it is game logic in the graphics/animation path, hence the fdps_ prefix.
open_question: The 0x24-byte draw context is used as an opaque struct here; only fields 0x0c, 0x10, 0x14 and 0x18 are touched, so the meaning of its remaining fields (blend mode, blend level, clip target) has to come from 0x13ed0 rather than from this function.

name: fdps_draw_composite_sprite
role: Looks up one entry by index in a sprite bank held in the draw request, then draws every 13-byte part record of that entry through the per-part blitter, offsetting each part from the request's base X/Y.
plate_comment:
Draws one composite sprite entry: a bank-indexed group of part records blitted at offsets from a common origin.

Algorithm:
1. Read the bank pointer from req+0x14 and the entry index from req+0x18. The bank header holds an unsigned 16-bit entry count at bank+0x0C and an (unaligned) 32-bit offset-table displacement at bank+0x0E. If the index is negative or >= the count, the lookup yields NULL and the function returns without drawing.
2. Otherwise entry = bank + *(int32 *)(bank + *(int32 *)(bank+0x0E) + index*4), i.e. table entries are bank-relative offsets.
3. Copy the caller's 0x24-byte draw request onto the stack as a scratch request, so per-part edits never touch the caller's copy.
4. Walk the part records, which start at entry+0x0A and are 13 bytes each; the signed 16-bit count is at entry+0x08. Each record holds: u16 sub-sprite id at +0, s16 dx at +2, s16 dy at +4, u8 mode at +6, s16 level at +7 (unaligned).
5. For each part, when req+0x20 in the caller's request is zero the record's mode byte selects the blend setup: mode 0 clears the scratch request's mode field to 0; mode 1 stores 0x10 - level into a small parameter block built from the two runtime tables at 0x000653F0 and 0x000643F0, sets the scratch mode field to 9, and points the scratch request at that block. Any other mode leaves the previous setup in place.
6. Set the scratch request's X to req+0x0C + dx, its Y to req+0x10 + dy, its sprite id to the record's u16, and call the per-part blitter at 0x00013FD0 with the scratch request.
7. After the loop, if the flag argument is non-zero, call 0x000142D0 with the bank pointer and the entry's leading u16.

Parameters:
  req  - pointer to a 0x24-byte draw request: X at +0x0C, Y at +0x10, sprite bank pointer at +0x14, entry index at +0x18, blend parameter block pointer at +0x1C, blend mode at +0x20.
  flag - when non-zero, run the post-draw call at 0x000142D0 for this entry.

Returns:
  Nothing. Silently does nothing when the entry index is out of range.
evidence: Arguments are read from [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18] after the PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP prologue, no registers carry inputs, and RET takes no immediate, so the caller cleans the stack: __cdecl. The unaff_EBX in the decompilation is a Ghidra guess; EBX is only saved and restored, never read. The body is pure game logic over a bank/entry/part-record layout with no CRT or Miles idiom, so pool fdps: bank+0x0C count, bank+0x0E offset-table displacement, bank-relative entry offsets, entry+0x08 part count, 13-byte part records of (id, dx, dy, mode, level). Graphics is settled by the X/Y accumulation from req+0x0C/+0x10, the per-part sprite id, and the mode-1 branch that builds 0x10 - level over the two runtime tables at 0x000653F0/0x000643F0, which reads as a translucency/blend level. The 0x24-byte copy through 0x0003D514 with PUSH len, PUSH src, PUSH dst, ADD ESP,0x0C is a plain memcpy of the request. 18 callers spread across UI, battle and screen code, including fdps_title_screen and fdps_show_game_over, mark it a shared drawing primitive rather than a startup one-shot; 0x00013FD0 is called from nowhere else and is this function's private per-part worker.
open_question: The per-part worker at 0x00013FD0 has not been read, so "draw/blit" is inferred from the request layout and call sites rather than proven; the exact meaning of the blend mode value 9 and of the two zero-filled tables at 0x000653F0/0x000643F0 (populated at runtime) is unsettled, as is what 0x000142D0 does with (bank, entry->id) when the flag is set.

name: fdps_sfx_play
role: Plays one indexed WAV entry of a loaded sound bank on the first idle Miles digital sample handle, configuring format, rate, length, volume and loop count before starting it.
plate_comment:
Algorithm: Returns immediately unless both sound-enable flags (DAT_00069d71, DAT_00069d70) are set and the entry index is within [0, bank->entry_count) where entry_count is the u16 at bank+0x2a. Locates the entry through the dword offset table at bank+0x2c: entry = bank + *(int*)(bank + *(int*)(bank+0x2c) + index*4), which points at an 8-byte header followed by raw PCM data. Scans the 8-slot sample-handle array at 0x00069d30 for the first handle whose AIL sample status is not 4 (playing); if all eight are busy the request is dropped silently. On the chosen handle it calls the Miles sequence init sample, set sample address (entry+8, length = *(int*)(entry+4)), set sample type (format code, flags 2), set loop count 1, set volume 0x28, set playback rate (u16 at entry+2), start sample. The format code is derived from the first two header bytes, channels at +0 and bits at +1: (1,8)->0, (1,16)->1, (2,8)->2, anything else->3, matching the Miles DIG_F_MONO_8 / MONO_16 / STEREO_8 / STEREO_16 enumeration.
Parameters: bank - base pointer of a loaded sound bank whose header holds the entry count at +0x2a and the entry offset table pointer at +0x2c; index - zero-based entry index within that bank.
Returns: nothing; failure to validate, disabled sound, or no free sample handle all return silently.
evidence: Both parameters arrive on the stack at [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18] after the PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP prologue, and every call site in the body pushes arguments and cleans up with ADD ESP, so the module is compiled with stack-based calling here; hence __cdecl. All seven configuration callees plus the status query live in the 0x3exxx-0x3fxxx Miles AIL block and are invoked in the canonical MSS order AIL_init_sample, AIL_set_sample_address, AIL_set_sample_type, AIL_set_sample_loop_count, AIL_set_sample_volume, AIL_set_sample_playback_rate, AIL_start_sample. The status constant 4 is SMP_PLAYING, so the loop picks the first non-playing handle in the eight-entry handle array at 0x00069d30. The channels/bits to format-code mapping reproduces the DIG_F_* enumeration exactly, which confirms the 8-byte per-entry header layout: channels u8, bits u8, rate u16, length u32, PCM data. The function itself is game code that drives the vendor library, so pool fdps rather than ail.
open_question: The single recorded caller is the function at 00014140 currently named fdps_draw_composite_sprite, which does not obviously belong with sound playback; either that neighbour's name is wrong or it is a combined effect trigger. Not investigated, since it is outside this ticket.

name: fdps_saf_advance_tick
role: Advances a SAF animation cursor by one tick, moving to the next frame when the current frame's hold time expires and reporting when the animation has run past its last frame.
plate_comment:
Advance a SAF animation playback cursor by one tick.

Algorithm:
The cursor is a 3-dword state block: [0] current frame index, [1] tick counter inside the current frame, [2] pointer to the loaded SAF image. When mode == 1 the call is a reset: both counters are zeroed and 0 is returned without touching the SAF. Otherwise the SAF header is sanity-checked by comparing the magic bytes 'S', 'A' and 'F' at offsets 0, 1 and 2 (note the original code accepts the file if ANY one of the three matches, not all three), and the frame count is taken from the u16 at header offset 0x0C; a zero frame count makes the function return -1. The tick counter is then incremented and the current frame record is located as saf + *(i32 *)(saf + *(i32 *)(saf + 0x0E) + index * 4), with the index bounds-checked against the frame count (an out-of-range index yields a null frame pointer). The frame's hold time is the i16 at frame offset 0x02; while the tick counter stays below it the frame is held. Once the counter reaches the hold time it is cleared and the frame index is incremented. If the index then reaches the frame count the animation has completed one pass: the tick counter is cleared and, when mode == 0, the index wraps to 0 to loop, otherwise it is clamped to the last frame so playback stops on the final frame; the function returns 1 in that case.

Parameters:
cursor - pointer to the 3-dword playback state block described above.
mode - 1 resets the cursor, 0 loops back to the first frame at the end, any other value holds on the last frame.

Returns:
1 when the animation just passed its last frame, 0 while it is still playing or after a reset, -1 when the SAF data is unusable (bad magic or zero frame count).
evidence: The function reads only the SAF header fields already documented in resource_info/saf.md: the 'S'/'A'/'F' magic at 0x00-0x02, the u16 frame count of section 0 at 0x0C, and the i32 section-0 start at 0x0E, then indexes the section's u32 offset table (saf + *(i32 *)(saf + tableOff + i * 4)) and reads the i16 hold time at frame offset 0x02 - exactly the 'advance one tick by hold time' entry the format document already attributes to 0x14550. It is a leaf (no callees) called from 12 places including fdps_title_screen and fdps_show_game_over, i.e. every site that plays an animation, which fits a per-tick cursor update rather than anything subsystem-specific. Pool is fdps: it decodes a game-specific container, references no CRT or AIL code, and lives in the game text range. Convention is the binary-wide -4s stack convention documented in rebuild_info/build_flags.md - the prologue is the exact 53 56 57 55 89 e5 signature, both arguments are read from [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18], the epilogue is mov esp,ebp / pop ebp, and RET carries no immediate so the caller cleans the stack.
open_question: The magic check is an OR of the three bytes rather than an AND, so a file matching only one byte passes; this looks like an original-source bug and must be reproduced verbatim rather than corrected. Also, mode values other than 0 and 1 are only distinguishable at the wrap point (hold on last frame) - it was not established from this function alone whether callers actually pass anything other than 0 and 1.

name: fdps_battle_system_menu
role: Modal system menu opened from the battle player phase: draws a four-entry menu, waits for a selection, and dispatches to the submenu, the two confirm-then-act file/state entries and the settings screen until the player leaves the menu.
plate_comment:
Battle system menu (modal loop).

Algorithm:
Copies two 16-byte tables out of the read-only island at 0x146e0 and 0x146f0 into locals: four menu entry codes {0x16, 0x0b, 0x0c, 0x13} and a matching four-entry state array cleared to zero. Clears the two menu-active globals DAT_00069cd0 and DAT_00060159 and enters the loop.

Each iteration draws the menu (FUN_00016130), reads a selection (FUN_00016200, which updates the selection index and returns -1 when the player backs out), then runs the close animation as a countdown 0x17, 0x13, 0x0f, 0x0b, 0x07, 0x03 through FUN_00015860 and calls FUN_0002beb0.

A -1 result sets both menu-active globals to 1 and returns 0. Otherwise the selection index picks a branch:
  index 0: calls FUN_00014ea0; any result other than -1 sets both globals to 1 and is returned to the caller as the menu result, otherwise the loop continues.
  index 1: darkens/prepares via FUN_000205b0(0), shows panel 0xaa44a with code 0x1ea, then calls FUN_00017990. On a zero result it shows panel 0xabc0a code 0x1eb, waits 300 ticks, dismisses (FUN_00020820), recomputes the cursor tile from DAT_00069cd4/24 and DAT_00069ccc/24, clears both menu-active globals, and walks every unit 0..DAT_00060150-1 (FUN_0002d210): for a unit whose byte 5 has none of mask 0x85 set, whose byte 6 equals 2 and whose byte 0x26 is zero, it centres on the unit tile (FUN_0002d7c0), sets DAT_00069d90 to 0xff, calls FUN_000119e0, dispatches through the handler table at 0x000601c4 when DAT_00069d90 changed, and finishes the unit with FUN_000119b0. It then redraws (FUN_0001e3f0), sets both globals to 1, calls FUN_0002db50 and returns 0. A non-zero result shows panel 0xabc0a code 0x1ec, waits and returns to the loop.
  index 2: calls FUN_000183d0 and stays in the loop.
  index 3: same shape as index 1 with codes 0x1ed / 0x1ee / 0x1ef and panel 0xad3ca; on success it clears DAT_00060159, redraws with FUN_0001e3f0, restores the flag and returns 0.

Parameters:
None. The prologue pushes EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP and builds a 0x48-byte frame but never reads [EBP+0x14] or beyond, so the function takes no arguments; the parameters shown by the decompiler are invented.

Returns:
int. 0 when the menu is dismissed or when an entry completed its action and the battle screen was restored; otherwise the non-negative command code produced by FUN_00014ea0.
evidence: Sole caller is fdps_battle_player_phase_loop @ 0002bae0, so this runs inside battle, not at startup. The body is a textbook modal menu: a fixed four-element entry table and a parallel four-element state array copied from read-only data at 0x146e0/0x146f0, a draw call, an input call that returns -1 on cancel and writes a selection index, a fixed close animation, and a four-way dispatch on the index that loops for non-terminal entries and returns for terminal ones. Two of the four entries share the pattern 'show panel, call FUN_00017990, branch on zero, show success or failure panel, wait 300 ticks, dismiss', with consecutive message codes 0x1ea-0x1ef, which is a confirm-or-file-operation entry pair. Pool is fdps: it touches battle globals (unit count DAT_00060150, unit accessor FUN_0002d210, cursor tile globals DAT_00069cd4/DAT_00069ccc scaled by the 24-pixel tile size) and a game handler table at 0x000601c4; nothing here is CRT or Miles. Convention is __cdecl because the binary default is the -4s stack convention (rebuild_info/build_flags.md) and every call site here pushes arguments and cleans them with ADD ESP,n while this function ends in a bare RET.
open_question: Which concrete commands the four entry codes 0x16/0x0b/0x0c/0x13 name is not settled. In particular it is unresolved whether FUN_00017990 is a yes/no confirmation shared by entries 1 and 3 or a save/load slot operation returning 0 on success, and therefore whether the unit sweep after entry 1 is 'reinstantiate every unit after restoring a save' or 'let each not-yet-acted unit of team 2 finish the turn'. Settling it needs FUN_00017990 and the message/panel resource at 0xaa44a/0xabc0a/0xad3ca.

name: fdps_battle_system_submenu
role: Runs the in-battle system submenu (four entries: item 0x17, save, load, quit) and performs the chosen action, including writing and reloading the FDE.SAV save file.
plate_comment:
In-battle system submenu: entry action, save, load, quit.

Algorithm:
Builds two parallel 4-entry stack arrays. The id array is copied from the
constant table at 0x00014700 and holds {0x17, 9, 10, 8}; the state array is
copied from the zero table at 0x00014710 and is then patched:
  - state[2] (load) is set to 1 when the CRT file-existence check at 0x00042438
    reports that "FDE.SAV" (0x00060118) is present.
  - state[1] (save) is set to 1 when any of the DAT_00060150 unit records
    obtained through FUN_0002d210(index) has flags byte +0x05 with bit 0 clear
    and bit 7 set.
Then loops: FUN_00016130 draws the menu, FUN_00016200 runs the selection and
returns the chosen index through an out parameter, FUN_000161b0 tears the menu
down, and fdps_render_view_frame repaints the battlefield. A return of -1 from
FUN_00016200 aborts the whole submenu with -1.
Selection handling:
  0 - calls FUN_00017ca0 and returns 0.
  1 - save. Shows message 0x1F3, asks for confirmation via FUN_00017990. On
      confirmation allocates a 0x59CB byte image, seeds it from the existing
      "FDE.SAV" opened "rb" (or, when no file exists, writes 0xFF slot markers
      at +0x3B2B, +0x4553, +0x4F7B, +0x59A3), copies 0x8A3 bytes from
      DAT_0006013C, 0xA00 bytes from DAT_00064108 at +0x8A3, DAT_00060150*0x50
      bytes from DAT_00069CD8 at +0x12A3 and 0x20 bytes from 0x000640D8 at
      +0x30A3, fills the descriptor at +0x30C3 (unit count, three coordinate
      globals divided by 0x18, chapter/flag globals), stores the FUN_00056898
      checksum at +0x59C7, scrambles with FUN_000568B7, writes the image back
      through "wb", frees it, reports 0x203, and returns 0.
  2 - load. Shows message 0x205, asks for confirmation, and on confirmation
      reports 0x206 and calls fdps_load_savegame; returns 0.
  3 - quit. Shows message 0x1F0, asks for confirmation, and on confirmation
      reports 0x1F1, sets the quit flag DAT_000643EB to 1 and returns 1.
A declined confirmation falls through to the top of the loop and redisplays the
menu.

Parameters:
None.

Returns:
-1 when the menu was aborted, 1 when the player confirmed quit (DAT_000643EB
has been set), 0 after any other selection completed.
evidence: The only caller is fdps_battle_system_menu @ 00014ab0, so this is a battle-side menu, not a title-screen one. Save/load identity is nailed by data: 0x00060118 holds the literal "FDE.SAV", 0x0006157C holds "rb" and 0x00061580 holds "wb", passed to the fopen-shaped FUN_0004265E, with fread-shaped FUN_0004270D on the read path and fwrite-shaped FUN_00042A41 on the write path over the same 0x59CB byte buffer allocated by FUN_0003D375 and released by FUN_0003D478. The load branch calls the already-named fdps_load_savegame @ 00023E20, and each loop iteration ends in the already-named fdps_render_view_frame @ 0002BEB0, confirming this runs over the live battle view. The quit branch sets a single global byte DAT_000643EB and returns 1, the classic exit-request flag. The 4-entry id table at 0x00014700 ({0x17,9,10,8}) and the parallel zeroed state table at 0x00014710, both handed to the same three FUN_00016130 / FUN_00016200 / FUN_000161B0 calls, are the menu widget's item-id and item-state vectors; state[2] is enabled exactly when the save file exists, which is what a greyed-out Load entry needs. Every call site pushes arguments and the caller executes ADD ESP,n afterwards, and the function itself reads no [EBP+8] parameter and ends in a bare RET, so the convention is stack-based __cdecl with no arguments.
open_question: Menu entry 0 (id 0x17, handler FUN_00017CA0) is unidentified, so the submenu's exact title cannot be fixed; the name assumes it is the battle system menu rather than a narrower save/load menu. The condition that enables entry 1 (save) -- some unit record having flags +0x05 bit 0 clear and bit 7 set -- is not understood, and the polarity of the state array (1 = selectable versus 1 = greyed) is inferred only from the load entry.

name: fdps_battle_unit_turn
role: Runs the complete interactive turn for one player-controlled battle unit: movement-range display, destination selection with undo, move execution, the four-entry command menu, and dispatch of the chosen action.
plate_comment:
Interactive turn of a single player-controlled battle unit.

Algorithm:
Loads the unit record for unit_index (helper at 0002d210; records are 0x50 bytes in the array based at 00069cd8). Field 0x3b selects a graphics resource that is acquired once up front (0003d375) and released once at the end (0003d478); field 0x20 is the movement allowance; field 0x08 is the class code; fields 0x00/0x01 are the tile X/Y. Two 16-byte command-menu templates are copied from rodata into locals: the command id list {3,2,1,0} and a per-entry state array {0,0,0,0}. Sets the global at 0006015c to 0x14 and then loops until the turn is finished.

Each pass: refreshes the map, resets the pending-action selector at 00069d90 to 0xff, computes the reachable set for (movement allowance + 1) via 00018b70, converts the current cursor pixel position (00069cd4 / 00069ccc) to tile coordinates by dividing by the 24-pixel tile size, paints the movement range (00010de0) and waits for a map selection (0002b4f0). A -1 selection restores the cursor to the origin tile and ends the turn. Otherwise the destination picker at 00011460 runs; its result -1 restarts the loop (move cancelled), 0 means the unit stays put, any other value is a path to walk. For a real move the class code is checked (values 7 and 3 leave menu entry 1 disabled, all others enable it), the walk is played back by 0002d2d0 and the command menu at 00015d00 is opened with the moved flag set; for a stationary unit the same menu is opened with the flag clear. A -1 from the menu is a cancel: when the global at 00060004 is zero the unit is written back to its origin tile and the loop repeats, otherwise the turn is committed. Any other menu result commits the turn.

On exit sets 00069cd0, releases the graphics resource, and if 00069d90 is no longer 0xff calls the handler at index 00069d90 of the function-pointer table at 000601c4 with unit_index, then calls the handler at index 00069cf4 of the table at 0006028c.

Parameters:
  unit_index - index of the acting unit within the battle unit array.

Returns:
  Nothing. The chosen action is carried out through the dispatch tables at 000601c4 and 0006028c.
evidence: Called from exactly one place, fdps_battle_player_phase_loop at 0002bae0, which fixes the subsystem as the battle player phase and the granularity as one unit. The single stack argument at [EBP+0x14] is used both as an index into the 0x50-byte unit array (DAT_00069cd8 + index*0x50, whose bytes 0 and 1 are written back with the tile X/Y computed here) and as the argument passed to the command menu, the move playback and the dispatch handler, so it is a unit index. Tile arithmetic is unmistakable: two globals holding cursor pixel positions are divided by 0x18 to get tile coordinates and multiplied back by 0x18 when the cursor is restored. The undo path is explicit - on a -1 from the menu at 00015d00 the original tile coordinates saved before the move are written back into the unit record and the loop repeats. The two 16-byte tables copied in from 00014720 and 00014730 are a command id list {3,2,1,0} and a parallel per-entry state array, one slot of which is toggled by the unit's class byte. All arguments are pushed on the stack and every call site is followed by ADD ESP,n, and this function itself returns with a bare RET leaving its own argument for the caller, hence __cdecl. Nothing here touches CRT or Miles AIL surface, so the pool is fdps.
open_question: The exact meaning of the four command ids {3,2,1,0} and of the global at 00060004 that decides whether a menu cancel undoes the move or commits the turn are not settled from this function alone; they need 00015d00 and the phase loop.

name: fdps_battle_action_menu
role: Runs the in-battle action command menu for one unit: computes which of the four commands are unavailable, draws and drives the menu, and dispatches to the chosen command (attack, and the three other command handlers), looping until a command completes or the menu is cancelled.
plate_comment:
Battle action command menu for a single unit.

Algorithm:
Outer do/while loop, re-entered whenever the chosen command aborts back to the menu.
Each pass:
  1. Clears cmd_disabled[0] and the global at 0x00069cec, then probes availability:
     - FUN_00025140(unit, 0) == -1  -> cmd_disabled[0] = 1 (command 0 unusable);
       otherwise FUN_00025200/FUN_00018b40 fetch a descriptor whose bytes +0x0b and
       +0x0c are range values fed, together with the cursor tile derived from the
       globals 0x00069cd4 and 0x00069ccc divided by the 24-pixel tile size, into
       FUN_00011e50; a zero result also sets cmd_disabled[0] = 1. FUN_00010b20
       releases whatever FUN_00011e50 built.
     - FUN_00025240(unit) == 0 -> cmd_disabled[2] = 1.
     - FUN_00027840(unit, 0) == 0, or byte +0x27 of the record from FUN_0002d210(unit)
       is non-zero -> cmd_disabled[1] = 1.
  2. Scans cmd_disabled[0..3] for the first zero entry and uses it as the initial
     highlighted index (-1 when every command is disabled).
  3. FUN_00016130 draws the menu, FUN_00016200 runs the selection loop and writes the
     chosen index back through a pointer, FUN_000161b0 erases it, then
     fdps_render_view_frame repaints. A selection result of -1 means cancel: the
     function returns the pending result value (-1, or 1 when command 2 previously
     reported code 2).
  4. Dispatch on the chosen index:
     index 0: saves the cursor position, allocates a 100-byte work block
       (FUN_0003d375), rebuilds the reachable/target set via FUN_00011e50, sets the
       global 0x00069cd0 to 1 and runs target selection FUN_0002b4f0, then frees the
       block. On cancel the cursor is restored with fdps_map_cursor_move_to and the
       menu is shown again. On success it resolves the action:
       fdps_battle_find_unit_at_cursor, FUN_0001c2e0, FUN_00018d60, FUN_00026180,
       FUN_0001d6c0, scales the 0x00069cec accumulator by 15/10, then FUN_0001dd30 and
       FUN_0001d990 apply the result and FUN_000119b0 finishes the turn; returns 1.
     index 1: FUN_00027c20(unit); on success FUN_000119b0 ends the turn, the byte flag
       at 0x00060159 is set to 1 and 1 is returned, otherwise the menu is shown again.
     index 2: FUN_000252b0(unit); result 2 latches the pending return value to 1 and
       re-shows the menu, any other non-(-1) result clears 0x00069cec and returns 1.
     any other index: when flag == 0 calls FUN_000120d0(unit) first, then FUN_000184f0
       and FUN_000119b0, and returns 1.

Parameters:
  unit         - pointer to the acting unit record; passed to every availability probe
                 and command handler.
  menu_ctx     - context value handed to the menu draw, select and erase helpers.
  cmd_disabled - caller-supplied int[4] scratch array; this function fills it with the
                 per-command disabled flags (0 = selectable, 1 = greyed out).
  flag         - when zero, the fall-through command runs the extra FUN_000120d0 step.

Returns:
  1 when a command was carried out and the unit's action is complete.
  -1 when the menu was cancelled with nothing done (caller returns to unit selection);
  1 is returned instead if command 2 had earlier reported result code 2.
prototype: int fdps_battle_action_menu(void *unit, int menu_ctx, int *cmd_disabled, int flag)
evidence: Sole caller is fdps_battle_unit_turn @ 00015470, so this is the per-unit action step of the battle turn. The body is a textbook command menu: it fills a four-entry int array with disabled flags, picks the first enabled entry as the initial highlight, calls a draw/select/erase trio (00016130 / 00016200 / 000161b0) that shares the same argument shape, then switches on the returned index 0/1/2/default with a separate handler per branch and re-enters the loop when a branch cancels. Branch 0 is unmistakably the attack path: it snapshots the cursor, allocates a 100-byte work block, rebuilds a range set from the descriptor bytes +0x0b/+0x0c and the cursor tile (globals 0x00069cd4 / 0x00069ccc divided by the 24-pixel tile pitch), runs target picking via FUN_0002b4f0, then resolves against fdps_battle_find_unit_at_cursor and restores the cursor with fdps_map_cursor_move_to on cancel. Pool is fdps: no CRT or AIL signature, and the only library-shaped callees are the allocator pair FUN_0003d375 / FUN_0003d478. Convention is __cdecl: four arguments are read from [EBP+0x14] through [EBP+0x20] after the four saved registers and the return address, all calls are followed by an explicit ADD ESP, and the function ends in a bare RET.
open_question: The identities of commands 1, 2 and the fall-through branch are not settled - they are almost certainly magic/item/wait or a permutation, but nothing in this function names them. The meaning of the global accumulator at 0x00069cec (scaled by 15/10 on the attack path, cleared on entry and on the command-2 success path) and of the byte flag at 0x00060159 set by command 1 are also unresolved.

name: fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop
role: Modal keyboard loop that moves a four-way menu cursor while redrawing each iteration, returning 1 when the player confirms and -1 when the player cancels.
plate_comment:
Modal four-way menu cursor input loop.

Algorithm:
Loops until a terminating key arrives. Each iteration reads one scan code
(masked to a byte) from the low-level keyboard reader at 0x000567be and
dispatches on it:
  0x01 (Esc) or 0x53      -> result = -1 (cancel), loop ends
  0x1c (Enter) or 0x39 (Space) -> result = 1 (confirm), loop ends
  0x48 (Up)    -> if dir_blocked[0] == 0 then *cursor_dir = 0
  0x4b (Left)  -> if dir_blocked[1] == 0 then *cursor_dir = 1
  0x4d (Right) -> if dir_blocked[2] == 0 then *cursor_dir = 2
  0x50 (Down)  -> if dir_blocked[3] == 0 then *cursor_dir = 3
A non-zero entry in dir_blocked suppresses movement in that direction, so the
cursor keeps its previous value. Any other scan code falls through unhandled.
After dispatch every iteration unconditionally calls 0x0002eab0 and 0x00015be0
(frame pacing / presentation), then calls 0x00015860(ctx, dir_blocked, 0x18,
*cursor_dir) to repaint the cursor, then repeats.

Parameters:
  ctx          - opaque context/handle forwarded unchanged as the first
                 argument of the redraw call at 0x00015860.
  dir_blocked  - pointer to four ints indexed by direction (0 up, 1 left,
                 2 right, 3 down); zero means that direction is selectable.
                 Also forwarded to the redraw call.
  cursor_dir   - in/out pointer to the currently selected direction index;
                 updated in place on an accepted arrow key.

Returns:
  1  on confirm (Enter or Space)
  -1 on cancel (Esc or scan code 0x53)
The function never returns while the loop result is still 0.
evidence: Scan-code constants are decisive and need no strings: 0x48/0x50/0x4b/0x4d are the IBM PC arrow-key make codes, 0x1c Enter, 0x39 Space, 0x01 Esc, and the handler writes the canonical direction indices 0/3/1/2 for up/down/left/right into *cursor_dir. The key source 0x000567be returns a value masked with 0xff, i.e. a raw scan code. The frame ends with a standard Watcom four-push prologue (PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP then MOV EBP,ESP), so the return address sits at EBP+0x10 and the three referenced slots EBP+0x14/0x18/0x1c are arguments 1-3, not 4-6 as the decompiler assumed; the decompiler's unaff_EBX and seven-parameter signature are artifacts of that misalignment. Convention is the binary-wide stack default: the epilogue is a bare RET with no immediate, and this function itself cleans a callee's arguments with ADD ESP,0x10 after CALL 0x00015860. Pool is fdps because the body and all game-side callees live below 0x3b000 in the game segment and the callers are menu code, including the already-named fdps_battle_system_menu at 0x00014ab0 (five callers total, all menu-like).
open_question: The concrete type behind ctx (arg1) is unknown -- it is only forwarded to 0x00015860. The literal 0x18 passed as that callee's third argument is unexplained (plausibly a cursor cell height or a widget kind). Whether dir_blocked is genuinely a blocked/allowed mask or a neighbour-id table whose zero entry means 'no neighbour' cannot be settled without reading the caller that builds it.

name: fdps_draw_unit_status_panel
role: Renders the contents of a unit status panel (portrait, HP/MP numbers and gauge bars, level, stats and equipment icons) into a 320-pitch destination buffer for the given unit index.
plate_comment:
Draws the body of the unit status panel for one unit.

Algorithm:
1. If the global mode flag at 0x00060070 is set, latch the caller-supplied unit index into 0x00063fb0.
2. Resolve the unit record via the accessor at 0x0002d210(unit_index) and copy the fields it will print into locals: current/max HP (record+0x40 / +0x42), current/max MP (record+0x44 / +0x46), a two-digit value at +0x21, four three-digit stats at +0x48, +0x4a, +0x4c, +0x4e, a three-digit value at +0x3e, a two-digit value at +0x3b, and byte fields +0x07, +0x08, +0x1f, +0x20 used as sprite indices. The byte at +0x3c is displayed as 1000 when it holds the sentinel 0xff.
3. Pick the portrait entry from the table based at 0x00060138 (stride 0x30, first dword of the entry is an offset relative to the table base). The index is record+0x02 in the normal path and the caller-supplied unit index when 0x00060070 is set. Blit that 0x18 x 0x18 image at destination offset 0xd21.
4. Print every numeric field with the digit renderer at 0x00017530 (destination, pitch 0x140, value, digit count, 0). Before each print, the global colour selector 0x0006000c is set to 3 when the current value differs from its maximum, to 1 when the corresponding status byte (record+0x22, +0x23, +0x24) is non-zero, and back to 0 otherwise.
5. Draw the HP gauge at offset 0x9396 and the MP gauge at offset 0xab56 with the bar renderer at 0x00017740; the filled length is 0 when the maximum is not positive, otherwise ceil(current * 0x75 / maximum).
6. Draw the field at record+0x07 with the renderer at 0x000177d0 at offset 0x513, then blit three icons through 0x0001ff60 from the sheet in 0x000643c4 using sprite indices record+0x08 plus 1, record+0x20 plus 0xa1 and record+0x1f plus 0x97, at destination offsets 0x709, 0x1d80 and 0x1dc7.

All destination offsets are byte offsets into a buffer whose pitch is 0x140 (320) pixels, so they encode fixed y*320+x positions inside the panel.

Parameters:
  unit_index - index of the unit whose record is fetched and drawn.
  dest - base address of the destination pixel buffer (320-byte pitch).

Returns:
  Nothing.
evidence: Standard four-push prologue with both arguments read from [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18] and no stack cleanup in the epilogue; every call it makes pushes arguments and follows with ADD ESP,n. That is the documented binary-wide stack convention in rebuild_info/build_flags.md, so __cdecl. Purpose is fixed by the shape of the work: one record pointer obtained from 0x0002d210(unit_index), then a long straight-line sequence of draw calls whose second argument is always the constant 0x140 (320, the screen pitch) and whose destination is the second parameter plus a fixed offset. Two of the calls (0x00017740) compute ceil(cur*0x75/max) from the paired word fields at +0x40/+0x42 and +0x44/+0x46, which is a gauge bar scaled to 117 pixels from a current/maximum pair -- the classic HP and MP bars. The global at 0x0006000c is written immediately before each digit call with 3 when cur != max and 1 when a per-record boolean byte is set, i.e. a colour selector for damaged or flagged values. The remaining calls pass sprite indices derived from small byte fields into 0x0001ff60 together with the sheet pointer in 0x000643c4. A caller is already named fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window (00016aa0), which places this squarely as the content-drawing half of that window. Game logic drawing on game data structures, no CRT or Miles signature anywhere, so pool fdps.
open_question: The individual record fields are not identified: which of +0x48/+0x4a/+0x4c/+0x4e is attack, defence, agility etc., what +0x3b, +0x3c (0xff means display 1000) and +0x3e hold, and what the booleans at +0x22/+0x23/+0x24 mean. The meaning of the mode flag at 0x00060070 (which switches the portrait index between record+0x02 and the caller-supplied index and latches that index into 0x00063fb0) is also unresolved. Settling these needs the unit record layout and the panel background art, not this function.

name: fdps_load_status_cel_image
role: Opens MISC.VFS, loads the "Status.cel" entry, decodes it into a freshly allocated 320x200 (64000 byte) offscreen image buffer and returns that buffer.
plate_comment:
Loads the Status.cel image out of MISC.VFS into a new 320x200 offscreen buffer.

Algorithm:
  1. fdps_vfs_open("MISC.VFS" @ 0x60128) -> archive handle.
  2. fdps_vfs_load_file("Status.cel" @ 0x61590, handle) -> heap block holding the raw CEL file.
  3. malloc(0xfa00 = 64000) -> destination image buffer (320*200, one byte per pixel).
  4. free(archive handle) - the directory handle is no longer needed once the entry is read.
  5. Pixel payload starts at cel_base + *(int *)(cel_base + 0x0f); that pointer plus the destination
     buffer are handed to the CEL decoder at 0x568db with (320, 200, 320, 0, 0), i.e. full frame,
     destination pitch 320, drawn at origin.
  6. free(raw CEL block) and return the decoded image buffer.

Parameters:
  none.

Returns:
  void * - malloc'd 64000 byte 320x200 8bpp image containing the decoded Status.cel.
  The caller owns the block and must free it.
evidence: Disassembly references exactly two strings: "MISC.VFS" at 0x60128 (passed to the already-identified fdps_vfs_open at 0x39ab0) and "Status.cel" at 0x61590 (passed to fdps_vfs_load_file at 0x39bd0), so the asset being loaded is named directly by the binary. 0xfa00 = 64000 = 320*200 is the mode 13h frame size and matches the 0x140/0xc8/0x140 (320/200/320) argument group passed to the drawing routine at 0x568db. The two calls to 0x3d478 release the archive handle and the raw CEL block, while the malloc'd 64000 byte buffer is the return value, so this is a loader returning an image, not a drawing call. One of the four callers is fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window (0x16aa0), consistent with a status-screen background image. Standard four-push prologue (EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP), all callee arguments pushed on the stack with ADD ESP cleanup by this function, matching the binary default stack convention documented in rebuild_info/build_flags.md.
open_question: Whether 0x568db is a CEL/RLE decompressor or a plain rectangular copy was not verified (that function was not read); the field at CEL header offset 0x0f is treated as the payload offset but the rest of the CEL header layout was not confirmed here.

name: fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window
role: Opens the 151x149 unit information window during the battle player phase: looks up the unit record, builds the panel off-screen, plays the window-open sound, zooms it open, shows a second cross-faded page when the content does not fit, then zooms it closed and restores the screen.
plate_comment:
Battle unit information window.

Algorithm:
1. Resolves the unit record for the incoming unit id via FUN_0002d210 and reads the class byte at offset 7. If the class is in the range 0x24..0x27 the function returns immediately without touching the screen, so those unit kinds have no information window.
2. Acquires the drawing context via FUN_00016840, saves the global flag at 0x00060159 into 0x00063fb8 and clears it, and calls FUN_0002beb0 when the flag at 0x00060070 is clear.
3. Plays the sound effect named by the string at 0x0006159c ("OpWin1.wav", the window-open cue).
4. Allocates a 64000-byte buffer and copies the whole 320x200 VGA frame from 0x000a0000 into it, then allocates a second 0x57e3-byte buffer (151*149) for the window rectangle, and saves the current contents of the window rectangle out of the off-screen page (context + 0x3b58, i.e. screen position x=152, y=47, pitch 320).
5. Renders the panel into the off-screen page: frame/background via FUN_00016300 and FUN_00024ea0, nine content rows via FUN_00016e80 called once per row index 0..8, then FUN_000170c0 with the unit field at offset 2.
6. Queries the page content with FUN_00027840 into a 40-byte local descriptor. When the returned count is non-zero the window is animated open by FUN_0002fe40 with step 2,4,6,8,10, each step waiting on one full vertical retrace read from VGA status port 0x3da; the reverse loop (11 down to 1, step -2) animates it closed.
7. When the returned count exceeds 8 a second page is drawn (FUN_000276f0 with page index 8) and cross-faded in by FUN_00030230 in 8 steps (1..15 step 2), again one retrace per step, before the closing animation.
8. Restores state via FUN_000168e0, frees the three buffers, and calls FUN_000567b3.

Parameters:
  unit_id - identifier of the unit whose information window is shown; passed straight to the unit record lookup and to the page/text routines.

Returns:
  Nothing. The screen and the saved global flag are restored before returning.
evidence: The only caller in the game code is fdps_battle_player_phase_loop (plus FUN_00033f80), so this is a player-phase battle UI action. The global at 0x0006159c that is handed to FUN_0002a1f0 is the ASCIIZ string "OpWin1.wav", the open-window sound cue, which pins the function to opening a window rather than any other effect. The geometry is unambiguous: malloc(0xfa00) plus a copy from 0x000a0000 saves the 320x200 frame, malloc(0x57e3) is exactly 151*149 for the window rect, and the blits use width 0x97, height 0x95 at page offset 0x3b58 (x=152, y=47, pitch 0x140). The content comes from a unit record obtained twice from FUN_0002d210 with the incoming argument, gated on the class byte at +7, so the window is unit-specific information. The two step-loops around FUN_0002fe40 with a VGA 0x3da retrace wait per step are an open/close zoom animation, and the >8 branch with FUN_00030230 and two 4KB tables is a cross-fade to a second page. Pool is fdps because the routine is game-specific UI; only the malloc/free/memcpy/inp helpers at 0x0003d375, 0x0003d478, 0x0003d514, 0x0003d4e4 belong to the CRT. Convention is __cdecl: the single argument arrives at [EBP+0x14] on the stack, the function ends with a bare RET, and every call it makes pushes arguments and cleans them with ADD ESP,n.
open_question: The exact content of the panel is not settled. FUN_00016e80 (nine rows) and FUN_000170c0 draw it, and FUN_00027840 returns a count that selects one or two pages, but which unit fields are shown -- stats, spell list or description text -- cannot be decided without walking those callees. The meaning of the class range 0x24..0x27 that suppresses the window is also unknown.

name: fdps_draw_status_window_anim_frame
role: Composites one frame of the nine-step slide-in animation of the four-panel status window over a saved background and flips it to the VGA framebuffer after a vertical-retrace wait.
plate_comment:
Renders one frame of the four-panel status window slide-in animation.

Algorithm:
1. Copies four 9-entry int tables (0x14788, 0x147ac, 0x147d0, 0x147f4) onto the stack; each holds the per-step offset of one panel. Values converge on 15 / 108 / 148 / 0 and overshoot by one pixel at steps 6-7, giving the window a small bounce as it settles.
2. Allocates a 64000-byte (320x200) off-screen buffer and copies the background image argument into it.
3. Blits four rectangles of the composed window image into that buffer with fdps_blit_rect, each clipped to the current step offset so it appears to slide in from its own edge:
   - upper-left  panel, final rows 0..107,   cols 15..147,  grows leftward from column 148
   - lower-left  panel, final rows 108..199, cols 15..147,  grows upward from the bottom
   - lower-right panel, final rows 44..199,  cols 148..305, grows leftward, width capped at 158
   - upper-right panel, final rows 0..43,    cols 148..305, grows upward from row 44
4. Calls the 0x3d370 thunk with 15, then polls the VGA input status register at port 0x3DA until vertical retrace begins and ends.
5. Copies the 64000-byte buffer to 0xA0000 and frees it.

Parameters:
  background   pointer to a 320x200 8bpp image used as the frame backdrop
  window_image pointer to a 320x200 8bpp image holding the assembled window graphics
  step         animation step index, 0..8, used to index the four offset tables

Returns:
  nothing.
evidence: Disassembly is unambiguous about the mechanism: 0xfa00 = 64000 = 320x200, pitch 0x140 = 320 on every fdps_blit_rect call, the classic IN 0x3DA / TEST AL,8 retrace pair, and a final 64000-byte copy to 0xA0000 followed by a free of the scratch buffer, so this is a full-screen off-screen compose plus flip. The four tables at 0x14788..0x147f4 hold 9 ints each and are indexed by the third stack argument, and their values (-120,-100,-70,-40,-15,15,14,14,15 / 190,175,160,140,125,108,109,109,108 / 300,270,240,215,175,148,149,149,148 / -36,-32,-24,-16,-8,0,-1,-1,0) start off-screen and converge with a one-pixel overshoot, which is a slide-in animation table, not a data table. The window attribution comes from the already-named caller fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window at 00016aa0. Pool is fdps because it references game-owned layout tables and calls fdps_blit_rect; the only CRT touches are malloc/free/memcpy/inp. Arguments are read from [EBP+0x14], [EBP+0x18], [EBP+0x1c] and the function ends with a plain RET, so the caller cleans the stack: __cdecl, not the project-default __watcall.
open_question: Four other callers (000168e0, 000259c0, 00025da0, 00027c20) were not inspected, so it is unconfirmed whether the same fixed panel geometry serves windows other than the battle unit status window; if it does, a more generic name may be warranted. The purpose of the 0x3d370 thunk call with argument 15 (likely a frame delay) is unverified.

name: fdps_unit_status_window_wait_input
role: Frame-paced input wait loop for the unit status window: each tick it recomposes the window image plus the unit's animated walk-cycle sprite into an off-screen 320x200 buffer, presents it, and returns as soon as the input poller yields a code <= 0x7f.
plate_comment:
Frame-paced input wait loop for the unit status window.

Algorithm:
Copies a 15-entry sprite Y-position table from 0x14818 (15, 30, 70, 105, 140, 170, 150, 130, 150, 170, 160, 165, 165, 160, 170 -- a drop from the top of the screen followed by two bounces) into a local array, and sets the idle-animation frame counter to -1 (inactive). When the flag argument is non-zero it samples the CRT helper at 0x42cf8 and, when the value is a multiple of 200, arms the idle animation by setting the frame counter to 0.

It then loops: poll the input source at 0x178f0; a returned code greater than 0x7f means nothing selected yet, so a frame is drawn. A frame is skipped entirely unless the global tick at 0x69d64 differs from the last-drawn tick at 0x63fc0.

Per frame: allocate a 0x15180-byte 360x240 backing buffer and a 0xfa00-byte 320x200 work buffer, zero the work buffer, capture the current screen into the backing buffer (from 0xa0504 when the mode flag at 0x60070 is set, otherwise via the helper at 0x2bf60), copy it back into the work buffer, then free the backing buffer. The walk-cycle frame index is (tick at 0x63fc0 % 16) / 4, with 3 folded back to 1, giving the 0,1,2,1 cycle; it selects one of three sprite pointers inside the 0x30-byte per-unit record at the table based at 0x60138, whose four 0x0c-byte groups (offsets 0x00, 0x0c, 0x18, 0x24) are the four facings. A 0x240-byte 24x24 scratch buffer receives the decoded cel via the cel blitter, is blitted into the caller's window image at offset 0xd21 (column 161, row 10), and the window image is then blitted into the work buffer as a 0x123 x 0xc8 region at offset 0xf.

When the idle animation is armed, the frame counter drives four phases -- frames 0..14 draw the facing-0 sprite at the table's Y positions (the drop and bounce), frames 15..24, 25..34 and 35..44 draw the other three facings standing at row 170 -- after which a separate Y counter starting at 170 walks the sprite upward in steps of 4 until it passes row 10, at which point the frame counter returns to -1 and the sprite goes back to the plain walk cycle.

The work buffer is presented to VGA memory at 0xa0000 (whole 64000-byte copy when the mode flag is clear, otherwise a 0x138 x 0xc0 rect blit at 0xa0504), both remaining buffers are freed, and the last-drawn tick is updated.

Parameters:
  window_image -- pointer to the 320-pitch composed status window image; the unit sprite is stamped into it at offset 0xd21 each frame
  unit_index -- index into the 0x30-byte-per-entry sprite pointer table at 0x60138; overridden by the global at 0x63fb0 when the mode flag at 0x60070 is set
  allow_idle_animation -- non-zero enables the randomly triggered drop/bounce/turn/rise idle sequence

Returns:
  The input code returned by the poller at 0x178f0 once it is <= 0x7f.
prototype: int fdps_unit_status_window_wait_input(unsigned char *window_image, int unit_index, char allow_idle_animation)
evidence: Prologue is exactly the -4s stack-convention pattern documented in rebuild_info/build_flags.md (PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP, MOV EBP,ESP, first argument at [EBP+0x14], epilogue MOV ESP,EBP without LEAVE), and all three arguments are read from [EBP+0x14], [EBP+0x18] and [EBP+0x1c] with every call site here using PUSH plus ADD ESP -- caller cleanup, so __cdecl. Pool is fdps: it composes game screens, calls the already-named fdps_blit_rect (0x2f2f0) and fdps_cel_blit_sprite (0x2dba0), and touches VGA at 0xa0000/0xa0504 with a 320x200 (0xfa00) buffer. Subsystem is battle because the only named caller is fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window at 0x16aa0. The animation reading is grounded in the literal table at 0x14818 (Y values dropping 15..170 then bouncing 150/130/150/170) and in the 0x30-byte stride with four 0x0c-byte facing groups and the (tick%16)/4 index folded 3->1 into the classic three-frame 0,1,2,1 walk cycle. The loop is frame-gated by the tick globals 0x69d64 vs 0x63fc0 and exits on an input code <= 0x7f returned by 0x178f0.
open_question: The second caller FUN_00025b20 is unidentified, so the window may serve a non-battle context (party or character menu) as well; the exact meaning of the mode flag at 0x60070 (two different screen-capture and present paths) and of the CRT helper at 0x42cf8 used for the 1-in-200 idle trigger (rand or a clock) were not resolved. The precise semantics of the input codes above 0x7f returned by 0x178f0 are also unknown.

name: fdps_prompt_two_choice
role: Modal two-option prompt: captures the already-drawn prompt panel from the screen, then runs its own frame loop compositing that panel plus an animated left/right option cursor until the player confirms or cancels, returning the chosen option index or -1.
plate_comment:
Modal two-option (left/right) prompt loop.

Algorithm:
1. Allocates a 0x561E byte buffer and copies a 302x73 (0x12E x 0x49) region of
   VGA memory at 0xA9609 into it at stride 302. The caller has already drawn the
   prompt panel there, so this captures the panel bitmap. The four corner pixels
   (offsets 0, 0x12D, 0x54F0, 0x561D) are then cleared to 0 so the later masked
   blit renders the panel with transparent (rounded) corners.
2. Loops until a confirm or cancel key arrives. Each iteration:
   - calls the per-frame update helper at 0002EAB0 and allocates a 0x15180 byte
     (360x240) off-screen work buffer;
   - if the flag at 00060070 is zero, hands the work buffer to 0002BF60 to draw
     the background; otherwise copies the current 312x192 screen area at 0xA0504
     into the work buffer at offset 0x21D8 (x=24, y=24, stride 360);
   - masked-blits the captured panel into the work buffer at offset 0xC4FD
     (x=29, y=140) via 0002F390;
   - if the pointer at 00060120 is non-null, draws it through 000568DB at work
     buffer offset 0x9AD0 (x=32, y=110);
   - draws the two option graphics from the cel sheet at 000643DC at x=249 and
     x=275, y=123. The unselected side uses a fixed cel (13 for the right slot,
     8 for the left); the selected side cycles a 4-frame animation, cels 4..7 on
     the left and 9..12 on the right, indexed by ((frame/3)%4);
   - waits for vertical retrace by polling port 0x3DA (bit 3), blits the work
     buffer back to the screen at 0xA0504 (312x192), spins until the tick
     counter at 00069D64 changes, records it as the animation frame, and frees
     the work buffer;
   - reads a scancode via 000567BE: 0x1C (Enter) or 0x39 (Space) confirms and
     keeps the current selection; 0x01 (Esc) or 0x53 (Del) exits with -1;
     0x4B (Left) selects 0; 0x4D (Right) selects 1. Codes >= 0x7F are ignored.
3. Frees the captured panel buffer and returns the selection.

Selection starts at 0, so the left option is highlighted on entry.

Parameters: none.

Returns: 0 or 1 for the confirmed option (left or right), -1 if cancelled.
evidence: Disassembly reads no incoming stack slot and every callee gets its arguments pushed with caller-side ADD ESP cleanup, matching the binary-wide -4s stack convention recorded in rebuild_info/build_flags.md (prologue 53 56 57 55 89 E5, epilogue MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP). The geometry is self-consistent and pins the behaviour: 0x12E*0x49 = 0x561E exactly matches the allocation, the four cleared offsets are exactly the four corners of that rect, 0xA0504 and 0xA9609 are VGA addresses (rows 4 and 120 at stride 320), and 0x21D8 / 0xC4FD / 0x9AD0 are exact row*360+col offsets into the 360x240 work buffer. Port 0x3DA bit 3 polling is the standard VGA retrace wait, and the scancode set 0x1C/0x39/0x01/0x53/0x4B/0x4D is Enter/Space/Esc/Del/Left/Right, which fixes this as a left-right two-option prompt. It has 14 callers including fdps_battle_system_menu and fdps_run_bar_shop, i.e. a shared UI primitive rather than one screen's code, so the fdps pool and the menu subsystem are certain.
open_question: Which side is affirmative is not settled: the two option labels are cels 4..8 and 9..13 of the sheet at 000643DC and their artwork was not decoded, so the return values 0 (left) and 1 (right) could not be mapped to yes/no. The role of the pointer at 00060120 drawn through 000568DB (portrait or background layer) is also unconfirmed.

name: fdps_options_menu
role: Runs the four-entry option toggle menu, redrawing each entry with its ON or OFF label and flipping the corresponding global setting flag until the player cancels.
plate_comment:
Option toggle menu (four boolean game settings).

Algorithm:
Copies 16 zero bytes from 0x00014a9c into a 4-entry menu state array on the stack and clears the selection index. Then loops: for each of the four settings it stores a label id into a 4-entry id array, choosing the ON id when the flag is non-zero and the OFF id otherwise -- 0x0d/0x31 for the CD music flag at 0x00060008, 0x0e/0x32 for the flag at 0x00069d70 (written by fdps_audio_init), 0x0f/0x33 for the flag at 0x00060010, and 0x18/0x3c for the flag at 0x00060158 (also read by fdps_run_village_phase). The OFF id is always the ON id plus 0x24. It then calls the menu widget trio at 0x00016130 (draw), 0x00016200 (run selection, returns the chosen entry or -1) and 0x000161b0 (erase), all with (id array, state array, &selection). A return of -1 ends the loop and the function. Otherwise the flag matching the selection index is XORed with 1; selecting entry 0 additionally calls the audio routine at 0x00030cc0 with (global at 0x00069cf4, 0), and the loop repeats so the labels are redrawn in their new state.

Parameters: none.

Returns: nothing.
evidence: Structure is unambiguous: four global bytes each mapped to a pair of label ids differing by a constant 0x24 (ON/OFF label blocks), fed to the generic menu draw/select/erase trio, and XORed with 1 when their entry is picked -- a settings toggle menu. All four globals are written together by fdps_load_savegame and fdps_load_game_screen and by fdps_title_screen, i.e. they are persisted user options, and 0x00060008 is read by fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll and by the audio routine 0x00030cc0 while 0x00069d70 is written by fdps_audio_init. The only caller is fdps_battle_system_menu, so this is the options entry of the in-game system menu. Pool is fdps: game-specific globals, no CRT or Miles signature. The function takes no arguments and does not clean any stack on return, so the convention field is the project default; note that its callees are called with stack arguments and caller cleanup (ADD ESP,0xc), so the callees themselves are __cdecl.
open_question: The individual meaning of each of the four options is only partly pinned down: entry 0 is CD/BGM music, entry 1 (0x00069d70) is audio-related via fdps_audio_init, entries 2 (0x00060010, read from 0x00012e50 and 0x00013c90) and 3 (0x00060158, used by fdps_run_village_phase) are unidentified. Confirming them needs the label id table that maps 0x0d/0x0e/0x0f/0x18 to on-screen text.

name: fdps_load_data_tables
role: Loads the nine global game data tables (Friaprda.dat, FriLevUp.dat, Item.dat, EnemyDat.dat, ProMap.dat, ProEqu.dat, MagicDat.dat, GetMgTab.dat, RankUp.dat) by calling the shared file loader once per file and storing each resulting buffer pointer into its own BSS global.
plate_comment:
Loads the nine global game data tables into their BSS pointer slots.

Algorithm: performs nine fixed, unconditional calls to the shared file loader at 0x29400. Each call passes the function's own single stack argument through unchanged as the loader's first argument, a literal .dat filename as the second, and the address of a distinct BSS pointer global as the third. The order and the filename/destination pairing are hard-coded: Friaprda.dat -> 0x63fd8, FriLevUp.dat -> 0x63fec, Item.dat -> 0x63fe0, EnemyDat.dat -> 0x63fd4, ProMap.dat -> 0x63fd0, ProEqu.dat -> 0x63fe4, MagicDat.dat -> 0x63ff0, GetMgTab.dat -> 0x63fe8, RankUp.dat -> 0x63fdc. There is no branching, no error handling and no return value inspection; every loader result is discarded.

Parameters: one 32-bit stack argument at [ebp+0x14], never inspected here, forwarded verbatim as the first argument of every loader call.

Returns: nothing. Its effect is entirely through the nine BSS pointer globals in 0x63fd0..0x63ff0, which are zero in the image and therefore filled in at runtime.
evidence: Prologue is the project's default four-push frame (53 56 57 55 / 89 e5) with the only argument read at [ebp+0x14], and every call site pushes three dwords then does ADD ESP,0xc with a plain RET at the end, i.e. the -4s stack convention documented in rebuild_info/build_flags.md. The nine string constants at 0x6160c..0x61680 are the game's data-table filenames, read straight out of memory; the nine destinations at 0x63fd0..0x63ff0 read as all zeros in the image, so they are runtime pointer globals rather than data. That makes this game data (fdps pool, file_io) and not CRT or AIL: no CRT or Miles routine knows these filenames. The callee 0x29400 is a shared loader used from four sites; this function is the one that drives it over the global table set. One of its two callers is already named fdps_load_global_resources @ 0x29660, which places this squarely in the global resource load path.
open_question: The single argument's type and meaning are unsettled: it is forwarded untouched to 0x29400 and never used here. Plausible candidates are a path/prefix string, an arena or allocator handle, or a load-mode flag; deciding requires reading 0x29400, which is out of scope for this ticket. The prototype therefore uses a placeholder int of the correct width.

name: fdps_free_global_resource_buffers
role: Releases the nine globally cached resource buffers at 0x00063fd0..0x00063ff0 by calling the CRT free helper once per pointer during shutdown.
plate_comment:
Frees the group of nine global resource buffers held at 0x00063fd0..0x00063ff0.

Algorithm: pushes each of the nine global pointers in a fixed order (0x63fd8, 0x63fec, 0x63fd4, 0x63fd0, 0x63fe0, 0x63fe4, 0x63ff0, 0x63fe8, 0x63fdc) and calls the CRT free helper FUN_0003d478 for each, adjusting the stack by 4 after every call. The pointers are not cleared to NULL afterwards, so the function must be called exactly once. The globals are filled by the matching loader at 0x00018930 (reached from fdps_load_global_resources); each buffer additionally has its own small accessor (0x00018ab0, 0x00018ae0, 0x00018b70, 0x00018bd0, 0x00018c00, ...).

Parameters: none.

Returns: nothing.
evidence: Disassembly is a straight sequence of nine PUSH dword ptr [global] / CALL 0x0003d478 / ADD ESP,0x4 pairs with no other work; 0x0003d478 has ~96 callers spread across the whole image, the signature of the CRT free(). The nine globals are a contiguous dword cluster 0x00063fd0..0x00063ff0, each written only by FUN_00018930 (called from fdps_load_global_resources) and read by one small accessor, so this is the mirror-image teardown of that loader. The sole caller is fdps_shutdown_free_resources @ 00029440, confirming shutdown-time release. Game-side code that owns game globals, hence the fdps_ pool. No stack parameters are read (EBP frame with SUB ESP,0), so the prototype is void(void) and the default __watcall applies.
open_question: Which resource kind the nine buffers hold is not settled: the loader at 0x00018930 and its per-buffer accessors were not read, and no string or file-name evidence is reachable from this function. If the loader turns out to name a concrete asset class (e.g. fonts, portraits, UI tiles) the symbol should be specialised accordingly, and the subsystem may be graphics or file_io rather than memory.

name: fdps_get_class_record
role: Returns a pointer to one 10-byte PROMAP.DAT class record, computed as the loaded class-table base pointer plus index * 10.
plate_comment:
Returns a pointer to one record of the class table loaded from PROMAP.DAT.

Algorithm: multiplies the single stack argument by 10 (the PROMAP.DAT record stride, taken straight from the IMUL immediate), adds it to the class-table base pointer held in the BSS global at 0x63fd0, and returns the sum. There is no bounds check, no null check on the base pointer and no branching; the whole body is one IMUL, one load and one ADD. The base pointer is filled in at runtime by fdps_load_data_tables, which loads ProMap.dat into it, and is released by fdps_free_global_resource_buffers. The table is 410 bytes, i.e. 41 records; record 0 is a default entry, so callers index it as class code + 1.

Parameters: one 32-bit stack argument at [ebp+0x14], the record index (class code + 1).

Returns: pointer to the first byte of the requested 10-byte class record. The result is undefined if the index is out of range or if the table has not been loaded.
evidence: The body is the project's canonical data-table accessor shape: default four-push frame (PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP, MOV EBP,ESP), sole argument read from the stack at [ebp+0x14], IMUL by the stride immediate 0xa, added to the dword loaded from the BSS pointer global 0x63fd0, plain RET with no stack cleanup (-4s stack convention per rebuild_info/build_flags.md, matching the already-named fdps_load_data_tables). Xrefs to 0x63fd0 tie it down exactly: fdps_load_data_tables @ 0x189a1 stores the ProMap.dat buffer there and fdps_free_global_resource_buffers releases it, so the base is the PROMAP.DAT class table and the stride 10 matches its 10-byte record. resource_info/data_tables.md already lists 0x18b70 as the PROMAP.DAT accessor with stride 10 and index 'class code + 1', which this disassembly confirms independently. Game data, therefore fdps pool; no CRT or Miles routine touches these globals. Eleven callers, spread over battle and map logic (including fdps_battle_unit_turn @ 0x15470), which is the expected profile for a shared table accessor rather than a one-shot startup routine.

name: fdps_battle_advance_turn
role: Ends the player phase and drives the whole inter-turn sequence: rest HP regeneration with map redraw, the allied-NPC phase, the enemy phase announced by EnyPhase.saf, the turn-counter increment, and the start of the next player phase announced by PlyPhase.saf including per-unit MP regeneration.
plate_comment:
Advances the battle to the next turn.

Algorithm:
1. Clears the input-enabled flag at 0x00060159, allocates a 0x15180-byte (360x240) offscreen map buffer via 0x0003d375 and renders the battle map into it with 0x0002bf60.
2. Walks every unit (count at 0x00060150, unit record via 0x0002d210). A unit that has kind byte +0x06 == 2, none of flag bits 0x81 set in byte +0x05, zero in bytes +0x25 and +0x26, and current HP (+0x40) below max HP (+0x42) recovers maxhp/5 HP, clamped to max. Each heal draws a floating value over the unit with 0x0001ee10(buffer, unit_index, 0xff00, 3) and records that at least one unit rested.
3. Waits for the VGA vertical retrace by polling port 0x3DA bit 3 (0x0003d4e4), then blits the 312x192 map viewport from buffer+0x21d8 to video memory at 0xa0504 (0x0002f2f0). If any unit rested, plays REST.WAV via 0x0002a1f0. Delays 40 ticks, frees the buffer and repaints the frame (0x0002beb0).
4. Runs the allied-NPC phase: selects side 1 (0x0002e0c0 / 0x0001fa30) and calls 0x00012b20.
5. Shows the EnyPhase.saf banner (0x0001eb00), selects side 0 and runs the enemy phase 0x00012960.
6. Increments the turn counter at 0x00069ce8, shows the PlyPhase.saf banner, clears the cursor-active flag at 0x00069cd0 and selects side 2 (player).
