7. Applies per-unit MP regeneration: looks up item 0xa6 then 0xa7 on unit 4, item 0xb1 on unit 8, and item 0xb3 on every unit (0x00034520). When the found slot has bit 0x40 set in unit+0x0a[slot], the unit is not disabled (byte +0x05 == 0) and current MP (+0x44) differs from max MP (+0x46), it gains MP via 0x000275a0(unit, 0x0f), scrolls the view to the unit (0x0002da50), shows a type-0x0d floating value (0x0001f510) and waits for the display to finish (0x0001f340).
8. Re-enables the cursor (0x00069cd0 = 1), centres the view on unit 0 unless 0x000109b0 says otherwise, calls 0x000567b3 and sets the input-enabled flag at 0x00060159.

Every stage after step 3 is guarded by the battle-abort flag at 0x00069da0; when it is non-zero the function returns immediately without re-enabling input.

Parameters: none.

Returns: nothing.
evidence: Three string constants are referenced directly: 0x00061784 "REST.WAV" passed to the sound entry 0x0002a1f0 right after the rest-heal loop, and 0x00061790 "EnyPhase.saf" / 0x000617a0 "PlyPhase.saf" passed to 0x0001eb00, which fixes the enemy-phase and player-phase boundaries inside the body. Between those two banners the function increments a single dword at 0x00069ce8, which is the turn counter, and calls two distinct AI entry points (0x00012b20 for side 1, 0x00012960 for side 0) after setting the side through the 0x0002e0c0 / 0x0001fa30 pair with arguments 1, 0 and 2. The two callers are fdps_battle_end_phase_if_all_units_done (0x0002ea10) and fdps_battle_system_menu (0x00014ab0), i.e. the automatic and the manual end-turn paths, which confirms this is the single turn-transition routine of the battle subsystem rather than a helper. Pool is fdps: it touches battle unit records, the map blitter fdps_blit_rect and fdps_render_view_frame, and only reaches the CRT for malloc/free/inp/delay. Convention is the binary-wide stack convention: canonical four-push prologue (ebx/esi/edi/ebp, mov ebp,esp), plain RET with no immediate, and every call site cleans its own arguments with ADD ESP,n; the function itself takes no parameters.
open_question: The literal unit indices 4 and 8 paired with item ids 0xa6/0xa7 and 0xb1 in the MP-regeneration block are unexplained; they look like fixed party slots holding a specific MP-regenerating item, but the item table was not consulted. The exact meaning of the side codes 1/0/2 passed to 0x0002e0c0 and 0x0001fa30 is inferred from the banner ordering, not proven, and the roles of 0x0002db50, 0x00030cc0 and 0x000567b3 were not investigated.

name: fdps_play_vfs_animation
role: Plays a named animation entry from MISC.VFS full-screen: saves the current 320x200 VGA image, fades it to black, hands the loaded entry to the player, then fades the saved image back in.
plate_comment:
Play a named full-screen animation entry out of MISC.VFS, wrapped in a fade-out / fade-in of the screen that was showing before.

Algorithm:
1. fdps_vfs_load_entry("MISC.VFS", name) loads the entry and returns its in-memory handle.
2. Allocates two 64000-byte (320x200) buffers via the CRT allocator at 0003d375; both receive the current VGA page at 0xa0000 through the CRT block copy at 0003d514. One buffer keeps the pre-animation screen, the other is scratch for playback.
3. Fade out: for level = 1..5 calls fdps_blit_tint_rect(saved, 320, 0xa0000, 320, 320, 200, DAT_000653f0, DAT_000643f0, 0, level), i.e. redraws the saved image through the tint tables at increasing darkness. Each step first spins on VGA input status port 0x3DA bit 3 (wait for the retrace to start, then to end) and then waits for the tick counter DAT_00069d64 to change, so one fade step lands per frame.
4. Re-snapshots the (now black) screen into the scratch buffer.
5. If the requested name is exactly "PLYPHASE.SAF" (CRT string compare at 00042fe0), calls FUN_0001e840 on the scratch buffer for that entry's extra setup.
6. Calls FUN_0001ecf0(entry, scratch) to actually decode and play the entry, then frees the scratch buffer.
7. Fade in: same loop with level = 5..1 over the buffer holding the pre-animation screen, restoring what was on screen before the call, and frees both remaining allocations.

Parameters:
  name - NUL-terminated entry name inside MISC.VFS, pushed on the stack by the caller.

Returns:
  Nothing. On return the VGA page holds the screen that was showing on entry and every buffer allocated here has been freed.
evidence: Direct string evidence: the first call is fdps_vfs_load_entry(0x60128, arg) and 0x60128 holds "MISC.VFS"; the compare at 00042fe0 tests the argument against 0x617c0 = "PLYPHASE.SAF" (with "EasyAni.Saf" adjacent in the same string block), so the parameter is an entry name and this is game-side asset playback, not CRT or AIL. The two 0xfa00 (64000 = 320x200) allocations, the hard-coded 0xa0000 VGA aperture, the 320/320/200 geometry passed to the already-named fdps_blit_tint_rect, the 0x3DA bit-3 retrace spin and the DAT_00069d64 tick wait make the two symmetric 1..5 / 5..1 loops an unmistakable frame-paced fade out and fade in around the playback call at 0001ecf0. Convention is __cdecl, not __watcall: the sole parameter is read from [EBP+0x14] (stack) and every call site here pushes arguments and cleans with ADD ESP,n, with a bare RET at the end.
open_question: Whether the CRT routine at 0003d514 is memcpy (screen snapshot) or memset (buffer clear) was not settled by reading this function alone; the fade structure works either way but the exact role of the second buffer depends on it. Likewise the entry format actually decoded by FUN_0001ecf0 (a .SAF animation vs a single still image) is inferred from the file names and from the fact that the previous screen is restored afterwards, not proven here.

name: fdps_chapter_state_reset
role: Resets the per-chapter runtime state block and counters, re-initialises the chapter data from the current chapter id, and marks the chapter state active.
plate_comment:
Resets the per-chapter runtime state and brings it back online.

Algorithm:
  1. Clears the chapter-state active flag at 00069cd0 and the shared
     counter at 00069da0.
  2. Calls FUN_00022be0 with the current chapter id held in 00069cf4.
     That helper is called from nowhere else and does the chapter-specific
     re-initialisation.
  3. Zeroes the 0x20-byte state block at 000640d8 (memset-style helper at
     00042cd0, args pushed and popped by the caller).
  4. Zeroes four more counters/indices: 00069ce4, 00069ce0, 00069cd4,
     00069ccc.
  5. Sets the active flag 00069cd0 and the second flag 00069ce8 to 1, then
     calls the shared runtime helper at 000567b3 and returns.

Parameters:
  none. All inputs are read from globals, chiefly the current chapter id at
  00069cf4 which is written by the title screen, the demo, and the save/load
  screens.

Returns:
  void.

Called from the 31 dispatch stubs at 00020e90..00021650 (reached through the
function-pointer table at 00060074, dispatched by fdps_title_screen) and from
fdps_title_demo, so it is the common reset tail every chapter entry runs.
evidence: Prologue is the exact -4s signature 53 56 57 55 89 e5 documented in rebuild_info/build_flags.md, and every call site pushes arguments and cleans them itself (ADD ESP,0x4 / ADD ESP,0xc), so the binary-default stack convention applies; the function takes no arguments of its own. Pool is fdps: it touches only game globals, has no CRT or AIL signature, and its 32 callers are all game code. The global 00069cf4 that it feeds to FUN_00022be0 is written by fdps_title_screen, fdps_title_demo, fdps_load_savegame and fdps_load_game_screen and read by main and fdps_run_village_phase, which identifies it as the current chapter/scenario id. The 31 callers occupy a regular 0x40-byte-spaced block reached through the data table at 00060074 via a COMPUTED_CALL in fdps_title_screen, i.e. one entry stub per chapter, all sharing this reset tail. The body is pure state clearing followed by setting two flags to 1, which is initialisation, not gameplay.
open_question: The exact meaning of the individual globals is not settled: 00069cd0 is written from 40+ sites across battle, menu and title code and behaves like a general 'state valid/active' gate, and 00069da0 is a widely shared counter. The 0x20-byte block at 000640d8 is also touched by fdps_load_savegame, so it may be save-persisted chapter state rather than purely transient. Whether the family should be called 'chapter' or 'scenario' depends on what FUN_00022be0 actually loads.

name: fdps_field_load_chapter_resources
role: Frees the previously loaded field-map resource set and reloads every chapter resource (text, map header, detail, layer descriptor table, and per-layer mpl/cel/attr blobs) for the current chapter from the Field/Field1/Field2 VFS archives, then allocates the working tile buffer.
plate_comment:
Loads the whole field-map resource set for the current chapter.

Algorithm:
1. Releases the resource set left over from the previous chapter: for each of the DAT_00069cdc layers it frees the mpl pointer in DAT_00069cb0[i], the cel pointer in DAT_00069c20[i] and the attr pointer in DAT_00069c98[i].
2. Frees DAT_00060124 and reloads it with "fdetxt%02d.txt" (current chapter DAT_00069cf4 plus one) from Field.vfs -- the chapter text block.
3. Frees DAT_0006013c and reloads it with "map%02d.dat" from Field.vfs. Bytes 1 and 2 of that blob are copied out as the map dimensions into DAT_00064118 and DAT_0006410c.
4. Frees DAT_00060148 and reloads it with "M%02d.dtl" from Field1.vfs.
5. Loads "dsc%02d.dat" from Field2.vfs into a temporary buffer. Its first dword is the layer count, stored into DAT_00069cdc. The remaining data is an array of 32-byte layer descriptors starting at offset 4; for layer i the six dwords at +0x00..+0x14 are scattered into the parallel arrays DAT_00069bf0, DAT_00069c08, DAT_00069c80, DAT_00069c68, DAT_00069c50 and DAT_00069c38, and the bytes at +0x18 and +0x1c into the byte arrays at 0x00069cfe and 0x00069cf8.
6. For each layer i it then loads "m%02d%d.mpl" and "m%02d%d.cel" from Field1.vfs and "attr%02d%d.dat" from Field2.vfs (chapter, i) into DAT_00069cb0[i], DAT_00069c20[i] and DAT_00069c98[i].
7. Frees the descriptor buffer, frees the old working buffer DAT_00060144, reads the 16-bit width and height at offsets 7 and 9 of layer 0's mpl blob, allocates width*height*2+4 bytes for the new working buffer and writes the two dimensions as words at its offsets 0 and 2.
8. Calls FUN_00010b20 to finish initialising the freshly loaded map.

All file names are built with sprintf into a 0x38-byte stack buffer and resolved through fdps_vfs_load_entry, which returns a malloc'd copy of the archive member.

Parameters: none. The chapter index is read from the global DAT_00069cf4.

Returns: nothing. All results are published through the globals listed above.
evidence: The function references seven format strings at 0x619a4..0x619f0 ("fdetxt%02d.txt", "map%02d.dat", "M%02d.dtl", "dsc%02d.dat", "m%02d%d.mpl", "m%02d%d.cel", "attr%02d%d.dat") and the three archive names at 0x600f8/0x60102/0x6010d ("Field.vfs", "Field1.vfs", "Field2.vfs"), and passes each formatted name to the already identified fdps_vfs_load_entry at 0002a140. The free/reload pairs on DAT_00060124, DAT_0006013c, DAT_00060148, DAT_00060144 and the three per-layer pointer arrays make it a full teardown-and-reload of one chapter's field resource set, so it is game logic (fdps pool) and file_io in nature. Its only callers are FUN_00022be0 and fdps_load_savegame, i.e. entering a map and restoring a save -- exactly when a chapter's resources must be swapped. It takes no arguments (no incoming register or stack parameter is read; the decompiler's param_1/param_2/unaff_EBX are artefacts), so the default __watcall applies trivially. The other callees are CRT helpers: 00042d41 is sprintf (variadic, caller-cleaned stack), 0003d375 malloc, 0003d478 free.
open_question: The meaning of the individual fields in the 32-byte layer descriptor record (the six dwords and two bytes scattered into the parallel arrays) is not determined here, nor which of DAT_00064118 / DAT_0006410c is width vs height.

name: fdps_set_palette_range
role: Uploads a range of VGA DAC palette entries from an RGB triple array, adding a per-channel bias and clamping each component to 0..63.
plate_comment:
Uploads VGA DAC colour registers for a contiguous palette index range.

Algorithm: For each index i from start to end inclusive, writes i to the DAC write-index port 0x3C8, then reads three consecutive bytes from rgb (red, green, blue). Each byte has the matching bias added, is clamped to the range 0..63 (values above 0x3F become 0x3F, values below 0 become 0), and is written to the DAC data port 0x3C9. The rgb pointer advances by 3 per entry. All port writes go through the Watcom CRT outp helper at 00042cb8 (MOV EDX,[ESP+4]; MOV AL,[ESP+8]; OUT DX,AL). The DAC index is rewritten every iteration rather than relying on the DAC auto-increment. The bias arguments make this the single upload path used for fades and brightness ramps: passing 0,0,0 uploads the palette unchanged.

Parameters: rgb - pointer to packed RGB triples, one per palette entry, the first triple corresponding to index start; start - first palette index to write; end - last palette index to write, inclusive; r_bias, g_bias, b_bias - signed offsets added to the red, green and blue components before clamping.

Returns: nothing.
prototype: void fdps_set_palette_range(unsigned char *rgb, int start, int end, int r_bias, int g_bias, int b_bias)
evidence: The body writes the loop index to port 0x3C8 and three biased, clamped bytes to port 0x3C9 per entry, which is exactly the VGA DAC colour-register write protocol; the clamp bound 0x3F is the 6-bit DAC component range. The only callee, 00042cb8, is byte-for-byte the Watcom CRT outp (8b 54 24 04 8a 44 24 08 ee c3), confirming these are I/O port writes and not memory stores. Every one of the six arguments is read from the stack frame at [EBP+0x14] through [EBP+0x28] with no register argument used at all, and the function ends in a bare RET, so the caller cleans the stack: __cdecl, not the Watcom register default. Sixteen callers spread across title screen, village phase, battle and menu code make this a shared graphics service, hence the fdps pool rather than a one-shot startup routine.

name: fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group
role: Loads the 12 consecutive sprites belonging to one group index out of an open .CEL sheet into a global growable sprite cache, reusing the slot if that group is already cached, and returns the cache slot index.
plate_comment:
Loads one 12-sprite group from an open .CEL sheet into the global sprite cache.

Algorithm:
1. fseek(fp, 0x0F, SEEK_SET) and fread a fixed 0x2970 bytes (2652 u32 = 221 groups x 12) of the CEL offset table into a temporary malloc'd buffer, then free it after use. The offset table position 0x0F is hardcoded; the header field at 0x05 is never read.
2. Copy the 13 offsets [group_index*12 .. group_index*12+12] into a local array. Entry 12 is the start of the next group and acts as the end sentinel, so group_bytes = off[12] - off[0].
3. If the cache is empty (count at 0x69CF0 == 0): record the group key in the key table at 0x64060, malloc 0x5A0 + group_bytes for the cache buffer at 0x60138, seek to off[0], read group_bytes directly after the 0x5A0 header area, and fill the 12 pointer-table slots with byte offsets 0x5A0 + (off[i] - off[0]). The write cursor at 0x6411C becomes 0x5A0 + group_bytes. Returns slot 0.
4. Otherwise scan the key table for group_index; on a hit return that slot immediately without touching the cache or the count.
5. On a miss, append: store the key, realloc the cache to cursor + group_bytes, seek and read the group at the cursor, fill pointer-table slots (count*12 + i) with cursor + (off[i] - off[0]), advance the cursor and increment the count. Returns the new slot index.

The 0x5A0-byte header region holds exactly 30 slots of 12 u32 offsets; nothing bounds-checks the slot count against 30, so a 31st distinct group would write its pointer table over the cached pixel data. The fixed 0x2970-byte table read is larger than the offset table of a 1920-sprite sheet and spills into pixel data, but only the entries of the requested group are used.

Parameters:
  group_index - index of the 12-sprite group within the sheet (sprite index = group_index * 12 + i)
  fp          - FILE * for the already-opened .CEL sheet; the file position is left inside the sheet

Returns:
  int - cache slot index for the group, valid for the pointer table at the head of the cache buffer
evidence: Both arguments arrive purely on the stack at [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18] behind a PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP frame, no register arguments are read, and RET does no stack cleanup, so this is __cdecl. Every callee is a CRT routine called cdecl-style with ADD ESP cleanup: 0x42E86 as fseek(fp, off, 0), 0x4270D as fread(buf, 1, len, fp), 0x3D375 as malloc, 0x3D478 as free, 0x4308C as realloc; there is no game logic in the callees, so this function itself is the fdps-pool loader. The seek to 0x0F and the u32 offset table with an end sentinel match the .CEL layout documented in resource_info/cel.md exactly (header 15 bytes, offset table hardcoded at 0x0F, length of sprite i = off[i+1] - off[i]). The stride of 12 with a 13th sentinel entry and the fixed table read of 0x2970 = 2652 = 221 * 12 u32 entries match ICON.CEL's 1920 sprites = 160 groups x 12. The globals form one cache: 0x69CF0 = cached group count, 0x64060 = key array of group indices, 0x60138 = cache buffer base, 0x6411C = append cursor; the 0x5A0 reserved head is 30 slots x 12 u32. Callers include fdps_load_field_chapter_resources and fdps_load_savegame, consistent with unit/tile sprite loading.
open_question: Which .CEL file the caller has open is not settled from this function alone; the 12-per-group stride and the 221-group table size point to ICON.CEL but the FILE * comes in as a parameter. The exact meaning of the 12 sprites in a group (directions x animation frames) is also unresolved, as is whether any caller can ever exceed the 30-slot pointer-table capacity.

name: fdps_roster_add_character
role: Appends one character to the 0x50-byte unit roster array, filling the new entry from the character's base record and its growth table (stats scaled by level).
plate_comment:
Adds a character to the unit roster.

Algorithm:
Computes the destination slot as g_roster_base[g_roster_count] where the entry
stride is 0x50 bytes. Looks up two per-character tables by id: a base record
(FUN_00018ab0) and a growth table (FUN_00018ae0). Level is base_record[2].
Max HP = *(int16*)(base+3) + growth[6] * (level - 1);
max MP = *(int16*)(base+5) + growth[8] * (level - 1).
The entry is then filled: +5 = 0, +6 = 2 (side/team tag), +7 and +8 = the
character id, +9 = 0, +0x0a = 0x40, +0x0b = base[0x0c], +0x0c = 0x40,
+0x0d = base[0x0d]. Four two-byte slots at +0x0e..+0x15 are copied from
base[0x0e..0x11]; each slot's flag byte is 0x80 when the source value is 0xff
(empty) and 0 otherwise. Two further slots at +0x16 and +0x18 are set to 0x80
(empty). Four bytes are copied from base+8 to entry+0x1a, +0x1e = 0,
+0x1f = base[0], +0x20 = base[1], +0x21 = level, six bytes at +0x22 are
cleared, +0x31 = 0xff. Three level-scaled stats follow:
+0x37 = *(int16*)(base+0x12) + growth[0] * level,
+0x39 = *(int16*)(base+0x14) + growth[2] * level,
+0x3e = *(int16*)(base+0x16) + growth[4] * level;
+0x3b = base[7], +0x3c = 0. Current and maximum HP are stored at +0x40/+0x42
and current and maximum MP at +0x44/+0x46. Finally FUN_00023ac0 is called with
the new slot index and the roster count is incremented.

Parameters:
  char_id - character/unit identifier, used as the lookup key for both the base
            record and the growth table, and stored in the entry at +7 and +8.

Returns:
  Nothing. The new entry is written into the global roster array and the global
  roster count is incremented.
evidence: The single argument arrives on the stack at [EBP+0x14] (four callee-saved pushes plus the return address precede it) and every call site is a 10-byte PUSH imm8 / CALL / ADD ESP,4 sequence, so the caller cleans up: __cdecl, not __watcall. The body is pure game data manipulation with no CRT or AIL character, hence pool fdps; the only library calls are a 4-byte block copy (0x0003d514) and a 6-byte zero fill (0x00042cd0). The purpose is fixed by the arithmetic: two per-id lookup tables feed base + growth * level formulas whose results land in adjacent word pairs at +0x40/+0x42 and +0x44/+0x46, the classic current/maximum HP and MP layout, while the entry index comes from a counter global (0x00064114) that the function increments and a base pointer global (0x00064108) with a 0x50-byte stride. Twelve distinct callers, one of which is the already-named fdps_title_demo, which calls it twelve times in a row with immediate constants to populate a demo party.
open_question: Whether this roster is specifically the battle unit array or a general party roster shared by the menu and battle subsystems could not be settled from this function alone; the subsystem field is the best fit rather than a confirmed one. The meaning of the constant 2 stored at +6 and of the four/six equipment-or-spell slots at +0x0e..+0x19 is also unresolved.

name: fdps_load_savegame
role: Reads the whole FDE.SAV save file into a temporary buffer, verifies its checksum, and rebuilds every global game-state block (field data, unit array, palette, scalar header fields) before handing control to the play phase.
plate_comment:
Loads the saved game FDE.SAV and restores the whole game state from it.

Algorithm:
1. malloc(0x59cb) for the raw save image; on failure print "Out of Memory on get save buffer!!!" and exit(1).
2. fopen("FDE.SAV", "rb"), fread(buf, 1, 0x59cb, fp), fclose.
3. Descramble the image (0x000568b7) and recompute its checksum (0x00056898); if the result differs from the dword stored at buf+0x59c7 the save is corrupt: blank the screen (0x000205b0), blit a warning message (0x0001ff60 with source 0xaa44a at 320,208 size 0x140x0xd0) and run 0x00020820.
4. Fan the image out into the global state:
   - buf+0x08a3, 0xa00 bytes -> buffer pointed to by [0x00064108]
   - reload the palette resource "Fde.pal" from "MISC.VFS" (0x0002a140) into [0x000643bc], freeing the previous one
   - buf+0x30c5 -> [0x00069cf4] (phase/chapter selector), then 0x000227e0
   - fresh malloc(0x8a3) "fieldadr" buffer at [0x0006013c] filled from buf+0x0000; its bytes 1 and 2 become [0x00064118] and [0x0006410c]
   - unit count = buf+0x30c4 -> [0x00060150]; fresh malloc(0x1e00) "ManDataSeg" buffer at [0x00069cd8] filled from buf+0x12a3 with count*0x50 bytes (0x50-byte records)
   - buf+0x30a3, 0x20 bytes -> 0x000640d8
5. fopen("ICON.CEL", "rb"), and for each unit record look up its icon with 0x00023050(record[7], fp), storing the result in record[2]; fclose.
6. Copy the remaining scalar header fields out of buf+0x30c3 (bytes 0, 3..6 scaled by 0x18, 9, dword at 0xa, bytes 0xe..0x11) into their globals, then free the save image.
7. Run the post-load setup (0x0002e910, 0x0002beb0), load "PlyPhase.saf" (0x0001eb00) and enter the play phase with 0x00030cc0(phase, 0).

Parameters: none.

Returns: nothing. Does not return at all when a malloc fails, because the error path calls exit(1).
evidence: The disassembly fopen()s the string "FDE.SAV" (0x00060118) with mode "rb" (0x00061a00), freads 0x59cb bytes, fcloses, then checksums the buffer and compares against the dword embedded at buf+0x59c7 -- the classic save-file integrity check. The three fatal-error strings it prints name exactly what it is allocating: "Out of Memory on get save buffer!!!" (0x00061a50), "Out of Memory at get fieldadr!!!" (0x00061a80) and "Out of Memory at get ManDataSeg!!!" (0x00061aa4). Every subsequent block is a memcpy from a fixed offset of the save image into a global, so the function is a pure save-image unpacker rather than a generic file reader. It is called from fdps_title_screen (0x0002a2b0), i.e. the load-game entry of the title menu, and from 0x00014ea0. Pool is fdps: it is in the game segment below 0x3b000, uses game globals and game resource files, and calls the CRT (malloc 0x0003d375, free 0x0003d478, memcpy 0x0003d514, fopen 0x0004265e, fread 0x0004270d, fclose 0x000428be, printf-like 0x00042deb, crt_exit) rather than being part of it. Convention is the binary default stack convention: standard four-push prologue (PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP, MOV EBP,ESP), MOV ESP,EBP epilogue, and every call site passes arguments on the stack and cleans up with ADD ESP,n. It reads no positive EBP offsets, so it takes no parameters -- the decompiler's param_1/param_2/unaff_EBX are artefacts.
open_question: The literal passed to 0x0001eb00 is 0x00061acc = "PlyPhase.saf", which starts one byte inside the string "\n FPlyPhase.saf" at 0x00061ac9 -- verified by a raw memory read, so either the real filename is "PlyPhase.saf" and the leading "\n F" belongs to a neighbouring format string, or this is an original off-by-one. What 0x000568b7 (descramble) and 0x00056898 (checksum) compute exactly, and the meaning of the individual header bytes at buf+0x30c3, were not opened.

name: fdps_load_game_screen
role: Shows the load-game screen, lets the player pick a save slot, then reads FDE.SAV and installs the chosen slot's 0xa00-byte block plus its trailing scalar fields into the live game state globals.
plate_comment:
Load-game screen: pick a save slot and install it into the live game state.

Algorithm:
1. Sets DAT_00064104 = 1 (mode/state flag while the load screen is up).
2. Loads the cel resource "Load.cel" (string at 0x00061aec) via FUN_00024830 and blits it full screen through FUN_0002fb80 (320x200 to 0xa0000, 16x16 tile params).
3. Calls the slot-selection UI FUN_00024650, passing &slot_index; it returns 1 when the player confirmed a slot. Releases the cel with FUN_0003d478.
4. On confirm: allocates 0x59cb bytes (FUN_0003d375), opens "FDE.SAV" (string at 0x00060118) with mode/second string at 0x00061a00 via FUN_0004265e, freads 0x59cb elements of size 1, post-processes the buffer with FUN_000568b7(buf, 0x59cb) (decode/checksum), closes the file.
5. Computes slot = buf + 0x312b + slot_index * 0xa28, memcpys the first 0xa00 bytes into the global game-state buffer pointed to by [0x00064108], then unpacks the trailing fields: slot[0xa00] -> DAT_00069cf4, slot[0xa01] -> DAT_00064114, dword slot[0xa02] -> DAT_000643a4, slot[0xa06] -> DAT_00060158, slot[0xa07] -> DAT_00060010, slot[0xa08] -> DAT_00060008, slot[0xa09] -> DAT_00069d70. When DAT_00060070 is zero it also copies the dword at slot+0x9ec into DAT_00064110.
6. Blits the caller-supplied cel handle back through FUN_0002fb80 to restore the screen and returns the selection result.

Parameters:
  restore_cel - cel/image handle blitted after the load screen closes, restoring the caller's background. Arrives on the stack at [EBP+0x14].

Returns:
  The slot-selection result: 1 when a save was loaded into the game state, otherwise the non-confirm code from the selection UI.
evidence: Two string references settle the purpose: 0x00061aec is "Load.cel" (the byte before it makes the Ghidra label read "tLoad.cel") and 0x00060118 is "FDE.SAV", the save file. The call pattern around FDE.SAV is textbook stdio: FUN_0004265e(name, mode) -> handle, FUN_0004270d(buf, 1, 0x59cb, handle) with the classic fread argument order, FUN_000428be(handle) close, with FUN_0003d375(0x59cb) as the matching allocation. The slot arithmetic buf + 0x312b + i*0xa28 and the memcpy of 0xa00 bytes into the global at [0x00064108] plus the byte/dword unpack at slot+0xa00.. is a save-slot record being installed into live state, so the pool is fdps game logic, not CRT. Convention is __cdecl: the only incoming argument is read at [EBP+0x14], i.e. the first stack slot after the pushed EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP and return address, the function ends in a plain RET, and every call it makes pushes arguments and follows with ADD ESP. The unaff_EBX and extraout_* soup in the decompilation is Ghidra guessing a register convention that the disassembly contradicts.
open_question: The second operand of FUN_0004265e (0x00061a00) was not read, so whether it is a mode string or a path prefix is unconfirmed. The exact meanings of the unpacked globals (DAT_00069cf4, DAT_00064114, DAT_000643a4, DAT_00060158, DAT_00060010, DAT_00060008, DAT_00069d70, DAT_00064110) and of the guard DAT_00060070 are unknown, as is what FUN_000568b7 does to the buffer (decrypt vs checksum).

name: fdps_save_slot_select_loop
role: Runs the interactive cursor loop over the three save/load slots: reads scancodes, wraps the slot index modulo 3, animates the LoadKon.cel cursor over a restored background page each vsync, and returns 1 on confirm or -1 on cancel.
plate_comment:
Save/load slot selection loop.

Algorithm:
1. Loads the cursor sprite "LoadKon.cel" out of "MISC.VFS" via fdps_vfs_load_entry and keeps the handle for the whole loop.
2. Loops until a result is decided:
   - Reads one keyboard scancode (masked to 8 bits).
   - Scancode 0x48 (Up) or 0x4B (Left): *slot = (*slot + 2) % 3, plays "Beep.wav".
   - Scancode 0x4D (Right) or 0x50 (Down): *slot = (*slot + 1) % 3, plays "Beep.wav".
   - Scancode 0x01 (Esc): result = -1, loop ends.
   - Scancode 0x39 (Space) or 0x1C (Enter): accepted when the global mode flag at 0x00064104 is zero, or when the per-slot entry at 0x000640F8[*slot] is non-zero; on acceptance result = 1 and "morSure.wav" plays. Otherwise the key is ignored.
   - Allocates a 64000-byte off-screen page, copies the caller's background page into it, picks the cursor animation frame as ((tick >> 2) & 3), folding frame 3 back to 1, where tick is the timer counter at 0x00069D64.
   - Blits the cursor with fdps_cel_blit_sprite at x = 10, y = 25 + 52 * (*slot) into the off-screen page, calls FUN_00015be0, waits for vertical retrace by polling bit 3 of port 0x03DA, copies the page to 0xA0000, waits for the timer tick to change, then frees the page.
3. Frees the cursor sprite and returns the result.

Parameters:
  background - pointer to a 64000-byte (320x200) source page that is restored under the cursor every frame.
  slot       - pointer to the currently highlighted slot index; updated in place and left holding the final selection.

Returns:
  1  when the player confirmed the highlighted slot.
  -1 when the player cancelled with Esc.
evidence: Both parameters are read from [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18] after the PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP prologue, i.e. they arrive on the stack, and the function returns with a plain RET while every call site inside it cleans with ADD ESP -- stack args plus caller cleanup means __cdecl. The identity comes from the strings it references: fdps_vfs_load_entry("MISC.VFS", "LoadKon.cel") loads the cursor sprite, and the two sound calls pass "Beep.wav" (move) and "morSure.wav" (confirm). The index arithmetic is a strict modulo 3 in both directions, the y coordinate is 25 + 52*index, and Enter/Space is gated on a per-index table at 0x000640F8 -- three selectable rows whose acceptance depends on the entry being occupied, i.e. save slots. Its callers are FUN_000241e0 and fdps_load_game_screen, which puts it squarely on the save/load screen. The frame body is the standard loop of this engine: allocate a 64000-byte page, restore background, blit, wait for retrace on port 0x3DA, copy to 0xA0000, wait for the timer tick at 0x00069D64.
open_question: The meaning of the global flag at 0x00064104 is not settled: when it is zero every slot is acceptable, otherwise only occupied slots are. It most likely distinguishes the save screen from the load screen, but that was not confirmed from this function alone. The contents and element type of the slot table at 0x000640F8 were likewise not inspected.

name: fdps_saveload_screen_build
role: Builds the save/load menu screen into a freshly allocated 320x200 offscreen page: blits the named background cel from MISC.VFS, reads FDE.SAV, marks and renders the three save slots, reloads the party icon set from ICON.CEL, and returns the page.
plate_comment:
Builds the save/load menu screen page.

Algorithm:
1. Loads the background cel named by bg_cel_name out of the MISC.VFS archive (fdps_vfs_load_entry) and allocates a 64000-byte (320x200) offscreen page. Blits the cel into the page at pitch 0x140 with all clip/offset arguments zero, then frees the cel.
2. Allocates a 0x59CB-byte save-file buffer and opens FDE.SAV with mode "rb". If the file exists it is read whole (fread size 1, count 0x59CB), post-processed by FUN_000568b7 over the same 0x59CB bytes, and closed; if it does not exist the buffer is filled with 0xFF so every slot reads as empty.
3. For each of the three save slots i (record base = buf + 0x312B + i * 0xA28): the byte at record + 0xA00 acts as the occupied marker. 0xFF stores 0 into the slot-occupied flag array at 0x640F8[i], anything else stores 1. The slot record is then rendered by FUN_00024A40 into the page at row 0x1A + i * 0x34, column 0x0D, pitch 0x140. The save buffer is freed afterwards.
4. If the icon-loaded flag at 0x69CF0 is set, the previously loaded icon block at 0x60138 is freed and the flag cleared. ICON.CEL is then opened "rb" and, for each of the 0x64114 party records (array at 0x64108, stride 0x50), the icon id at record + 7 is passed to FUN_00023050 together with the open file; the file is closed at the end.
5. Returns the offscreen page pointer.

Parameters:
  bg_cel_name - name of the background cel entry inside MISC.VFS; this is what distinguishes the save screen from the load screen, both of which call this function.

Returns:
  Pointer to the newly allocated 64000-byte offscreen page holding the composed screen. Ownership passes to the caller, which is responsible for freeing it.
evidence: Disassembly reads exactly one stack argument at [EBP+0x14] (frame is PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP, MOV EBP,ESP, so that is the first stack slot past the return address) and every call site pushes arguments and cleans with ADD ESP, so the convention is stack-based __cdecl and the single parameter is a char*. That parameter is passed as the second argument to the already-named fdps_vfs_load_entry alongside the literal "MISC.VFS" at 0x60128, so it is a VFS entry name. The 0xFA00 allocation is exactly 320*200 and is handed to the already-named fdps_cel_blit_sprite with pitch 0x140, identifying it as a full-screen offscreen page; the same pointer is what the epilogue returns. The literal "FDE.SAV" at 0x60118 opened with "rb" at 0x61A00 via the fopen/fread/fclose/memset quartet (0x4265E / 0x4270D / 0x428BE / 0x42CD0, recognisable from their argument shapes: ptr,1,count,fp and ptr,0xFF,count) fixes the save-file read; the 3-iteration loop with 0xA28 stride and the 0xFF empty marker at +0xA00 is per-save-slot, and the destination rows 0x1A + i*0x34 are evenly spaced screen lines. The literal "ICON.CEL" at 0x61A04 plus the loop over the 0x50-stride record array at 0x64108 bounded by the count at 0x64114 is the party icon reload. Both callers (FUN_000241E0 and the already-named fdps_load_game_screen at 0x24490) are menu-level, matching a shared save/load screen builder parameterised by the background name. Game logic reading game data files, hence the fdps pool.
open_question: FUN_000568b7 is applied to the whole 0x59CB-byte save image right after the read and could be a decrypt, a checksum verification or a version fixup; the disassembly here only shows it takes (buffer, size) and its return value is discarded. The exact meaning of the 0x312B header preceding the three 0xA28 slot records is also not settled by this function.

name: fdps_unit_collect_known_spells
role: Expands the 40-bit spell bitmask held at offset 0x1a of a unit record into a list of spell ids, optionally writing the ids into a caller-supplied byte buffer, and returns how many bits were set.
plate_comment:
Expands a unit's 40-bit spell bitmask into a list of spell ids.

Algorithm: Looks up the unit record for the incoming id via fdps_get_unit_record (0x0002d210). Walks the five bytes at record offset 0x1a..0x1e; for each byte it tests bits 0..7 from least significant upwards. For every set bit it forms the id byte_index * 8 + bit_index (0..39) and, when the output pointer is non-NULL, stores that byte at the next free slot of the output buffer; the running slot counter is incremented for every set bit whether or not the buffer is written. Nothing bounds-checks the buffer, so it must have room for all 40 ids. Passing NULL as the buffer turns the function into a pure population count of the mask.

Parameters:
  unit_id - index of the unit record, passed unchanged to fdps_get_unit_record.
  out_ids - byte buffer receiving the ids of the set bits in ascending order, or NULL to only count them.

Returns: The number of set bits in the 40-bit mask, i.e. the number of ids written when out_ids is non-NULL.
evidence: Disassembly is unambiguous about the mechanism: the only callee is fdps_get_unit_record (0x0002d210, already identified as base + index*0x50 accessor of the global unit-record array), the outer loop runs local index 0..4 reading MOV AL,byte ptr [EDX + 0x1a], the inner loop runs 0..7 with SAR EAX,CL / TEST AL,0x1, and the stored value is MOV AL,[EBP-0xc] / SHL AL,3 / ADD AL,[EBP-0x14], i.e. byte*8 + bit. The store is skipped when [EBP+0x18] is zero, so the second argument is an optional output buffer, and the counter at [EBP-0x10] is returned. Five bytes is exactly 40 bits and the game has exactly 40 spells (assets/spells.md), which fixes the mask as one bit per spell rather than an arbitrary flag word. Caller set supports the spell reading: fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window uses the returned count to decide whether a second information page is needed (count > 8, second page drawn with page index 8, i.e. eight list rows per page), and the remaining callers (0x00013420, 0x00013920, 0x00015d00, 0x000276f0, 0x000278e0, 0x00027c20, 0x00028130) are menu/battle-UI routines, which is where a spell list is enumerated. Pool is fdps: game-specific record layout, no CRT or AIL behaviour. Convention is __cdecl - prologue is the standard binary-wide Watcom stack frame (PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP, MOV EBP,ESP), both arguments are read from [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18], the call to 0x0002d210 pushes its argument and cleans with ADD ESP,4, and the function itself ends in a bare RET.
open_question: That the ids are spell ids rather than some other 40-value enumeration is inferred from the bit width matching the 40-spell table and from the caller context; no caller was read to confirm that the returned bytes are used as spell-table indices, and the field at unit-record offset 0x1a is not yet documented in the knowledge base. Subsystem is tagged battle because the confirmed caller is the battle status window, but menu callers exist too.

name: fdps_set_flag_bit
role: Sets one bit in the 8-bit-per-byte flag array that starts at offset 0x1a of the record returned by the resolver at 0x2d210 for the given handle.
plate_comment: Algorithm: Builds an 8-entry power-of-two mask table on the stack by copying 8 bytes from the const image at 0x27660 (01 02 04 08 10 20 40 80) with two MOVSD. Calls the record resolver at 0x2d210 with the first argument and keeps the returned base pointer. Splits the second argument into a signed byte index (arg2 / 8, compiled as the SAR/SBB divide-by-power-of-two idiom) and a bit index (arg2 % 8, computed with IDIV by 8 and taking the remainder). ORs the mask for the bit index into the byte at base + 0x1a + byte index, i.e. base[0x1a + n/8] |= 1 << (n % 8). Nothing is read back and nothing is returned. Parameters: arg1 at [EBP+0x14] is the handle or record selector passed straight through to the resolver at 0x2d210; arg2 at [EBP+0x18] is the signed bit number within the flag array at offset 0x1a. Returns: nothing; EAX is left holding the resolved record pointer as a side effect only.
evidence: Prologue is exactly the project default 53 56 57 55 89 e5 with the first argument at [EBP+0x14], the -4s stack calling convention recorded in rebuild_info/build_flags.md, and the epilogue is MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP with a plain RET, so the caller cleans the stack: __cdecl. The callee at 0x2d210 is invoked as PUSH EAX / CALL / ADD ESP,4, same convention. The 8 bytes at 0x27660 read back as 01 02 04 08 10 20 40 80, which fixes the local array as a bit-mask table rather than data, so the OR at 0x28309 is unambiguously a set-bit-n operation on a byte array based at record offset 0x1a. No CRT or AIL string, no library idiom, four in-image callers including the already-named fdps_title_demo at 0x2ac10, so the pool is fdps.
open_question: What the record at 0x2d210 actually is and what the flag array at offset 0x1a means are both unresolved, so the subsystem cannot be pinned down; 0x2d210 is a 0x25-byte accessor with no data references of its own, meaning its base comes from the argument. Identifying it would also settle whether arg1 is a pointer or an index, and would let this function get a more specific name than the generic set-flag-bit.

name: main
role: The program's C entry point: verifies the installation and the CD-ROM, reads the Disk.no file, switches to VGA mode 13h, then runs the top-level game state loop until the quit flag is set and restores text mode on the way out.
plate_comment:
C entry point of FDPS. Called by the Watcom startup routine at 0004df4c, which pushes _argc (0006a3b4) and _argv (0006a3b8) and passes this function's return value to exit().

Algorithm:
  1. access("DISK.NO", 0) via INT 21h AH=43h. A non-zero result means the game was
     never installed: print "\nCan't found file 'Disk.No' !!!\a\n" and
     "Please use install function.\n", then exit(1).
  2. fopen("Disk.no", "rt"), three fscanf(fp, "%s", ...) reads and fclose(). The first
     two tokens go to a stack buffer and are discarded; the third is stored in the
     global string buffer at 000643e8. Sets the global at 00069d54 to -1.
  3. Calls the CD-ROM presence check at 0003c636 (returns a 16-bit value, sign-extended
     by CWDE). Anything other than 1 prints
     "Fatal error: CDROM is not install!!!\a\n" and "Check your CDROM please!!!\n",
     then exit(1).
  4. Subsystem init: 000304e0(0x19) and 00029660(), then int386(0x10, &regs, &regs)
     with regs.ax = 0x13 to enter VGA 320x200x256 mode.
  5. Clears the state globals (00069cf0, 00069cdc, 00069da0) and the quit flag at
     000643eb, calls 0002a2b0() once, then loops while the quit flag is zero:
       - 0002bae0() pumps one iteration;
       - the request code left in 00069da0 is dispatched: 0 does nothing, 1 runs
         0002a960() followed by 0002a2b0(), 2 calls the handler taken from the
         function-pointer table at 00060304 indexed by the mode selector in 00069cf4
         and then 00031210();
       - the request code is reset to 0 at the end of every iteration.
  6. Shutdown: 00029440(), 000305a0(), 0003c4a7() (pairs with the CD check),
     int386(0x10, &regs, &regs) with regs.ax = 3 to return to text mode, and finally
     prints "\nThank you for playing Flame Dragon Plus!! \n\n".

Parameters:
  argc, argv - passed on the stack by the startup code but never read by this function.

Returns:
  Nothing meaningful. Control falls off the end of the function, so EAX holds whatever
  the final print call left there; the startup code feeds it to exit(). In C source
  terms this is a main() with no return statement.
evidence:
Caller 0004df4c is the Watcom C startup: it computes the stack size from 00060438, calls the initialisation chain, pushes the globals at 0006a3b4/0006a3b8 (argc/argv), calls this function and passes the result straight to exit (00042e0f) - the canonical __CMain -> main -> exit shape, and 0004df4c is this function's only caller. String evidence, read directly out of .data: 00061be0 "DISK.NO", 00061be8 "
Can't found file 'Disk.No' !!!\a
", 00061c0c "Please use install function.
", 00061c2c "rt", 00061c30 "Disk.no", 00061c38 "%s", 00061c3c "Fatal error: CDROM is not install!!!\a
", 00061c64 "Check your CDROM please!!!
", 00061c80 "
Thank you for playing Flame Dragon Plus!! 

" - the last one names the game and is the program's final output. CRT primitives identified by reading them: 00042438 is access() (INT 21h AH=43h get-attributes on the EDX filename, error funnelled through 0004bd13); 0004265e is fopen (name, mode); 00043243 is fscanf (stream, format, buffer); 000428be is fclose; 00042deb is the single-argument print used for every message; 00042e0f is exit; 00043268 is int386 - it reserves a 12-byte segment-register block, fills it via 0004df22 and forwards intno/in/out plus that block to int386x at 00043657, and both call sites here pass intno 0x10 with a local union REGS whose ax field is set to 0x13 then 3, i.e. the VGA mode-13h enter/exit pair. Data touched: 00069d54 (set to -1), 000643e8 (destination of the third Disk.no token), 000643eb (quit flag polled by the loop), 00069cf0 / 00069cdc / 00069da0 (state and request-code globals), 00069cf4 indexing the function-pointer table at 00060304.
open_question: The quit flag at 000643eb sits three bytes after the buffer at 000643e8 that receives the third "%s" token scanned from Disk.no. Whether these are two independent globals or the flag is byte 3 of a small buffer could not be settled from this function alone; at runtime it does not matter, because the flag is explicitly zeroed after the file is read, but it needs deciding before the buffer gets a declared size in the rebuilt source. Also unresolved: what the three whitespace-separated tokens in the Disk.no file mean and why only the third is kept.

name: fdps_vfs_load_file_or_exit
role: Loads a named file through the VFS into the caller's buffer, stores the resulting pointer through an out parameter, and terminates the program if the load failed.
plate_comment:
Fatal-on-failure wrapper around fdps_vfs_load_file.

Algorithm: Calls fdps_vfs_load_file(name, dest) with the file name and destination buffer taken from its stack arguments and writes the returned pointer through the out parameter. If the returned pointer is NULL the routine calls the shutdown/cleanup helper at 000567a0 and then crt_exit(1), so control never comes back on a failed load. On success it simply returns; the loaded pointer is only visible through *out.

Parameters: dest - destination buffer handed to the VFS loader (may be the caller's preallocated storage); name - NUL-terminated file name looked up by the VFS; out - address of the caller's pointer variable that receives the load result.

Returns: nothing. On failure the function does not return, it exits the process with status 1.
evidence: The whole body is a three-argument stack frame (args read from [EBP+0x14], [EBP+0x18], [EBP+0x1C] after PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP; RET with no immediate, so the caller cleans the stack -> __cdecl, and the inner call itself uses PUSH/PUSH/ADD ESP,8). It pushes those two arguments into the already-named fdps_vfs_load_file at 00039BD0, stores EAX through the third argument, and on a zero result calls 000567A0 followed by crt_exit(1). That places it in the game's own file_io layer (fdps_ pool), not the CRT: it contains no allocation or stdio logic of its own, only the VFS call plus the fatal-error path. Its four callers are all resource/table loading sites (fdps_load_data_tables at 00018930 among them), which matches a load-or-die helper.
open_question: The exact meaning of the first argument (dest) is inferred from fdps_vfs_load_file's existing signature (void *) and not verified at a call site; it could be a preallocated buffer or a size/mode word. The role of the cleanup callee 000567A0 before exit (likely video-mode restore or resource teardown) is not yet established.

name: fdps_shutdown_free_resources
role: Program-exit teardown: frees every globally held allocation (18 unconditional buffers, 7 null-guarded ones and three parallel pointer arrays of DAT_00069cdc entries) and then calls two further shutdown routines.
plate_comment:
Program-exit teardown for all globally held allocations.

Algorithm: Calls the CRT free helper at 0003d478 on 18 global pointers unconditionally (DAT_00064108 and the block DAT_000643a0..DAT_000643e4), then on 7 more global pointers only when they are non-NULL (DAT_00060120, DAT_00060124, DAT_00060138, DAT_0006013c, DAT_00060144, DAT_00060148, DAT_00069cd8). It then walks i = 0 .. DAT_00069cdc-1 and for each index frees the corresponding dword of three parallel pointer arrays based at 0x00069cb0, 0x00069c20 and 0x00069c98. Finally it calls the subsystem teardown at 00018a20 and the library teardown at 00056818, then returns normally.

Parameters: none.

Returns: void.
evidence: Prologue PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP + MOV EBP,ESP and epilogue MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP / POP EDI / POP ESI / POP EBX is the documented -4s stack-convention shape from rebuild_info/build_flags.md, so __cdecl. The body is a flat sequence of 'PUSH dword ptr [global]; CALL 0003d478; ADD ESP,4' with no use of a return value; 0003d478 has ~96 callers spread over the whole game segment and into the library range (0003ca22, 0004299a, 000556a9, 0005600f), which is the signature of the CRT free. Freeing pointers that are only conditionally allocated behind explicit NULL tests, plus the parallel-array sweep bounded by a count global, is textbook release-everything cleanup. The function is called from exactly one place, main @ 00029220, which places it on the program-exit path rather than in any per-frame or per-level path, hence the fdps_ pool and the lifecycle subsystem.
open_question: Which subsystem each freed global belongs to is not established here; the three parallel arrays at 0x00069c20 / 0x00069c98 / 0x00069cb0 with count 0x00069cdc look like one resource table with three fields per entry but that is unconfirmed. The final callee 00056818 sits in the library address range and may be a CRT exit or an AIL shutdown rather than game code, so it was left out of walk_next.

name: fdps_load_global_resources
role: One-shot startup routine called from main that opens Misc.vfs and Field.vfs, caches pointers to every globally used palette, cel, font and text entry, builds the two Bar/EasyBar strip buffers, and either loads or generates-and-writes the palette merge tables Mer1.tmp/Mer2.tmp and FMer1.tmp/FMer2.tmp.
plate_comment:
Loads all globally shared game resources at startup.

Algorithm:
1. Initializes the byte/dword configuration block at 0x6403c-0x6404f (0x10, 0x10, 1, 1, 0x20, 0, 0x10, 0x12), calls the subsystem init at 0x567f0 and allocates a 0xa00 byte scratch buffer into the global at 0x64108.
2. Opens the archive "Misc.vfs" (0x60128). On failure it prints "file not found : Misc.vfs" and exits with status 1.
3. For each of the following entries it looks the name up in the archive and stores the resulting pointer in a global; a NULL result calls the error reporter at 0x567a0 and exits with status 1:
   Fde.pal -> 0x643bc, Fight.pal -> 0x643e4, Cusor.cel -> 0x643b8, Command.cel -> 0x643ac, Shadow.cel -> 0x643dc, IconSts.cel -> 0x643d4, Message.cel -> 0x643d0, Number.cel -> 0x643d8, SelBar.cel -> 0x643c0, LevUp.cel -> 0x643b0, BaseWav.vfs -> 0x643a0, BaseAni.vfs -> 0x643a8, ADWin.cel -> 0x643e0.
4. Loads EasyBar.cel into a temporary, allocates 0x306 bytes into the global at 0x643b4, zero-fills it and copies its first three sub-images (0x2b x 6, stride 0x102) into that buffer, then frees the temporary.
5. Loads Bar.cel the same way into a 0xaf8 byte buffer at 0x643c8, copying three sub-images of 0x75 x 8 with stride 0x3a8, then frees the temporary and closes Misc.vfs.
6. Opens the archive "Field.vfs" ("file not found : field.vfs" plus exit 1 on failure), takes Fdetxt.fon -> 0x643cc and Fdetxt00.txt -> 0x643c4, then closes it.
7. Tests for the cached file "FMer1.tmp". If the cache is absent it reads Mer1.tmp (0x4800 bytes into 0x653f0) and Mer2.tmp (0x1000 bytes into 0x643f0) in mode "rb". If the test reports otherwise it builds the tables from Fight.pal and Fde.pal via the routine at 0x2af60 and writes FMer1.tmp/FMer2.tmp and Mer1.tmp/Mer2.tmp in mode "wb" from the same two buffers.

Parameters: none.

Returns: nothing. Does not return on any resource failure; it exits the process with status 1.
evidence: Every callee is invoked with PUSH arguments followed by ADD ESP,n and the prologue is the standard four-push game-module shape, i.e. the -4s stack convention documented in rebuild_info/build_flags.md; the function itself reads no stack parameters, so its own signature is void(void). The purpose is settled by the string references it passes to the archive lookup at 0x39bd0: Fde.pal, Fight.pal, Cusor.cel, Command.cel, Shadow.cel, IconSts.cel, Message.cel, Number.cel, SelBar.cel, LevUp.cel, BaseWav.vfs, BaseAni.vfs, ADWin.cel, EasyBar.cel, Bar.cel out of Misc.vfs, and Fdetxt.fon plus Fdetxt00.txt out of Field.vfs, with the error paths printing "file not found : Misc.vfs" / "file not found : field.vfs" and calling crt_exit(1). The tail block references the raw byte strings FMer1.tmp, FMer2.tmp, Mer1.tmp, Mer2.tmp with the mode literals "rb" (0x61df4) and "wb" (0x61dcc), confirming a cached-table load/generate pair over the fixed buffers at 0x653f0 (0x4800) and 0x643f0 (0x1000). It is called exactly once, from main at 0x29220, which fixes it as startup rather than a reusable loader. Pool fdps: it lives in the game segment below 0x3b000 and all its CRT work is delegated to the 0x3d000/0x42000 helpers.
open_question: The exact semantics of the file test at 0x42438 (presumed access-style, returning 0 when FMer1.tmp exists) was not verified, so the read branch and write branch could be swapped. The routine at 0x2af60 that produces the 0x4800 and 0x1000 byte tables from a palette is assumed to be a colour-blend/translucency table builder but was not read.

name: fdps_vfs_load_entry
role: Loads a named entry out of a VFS archive into a freshly allocated memory block and returns it, aborting the program with an error message if either the archive or the entry cannot be read.
plate_comment:
Loads one named entry from a VFS archive into newly allocated memory.

Algorithm:
1. Calls the VFS directory loader at 0x00039ab0 with the archive path (first stack argument). The returned pointer is the in-memory directory table whose entries are 0x1a bytes wide (size at +0x1e, file offset at +0x27, as used by 0x00039bd0).
2. If the directory pointer is NULL, prints "file not found: '%s'" (format string at 0x00061df8) with the archive path and terminates via exit(1).
3. Copies the directory pointer, the entry name and the address of a local result slot into a small stack block and re-loads them - the shape of an inlined helper - then calls the VFS entry reader at 0x00039bd0 with (entry name, directory table). That callee locates the entry by name, opens the backing VFS file, allocates a block of the recorded size, seeks to the recorded offset and reads the entry in. Its return value (the allocated block, or NULL) is stored into the local result slot.
4. If the result is NULL, calls 0x000567a0 and terminates via exit(1).
5. Frees / closes the directory table via 0x0003d478 and returns the allocated block.

Parameters:
  vfs_path   - path of the VFS archive file whose directory is loaded; also the value printed in the "file not found" message.
  entry_name - name of the entry inside that archive to extract.

Returns:
  Pointer to the newly allocated buffer holding the entry's bytes. The function never returns on failure; it exits the process instead. The caller owns the returned block.
evidence: Both arguments arrive on the stack ([EBP+0x14], [EBP+0x18], with EBP+0x10 holding the return address after PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP) and the function returns with a plain RET while every internal call is followed by ADD ESP,n - caller-cleaned stack arguments, i.e. __cdecl rather than Watcom's register default. The first argument is passed to 0x00039ab0 and, on a NULL result, printed through 0x00042deb with the format string at 0x00061df8 ("file not found: '%s'") before crt_exit(1). The second callee 0x00039bd0 is unambiguously the VFS reader: it references "Can't find the string: %s", "Can't open the source VFS file..." and "Can't allocate memory for VFS fi...", indexes a directory table with stride 0x1a (size at +0x1e, offset at +0x27), allocates, seeks and reads. That pins this function as the caller-facing wrapper: open archive directory, extract one named entry, release the directory, return the buffer. It is game code, not CRT or Miles - 30 distinct callers spread across title screen, village phase, game over and many battle/menu functions, which is exactly the profile of the project's generic asset loader.
open_question: Callee 0x000567a0, invoked only on the allocation/read-failure path just before exit(1), decompiles to a nonsensical spin over two adjacent bytes at 0x00070019/0x0007001d and is probably mis-analysed; its real purpose (likely an error report or screen restore) is unresolved. Also unverified whether the second argument is strictly an entry name string or can be an index/handle for some callers.

name: fdps_play_sfx
role: Looks up a named digital sound sample in the globally loaded sound pack and, if present, hands it to the sample playback helper with default volume and pan.
plate_comment:
Play a sound effect by resource name.

Algorithm:
  1. Call the sound pack directory lookup at 00039cf0 with the pack base held
     in the global at 000643a0, the caller supplied name, and the address of a
     local dword that receives the entry size. The lookup walks fixed 26 byte
     directory entries, compares the entry name against the caller name and
     returns pack_base + entry_data_offset, or 0 when the name is absent.
  2. If the lookup returned a non-null pointer, call the sample playback
     helper at 00030a00 with (sample, 1, -1, -1). That helper scans the eight
     AIL sample voices for one whose status is not the playing status, then
     initialises and starts the sample on it. The two -1 arguments select the
     default volume and pan path.
  3. A missing name is silently ignored; no sound is played and nothing is
     reported.

Parameters:
  name - NUL terminated resource name of the sample inside the loaded sound
         pack.

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX on exit is leftover from the last call and is not a result.
evidence: Single stack parameter read at [EBP+0x14] with plain RET and caller-side ADD ESP cleanup at every call site, so the convention is stack based caller cleanup. The first callee 00039cf0 is a resource pack directory search: it copies an 11 byte header from the pack base, iterates entry_count entries of 0x1a bytes each, extracts a 13 byte name field, compares it against the caller supplied string, and on match returns pack_base + entry offset while storing the entry size through the third argument. The pack base comes from the global at 000643a0, which is zero in the image and therefore filled at load time. The second callee 00030a00 is unmistakably a Miles AIL sample dispatcher: it checks two audio-enabled flag bytes at 00069d70/00069d71, scans eight voice slots comparing a status query against the constant 4 (sample playing), then calls a run of library routines in the 0003ee00-0003f500 range corresponding to init sample, set sample address, set sample volume, pan, loop count and start sample. A wrapper that resolves a name in the sound pack and starts a one-shot sample on a free voice is a sound effect trigger. The 24 callers spread across battle, menu and village code match a general purpose SFX entry point rather than music, which would use sequence rather than sample calls.
open_question: The exact meaning of the constant 1 passed as the second argument to 00030a00 (loop count versus a sample type or priority selector) was not settled, and the name string constants passed by callers were not inspected, so the pack could in principle hold voice clips rather than short effects.

name: fdps_title_screen
role: Runs the whole opening attract cycle: plays the Logo.saf company/title animation, then shows the 4-entry title menu (StBoard/StSel art, FD%d music), and dispatches the player's choice, returning the selected index to main.
plate_comment:
Title screen and opening attract loop; the only caller is main.

Algorithm:
1. Reset the input/keyboard state, set the global 'in title screen' flag at 0x60159 and clear 0x64110.
2. Try to open the save file "FDE.SAV" ("rb") with the stdio wrappers, read 0x59cb bytes into a malloc'd buffer, close it, then compute a checksum over the buffer and compare it against the dword stored at buffer+0x59c7. If the checksum matches and the byte at buffer+0x30c5 is not 0xff, clear menu-state entries 1 and 2 of the local 4-byte menu flag array (initialised from the dword at 0x29210, where 0 means selectable and 2 means greyed out), i.e. enable the save-dependent menu entries.
3. Outer attract loop, repeated until a menu entry has been chosen: load "Dynasty.pal" from MISC.VFS, allocate a 0x16480 byte animation buffer and load "Logo.saf"; play the animation frame by frame, blitting the frame at offset 0x2298 to 0xa0000 (320x200, source pitch 0x170) after waiting on the VGA vertical retrace bit of port 0x3da and on the timer tick counter at 0x69d64. Any key with scancode < 0x80 aborts the animation.
4. Format "FD%d" with the alternating track index and start that music track, then enter the title menu loop: load "StSel.cel", "StBoard.cel" and "StBoard.pal" from MISC.VFS, allocate a 64000 byte offscreen buffer, and run a menu frame loop with a 0x6d6 tick idle counter. Up (0x48) and Down (0x50) move the selection modulo 4; Enter (0x1c) or Space (0x39) accepts, but only when the selected entry's flag byte is 0. Each frame clears the offscreen buffer, draws the board cel, draws the four selection cels using frame index i*3 + (i == selection ? 1 : flags[i]) at y = 0x48 + i*0x11, waits for retrace and copies the buffer to 0xa0000.
5. On exit from the menu loop, fade the palette to black over 10 retrace-synchronised steps, clear video memory, free all buffers and reset the palette. If the idle counter did not reach zero, dispatch on the selection: 0 starts a new game through the state-machine function pointer table at 0x60074 (index 0x69cf4), 1 opens the load-game screen and, on success, runs the post-load entry, 2 runs the other save-dependent entry, and 3 sets the quit flag at 0x643eb. If the idle counter did reach zero the demo/attract routine runs instead and the whole cycle repeats with the other music track.

Parameters: none.

Returns: the index of the title menu entry that was finally chosen (0-3).
evidence: String and data evidence is decisive: the function references "FDE.SAV", "MISC.VFS", "Dynasty.pal", "Logo.saf", "FD%d", "StSel.cel", "StBoard.cel" and "StBoard.pal" (bytes read at 0x61df4-0x61e70), i.e. exactly the opening-animation and start-screen assets. The control flow matches a title screen: VGA retrace polling on port 0x3da, timer tick wait on 0x69d64, arrow-key scancodes 0x48/0x50 wrapping a selection modulo 4, Enter/Space (0x1c/0x39) accepting only when the selection's flag byte is 0, and an idle counter that falls through to a demo routine. Its only caller is main at 0x29220. Pool is fdps: it is game logic that calls the CRT wrappers rather than being one. Convention is the binary-wide stack convention (-4s per rebuild_info/build_flags.md): standard four-push prologue, no register arguments used, and every call site pushes arguments and cleans up with ADD ESP.
open_question: Which concrete menu entries indices 2 and 3 are was not settled from this function alone: index 2 calls 00023e20 and index 3 only sets the quit flag at 0x643eb. Index 2 being greyed out until a valid FDE.SAV exists suggests a save-dependent mode, but its identity needs 00023e20 to be walked. Ghidra's decompiled signature (param_1, param_2, unaff_EBX) is invented; the disassembly reads no incoming registers or stack arguments.

name: fdps_show_game_over
role: Presents the Game Over screen: loads "GameOver.saf" from MISC.VFS, shows it until the player presses a key, fades the screen out over 16 steps, frees its buffers and hands control to the program termination stubs.
plate_comment:
Game Over screen sequence.

Algorithm:
1. Allocates a 64000-byte (320x200) buffer and copies the current VGA frame at 0xA0000 into it, so the screen the player was looking at can be redrawn.
2. Loads the resource "GameOver.saf" (0x61e68) out of the archive "MISC.VFS" (0x60128) via the VFS loader at 0002a140, and allocates a 0x16480-byte working surface whose pixel area begins at offset 0x2298.
3. Fills a 0x50-byte on-stack descriptor (pitch 0x170, 0xf8, 0x18, 0x18, plus the loaded resource pointer) and loops: blit the saved frame into the work surface, run the draw call at 00014140, wait for VGA vertical retrace by polling port 0x3DA (bit 3) low then high, blit the work surface to 0xA0000, wait for the timer tick counter at 00069d64 to advance, and poll the input routine at 00014550. The loop ends when input returns non-zero.
4. Runs a 16-step fade: for each step i the fade blit at 00030010 is called with the two 4 KB lookup tables at 000653f0 / 000643f0 and level 0x6f, the descriptor is redrawn twice (once with the table pair, once with mode 0x1f), and each step is again paced by retrace and by the tick counter.
5. Frees the work surface, the loaded resource and the saved frame, then calls 000567b3 and 000567a0, which are the program termination stubs.

Parameters: none.

Returns: nothing. The trailing RET is present but is not expected to be reached, because the two calls that precede it terminate the program.
evidence: Two string references settle the purpose: 0x60128 is "MISC.VFS" and 0x61e68 is "GameOver.saf", passed together to the VFS resource loader at 0002a140. The rest is textbook full-screen presentation code for this engine: 64000-byte buffer, memcpy to/from the VGA aperture at 0xA0000, port 0x3DA retrace polling, tick counter at 00069d64, a 320x200 (0x140 x 0xc8) rect blit through 0002f2f0, and a 16-iteration fade through 00030010 with the two 4 KB tables at 000643f0/000653f0. It is called from exactly one place, main at 00029220, and it ends by calling two stubs at 000567b3/000567a0 with no cleanup afterwards, matching a terminal end-of-game path. Pool is fdps: it references game resources by name and contains no CRT or AIL idiom of its own; malloc/free/memcpy/inp are all reached by call. Convention is __cdecl per the project-wide -4s stack default; every call it makes pushes arguments and cleans up with ADD ESP.
open_question: The identity of 000567b3 and 000567a0 is inferred from position (top of the CRT range, called last, nothing after them) rather than read; if they turn out to be exit/_dos_exit then no_return should become true. Also unverified: whether the loop at 00014140 draws a menu with selectable entries or only static artwork, and what mode value 0x1f versus the table pair means to it.

name: fdps_title_demo
role: Runs the title screen's attract-mode demo: loads twelve resource sets, primes twelve unit slots with fixed demo stats, plays a two-pass per-unit animation loop that any keypress aborts, then blanks the VGA frame buffer and returns.
plate_comment:
Title screen attract-mode demo sequence.

Algorithm:
1. Sets three globals: DAT_00069cf4 = 0x19, DAT_00060159 = 0 (demo-active flag), DAT_00064114 = 0.
2. Calls the loader at 00023bc0 twelve times with ids 0,1,8,9,2,10,3,11,4,12,5,6, then calls 00022750 once and clears DAT_00069cd0.
3. Fetches record 3 via the table accessor at 0002d210 and stores 4 into its byte at offset 0; calls 00036b60(0,0x0b,0) and 000282b0 twice (1,0x27) and (4,0x0b).
4. For slots 0..11 fetches the record via 0002d210 and writes byte[6]=1, word[0x40]=word[0x42]=2000, word[0x44]=word[0x46]=word[0x48]=800, word[0x4c]=400 -- a canned set of demo values so nothing in the demo can be knocked out.
5. Flushes the keyboard ring buffer via the stub at 000567b3 (write index := read index), then runs an outer pass counter initialised to 2. Each pass walks i = 0 .. DAT_00060150-1: record = 0002d210(i); if 000109b0(i) returns 0, calls 00010010(i, record->byte[6]); when i == 0x0c it calls the frame routine 0002db50. After each unit it polls the key stub at 000567be, which returns 0xff when the 10-entry ring at 0x0007000f is empty; any value below 0x7f is a real keypress, which forces the pass counter to 1 and breaks out. Each pass ends with 0002db50 and decrements the counter.
6. On exit calls 0003d478(DAT_00064108), clears DAT_00064114, sets DAT_00060159 = 1, blanks 64000 bytes at 0x000a0000 (mode 13h frame buffer) via the fill routine at 00042cd0, and flushes the key buffer again.

Parameters: none. The stack frame is PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP, MOV EBP,ESP, SUB ESP,0x0c with three locals and no read above the frame pointer.

Returns: nothing.
evidence: Only caller is fdps_title_screen @ 0002a2b0, so this is a title-screen sub-mode, not a gameplay routine. The body is unmistakably an attract loop: a fixed repeat count of 2, a per-frame poll of the keyboard ring stub at 000567be that aborts on any real key, and a final memset of 64000 bytes at 0x000a0000 -- exactly the mode 13h frame buffer -- to blank the screen on the way out. The two tiny stubs were decoded from raw bytes: 000567b3 is 'MOV EAX,[0x00070019]; MOV [0x0007001d],EAX; RET' (buffer flush) and 000567be returns 0xff when read index == write index, otherwise reads byte[0x0007000f + index] and advances the index modulo 10 -- a 10-entry keyboard ring, which is why 0xff means 'no key' and < 0x7f means 'key pressed'. The bulk setup of twelve slots with identical oversized field values (2000/2000, 800/800/800, 400) is canned demo state, not gameplay state. Pool is fdps: it touches game globals and the game's own table accessor 0002d210, references no CRT string or AIL entry point, and has no import-style behaviour. Convention: every call site pushes arguments and cleans with ADD ESP,n, matching the binary-wide stack convention (-4s) recorded in rebuild_info/build_flags.md; this function itself reads nothing above EBP, so it takes no arguments.
open_question: What the twelve records reached through 0002d210 actually are is not settled -- fields 0x40..0x4c read like hp/max plus three 800s and a 400, which fits a unit stat block, but they could equally be animation timers. Whether the demo is a scripted battle, a character parade or an opening animation cannot be decided without walking 00010010 and 00023bc0. The meaning of DAT_00069cf4 = 0x19 and of the ids passed to 00023bc0 is also unknown.

name: fdps_build_palette_tables
role: Builds the global palette helper tables from a 256-entry VGA palette: an 18-level brightness ramp table of packed 4-4-4 colours and a 16x16x16 RGB-to-palette-index lookup cube.
plate_comment:
Builds the global palette helper tables used by the shading and colour-matching code.

Algorithm:
1. Copies the 18-entry brightness coefficient table at 0002ae40 onto the stack. The coefficients are {0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,16,15,14,13,12,11,10,9,8}, indexed by shade level.
2. For each of the 256 palette entries: reads the three bytes (r,g,b) of the source palette (each a 6-bit VGA component, scaled by 4 to 8 bits), packs them as r<<16|g<<8|b, then calls the three component extractors (0002ae90 red, 0002aec0 green, 0002aef0 blue). Each component is masked with 0xF0 and repositioned so the result holds the high nibble of red in bits 16-19, green in bits 8-11 and blue in bits 0-3. Level row 0 of the ramp table (000653f0) is zeroed (black) and this packed value is stored into level row 1 (000657f0, i.e. 000653f0 + 0x400).
3. For levels 2..17, each of the 256 packed row-1 values is multiplied by the level coefficient and stored at 000653f0[level*256 + index]. Because each channel occupies only the low nibble of its own byte, a multiply by up to 16 scales all three channels at once without carrying between them.
4. Fills the 16x16x16 inverse lookup cube at 000643f0: for every (r,g,b) triple of 4-bit components (passed as component*4) it calls the nearest-colour matcher at 0002b1b0 with the source palette and stores the returned palette index as a byte, written sequentially over 4096 entries.

Parameters:
  palette - pointer to 256 packed 3-byte RGB entries (VGA 6-bit components) in r,g,b order.

Returns:
  Nothing meaningful. EAX holds a leftover loop counter; the decompiler models it as an int return but no caller uses it.
evidence: The disassembly reads the argument as a 256-entry stride-3 byte table (LEA EAX,[EAX+EAX*2]; ADD EAX,[EBP+0x14]; three byte loads at +0,+1,+2), which is exactly a VGA 768-byte palette. Each component is scaled by 4 (6-bit to 8-bit VGA) and repacked as nibbles so that the later multiply by the coefficient table at 0002ae40 (values 0..16) cannot carry between channels: a brightness/fade ramp of 18 levels written to 000653f0 (18*256 dwords, 000657f0 is level row 1 of the same table). The final triple 16x16x16 loop calls 0002b1b0 with (b*4, r*4, g*4-style component arguments plus the palette pointer) and stores the byte result sequentially into 000643f0, a 4096-byte RGB-to-index inverse lookup cube; 000643f0 + 0x1000 == 000653f0, so the two tables are adjacent globals. Only caller is fdps_load_global_resources @ 00029660, i.e. one-time setup, which matches table construction. Game-owned graphics logic, no CRT or AIL signature, hence pool fdps. The single argument arrives on the stack at [EBP+0x14] and every call it makes is followed by an ADD ESP fixup, so this module uses stack-based, caller-cleaned calls: __cdecl.
open_question: The exact semantics of the 18 shade levels (why level 9 uses coefficient 16 and levels 10..17 ramp back down to 8) is not settled here; it needs the consumers of 000653f0 to be read.

name: fdps_palette_find_nearest_color
role: Scans a 256-entry 3-byte RGB palette and returns the index of the entry with the smallest squared Euclidean distance to the given r/g/b triple.
plate_comment:
Finds the palette index whose RGB triple is closest to a requested color.

Algorithm: keeps a running best squared distance seeded with 10000000 and a running best index seeded with 0x100. Walks a fixed 256 iterations over the palette, consuming three consecutive bytes per entry (red, green, blue in that order) through an advancing byte cursor. For each entry it forms dr = r - pal[0], dg = g - pal[1], db = b - pal[2] and computes dr*dr + dg*dg + db*db as signed 32-bit arithmetic. If that sum is strictly less than the current best it becomes the new best and the loop counter becomes the new best index. The loop count is hardcoded to 256 and is not derived from any argument, so the palette buffer must hold at least 768 bytes. The strict less-than test makes the first of several equally close entries win. The 0x100 seed can never survive because the maximum possible distance is 3*255*255 = 195075, well below the 10000000 seed, so the function always returns a value in 0..255.

Parameters: r, g, b are the target color components, passed as full 32-bit ints and only compared as such (the palette bytes are zero-extended, the targets are not masked). palette points at the first byte of a 256-entry, 3-bytes-per-entry RGB table.

Returns: the 0..255 index of the closest palette entry.
prototype: int fdps_palette_find_nearest_color(int r, int g, int b, unsigned char *palette)
evidence: The body is unambiguous: a 256-iteration loop over a cursor advanced by 3 bytes per step, computing dr*dr + dg*dg + db*db against three separate stack arguments and tracking the minimum plus its index. That is the textbook nearest-color palette lookup and nothing else. The sole caller is fdps_build_palette_tables at 0002af60, which is exactly the consumer such a helper has, so pool fdps / subsystem graphics is settled by both the body and the call site. Convention: after PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP and MOV EBP,ESP the frame puts the return address at [EBP+0x10], so [EBP+0x14], [EBP+0x18], [EBP+0x1c] and [EBP+0x20] are four incoming stack arguments; no argument arrives in a register, and the function ends in a plain RET with no immediate, leaving the caller to pop them. That is caller-cleanup stack passing, i.e. __cdecl, not the register-based __watcall default.
open_question: Whether the three color arguments are always already in 0..255 at every call site. The function never masks them, so an out-of-range value would still produce a valid index but a mathematically meaningless one; that can only be settled from fdps_build_palette_tables, which this ticket does not cover.

name: fdps_map_cursor_select_loop
role: Runs the interactive map-cursor loop: reads the keyboard scancode each frame, moves and scrolls the tile cursor, cycles through a caller-supplied candidate unit list, and returns whether the player confirmed (1) or cancelled (-1) a selection under the given selection mode.
plate_comment:
Interactive battle-map cursor / target selection loop.

Algorithm:
Reads the map dimensions from the header at 0x00060144 (tile width at +0, tile height at +2) and converts them to pixel extents by multiplying by the 0x18 tile size. When mode == 6 the candidate list length is stashed and then forced to zero, so list cycling is disabled in that mode. If a candidate list is supplied and the first candidate's unit record byte at +7 is not 'y', the cursor is snapped onto that candidate via fdps_map_cursor_move_to using its tile coordinates from unit record bytes +0 and +1 (unit records are 0x50 bytes, base pointer at 0x00069cd8).
FUN_00056799 yields the pointer to the current keyboard scancode byte; it is reset to 0xFF before the loop and after a cancel. Each iteration calls fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll, then reads the scancode:
  0x01 (Esc) / 0x53 (Del)  -> result = -1, loop ends
  0x39 (Space) / 0x1C (Enter) -> confirm. In mode 6 the whole unit array (count at 0x00060150) is scanned for a unit standing on the cursor tile that fails FUN_000109b0; if none blocks, FUN_00018b70 and FUN_0002ba00 are consulted and the tile cost byte read through 0x00069d09 must be below 0x14 for the confirm to succeed (returns 1). Outside mode 6, mode 5 confirms nothing; otherwise FUN_0002ba00 resolves the tile under the cursor and the resolved index at 0x00069d0c must not be 0xFF; mode 4 then returns 1 directly, other modes call FUN_000109f0 with the cursor tile, the clamped value of 0x00069cd0 and the mode, and set the result to 1 when it accepts.
  0x2C (Z) / 0x4C (numpad 5) -> advance to the next entry of the candidate list (wrapping) and snap the cursor to that unit.
  0x48/0x50/0x4B/0x4D (arrows) -> move the cursor one tile (0x18 pixels) in Y (0x00069ccc) or X (0x00069cd4), clamped to the map extents, each move playing "Beep.wav" through FUN_0002a1f0. A repeat counter suppresses movement while the same scancode has been held for 1..5 iterations, giving the usual key-repeat delay.
After key handling the view origin (0x00069ce0 for Y, 0x00069ce4 for X) is scrolled by whole tiles so the cursor stays inside the visible window, and fdps_render_view_frame redraws.

Parameters:
  mode  - selection mode; 4, 5 and 6 take special confirm paths, other values are passed on to FUN_000109f0
  count - number of entries in the candidate list; 0 disables list cycling, and mode 6 forces it to 0 after saving it as the acting unit index
  list  - array of unit indices to cycle through with the cycle key

Returns:
  1 when the player confirmed a valid selection, -1 when the player cancelled. Selected tile coordinates are left in the cursor globals 0x00069cd4 (X) and 0x00069ccc (Y).
prototype: int fdps_map_cursor_select_loop(int mode, int count, unsigned char *list)
