The error string is game-authored text (same block as other in-game messages), and the wrapper itself is not library code, so the pool is fdps while the three timer primitives it calls belong to the vendor sound library. Convention is __cdecl: the sole parameter is read from [EBP+0x14] (stack slot above the return address and the four saved registers) and the function returns with a bare RET, leaving argument cleanup to the caller.
open_question: The exact vendor identities of FUN_0003e196 / FUN_0003e3ea / FUN_0003e5b3 (most plausibly the AIL register-timer, set-timer-rate and start-timer entry points) were not confirmed here - they belong to the ail-pool ticket. It is therefore also unsettled whether the rate argument is a frequency in Hz or a period in microseconds.

name: fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll
role: Per-frame poll that, once every 75 timer ticks, checks whether the current CD audio track has stopped and restarts it so background music keeps looping.
plate_comment:
Periodic CD background-music keep-alive, polled from the game loops.

Algorithm:
  Compares the cached tick value at 0x00069d74 with the live timer tick at
  0x00069d64 and returns immediately when they are equal, so the body runs at
  most once per timer tick regardless of how often the caller polls.
  On a new tick it increments the tick accumulator at 0x00060170. When the
  accumulator reaches 0x4b (75 ticks) it performs the actual check: if a track
  is selected (0x00069d54 != -1) and the CD audio enable flag at 0x00060008 is
  non-zero, it queries playback state via FUN_0003c6e8; a non-zero 16-bit
  result means the track is no longer playing, in which case FUN_0003c85b is
  called with (track index + 1) to start the track again. The accumulator is
  then reset to zero. Finally the cached tick is refreshed from the live tick.
  The selected-track global holds a zero-based index; the play routine takes a
  one-based CD track number, hence the +1.

Parameters:
  None. All state is read from and written to globals.

Returns:
  Nothing.
evidence: The function takes no arguments (the prologue pushes EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP, sets up EBP and subtracts 0 from ESP; no parameter register or stack slot is read) and touches only globals, so it is __watcall void(void); the decompiler's param_1/param_2/unaff_EBX are invented. Its only two callees are FUN_0003c6e8 and FUN_0003c85b; FUN_0003c85b sits in the CD block and itself calls the already-identified fdps_cd_stop_audio (0003c4a7) before starting playback, which pins this whole cluster to the CD-audio subsystem and makes FUN_0003c85b a start-track routine. The argument passed to it is DAT_00069d54 + 1, the classic zero-based-index to one-based-CD-track conversion. FUN_0003c6e8 is called with no arguments and only its AX result is tested, i.e. a playback-state query. The 0x00069d74 vs 0x00069d64 compare-then-copy is a once-per-tick edge gate, and 0x00060170 is a tick accumulator that fires every 75 ticks (about 4 s at the 18.2 Hz DOS tick). Eight callers, all game loops including fdps_battle_player_phase_loop and the various screen loops, which is exactly the call pattern of a background-music keep-alive rather than a one-shot. Pool is fdps: the address lies in the game's own code range and the routine encodes game policy (repeat the current track), not vendor library or CRT behaviour.
open_question: The exact polarity of FUN_0003c6e8's AX result is inferred, not proven: it is read here as 'non-zero means playback has ended'. The identity of the two tick globals (0x00069d64 as the live timer tick, 0x00069d74 as this routine's cached copy) is likewise inferred from the compare-then-copy shape; whichever ticket names the timer ISR should confirm it.

name: fdps_cd_verify_disc_and_play_track
role: Blocks until the CD-ROM holding the requested chapter is inserted, then starts that chapter's CD audio track from a 30x2 track table.
plate_comment:
Verify the correct game CD is inserted for a chapter, then start its CD audio track.

Algorithm:
1. Copy a 60-byte constant table from 000304a0 onto the stack. It is 30 chapter rows of 2 bytes; the row is the chapter, the column is the track slot, and the byte is a zero-based CD audio track index.
2. Stop any playing CD audio (fdps_cd_stop_audio at 0003c4a7).
3. Loop until the inserted disc is acceptable:
   - Uninstall the keyboard ISR (00056818) and drain pending input (00043570 / 00043587).
   - Build "%s\\Pack.vfs" from the CD-ROM root path global at 000643c4 (00042d41) and probe it (00042438). A non-zero result means the archive could not be opened, i.e. no usable disc.
   - On success, load the "Pass.Dat" entry through fdps_vfs_load_entry and take its first byte minus '0' as the disc number (1 or 2).
   - Chapters 0..17 live on disc 1, chapters 18 (0x12) and above on disc 2. If the probe failed, or the disc number does not match the chapter, draw the matching prompt string (message id 0x223 for "insert disc 2", 0x222 for "insert disc 1", followed by id 0x22a) via 0001ff60 at 320x208, wait 20000 ticks (0003d370), tear the prompt down (00020820) and retry.
   - Otherwise set the done flag and leave the loop.
4. Reinstall the keyboard ISR (fdps_install_keyboard_isr).
5. If the CD audio enable flag at 00060008 is clear, store -1 into the current-track global at 00069d54 and stop CD audio. Otherwise read table[chapter * 2 + slot], store it at 00069d54, and start playback of track value + 1 (0003c85b).

Parameters:
  chapter - chapter index, 0..29; also selects the required disc (>= 18 means disc 2).
  slot    - which of the chapter's two track entries to play, 0 or 1.

Returns:
  Nothing. Does not return until an acceptable disc is present.
evidence: The format string at 00061ebc is "%s\\Pack.vfs" and 00061ec8 is "Pass.Dat"; the loaded Pass.Dat byte is converted with SUB EAX,0x30 into a disc number that is compared against 1 and 2, gated on the chapter being below or at/above 0x12. That is a disc-swap check. After the loop the function indexes a 60-byte constant table by chapter*2 + slot and passes value+1 to 0003c85b while the already-named fdps_cd_stop_audio (0003c4a7) is the alternative branch, so 0003c85b is CD track playback and 00069d54 is the current-track global; 00060008 gates it as the CD audio enable flag. The table's first 36 bytes are small values (13,6 / 4,4 / 9,9 / 14,18 ...) consistent with red-book track numbers, and its shape changes character exactly at the row for chapter 18, matching the disc-1/disc-2 split. Callers are chapter/phase level game code (fdps_run_village_phase, fdps_load_savegame), so pool is fdps. Convention is __cdecl: after PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP and MOV EBP,ESP the two arguments are read at [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18], i.e. past the return address at [EBP+0x10], and the epilogue is a plain RET with the caller cleaning the stack; a __watcall function would have taken the first two ints in EAX/EDX.
open_question: Which of the two per-chapter track slots is which situation (e.g. map/village versus battle) is not settled here; it would come from the four callers. The exact meaning of the non-zero return of 00042438 (open failure versus drive-not-ready) is also unconfirmed.

name: fdps_play_movie
role: Plays one full-screen FMV sequence: fades the palette to black, stops CD audio, builds the player/.Vid/.Aud path trio from the base directory and the caller-supplied movie name, runs the playback routine, then blanks VGA memory and restarts audio.
plate_comment:
Plays one full-screen FMV sequence by name.

Algorithm:
1. Calls 0003d8b2 and 00056818 to quiesce the current display/audio state, then spins on 00043570 / 00043587 until the pending playback-side work drains.
2. Calls fdps_cd_stop_audio, then fades the active palette at DAT_000643bc down by (-64,-64,-64) over entries 0..255 via 00022f40.
3. Formats three paths with sprintf (00042d41) into local buffers, all rooted at the base directory string at DAT_000643e8:
     [ebp-0x3c] = "%s\\fd.exe"      (player/module path, no extra argument)
     [ebp-0x28] = "%s\\%s.Vid"      (video stream, second %s = movie_name)
     [ebp-0x14] = "%s\\%s.Aud"      (audio stream, second %s = movie_name)
4. Invokes the playback entry 000435a2 with (0, fd_exe_path, fd_exe_path, vid_path, aud_path, 0).
5. On return, zero-fills 64000 bytes at 0x000a0000 (mode 13h framebuffer) via 00042cd0, re-programs the palette to all-zero through 00022f40, calls 000567f0 to tear down the playback display state, and finally calls fdps_audio_init(0x19) to bring music back up.

Parameters:
  movie_name - pointer to the base name of the movie, substituted for the second %s of both the .Vid and .Aud path templates. Passed on the stack at [ebp+0x14].

Returns:
  Nothing. Returns after the movie has finished and the screen has been cleared.
evidence: The three format strings it references are decisive: 0x61ed4 = "%s\\fd.exe", 0x61ee0 = "%s\\%s.Vid", 0x61eec = "%s\\%s.Aud". All three are formatted with the same base-directory pointer at DAT_000643e8 and the single stack parameter, then handed to 000435a2 together, so the function is the wrapper that turns a movie name into a played .Vid/.Aud pair. The surrounding work confirms the framing: palette fade-out through 00022f40, fdps_cd_stop_audio before playback, a memset of 64000 bytes at 0xa0000 (the mode 13h framebuffer) afterwards, and fdps_audio_init(0x19) to restore audio. Pool is fdps: it touches game globals, VGA memory and the project's own CD/audio routines, and there is no CRT or Miles signature anywhere in it. Callers are fdps_title_screen (0002a2b0) and FUN_0001ba40, i.e. the opening/scene cutscene sites, not a generic utility. Calling convention: the prologue is the standard four-push sequence (push ebx/esi/edi/ebp; mov ebp,esp) and the only parameter is read from [ebp+0x14], with every call site cleaning its own arguments via ADD ESP,n -- rebuild_info/build_flags.md records -4s stack convention as the binary default and this four-push form as its marker, and ebx/esi/edi are saved but never read, which rules out register arguments.
open_question: Whether "fd.exe" is a separate player executable that 000435a2 loads/spawns or merely a data container that happens to carry an .exe name, and what the 0x19 handed to fdps_audio_init selects (music track vs. audio mode) -- both live inside callees, not here.

name: fdps_run_village_phase
role: Runs the between-battle village phase for the current chapter: shows the village hub screen and its five-facility menu loop (or a blank screen for chapters that have no village), then invokes the current chapter's script entry from the per-chapter function pointer table.
plate_comment:
Runs the village phase between chapters.

Algorithm:
1. Poll the background service at 0x000567b3, then bail out immediately with 0 if the global abort flag at 0x000643eb is set.
2. Test the current chapter number at 0x00069cf4. Chapters 16, 17, 21, 22 and 26+ have no village: those call the fade/transition helper at 0x00030bf0 with -1 and, unless the suppress flag at 0x00060131 is set, clear VGA memory at 0xa0000 (64000 bytes), run the palette routine at 0x00022f40 with the palette at 0x000643bc, allocate and clear a 64000-byte offscreen buffer, present it via 0x000241e0 and free it. Control then falls through to step 6.
3. Otherwise set the in-village flag at 0x00060070, load "ShopWin.Cel" from the "MISC_VFS" archive via the resource loader at 0x0002a140, cache the handle in 0x00069d84, run the village setup at 0x00031540 and fade in via 0x00030bf0 with mode 2.
4. Menu loop: allocate a 64000-byte page, load "Village.cel" from "MISC_VFS", blit it to the page at pitch 0x140 via 0x0002dba0, free the background, draw the cursor highlight at the coordinate pair for the current selection (x table at 0x00060174, y table at 0x0006018c) via 0x00031780 with flag 1, run the menu input handler at 0x00031bc0 which updates the selection in place, erase the highlight with flag 0, free the page.
5. Dispatch on the selection through the jump table at 0x00031328: 1 -> 0x00035cc0 (which forces the selection back to 0 for chapters that have no village), 2 -> 0x00035aa0, 3 -> 0x00035860, 4 -> 0x00035fd0, 5 -> 0x00036210. Poll 0x000567b3 and repeat while the selection is non-zero and no abort is pending. On exit free the two cached cel handles, clear the in-village flag at 0x00060070 and the state words at 0x00060150 and 0x00069cd8.
6. Save and clear the input-enable byte at 0x00060158, fade out via 0x00030bf0 with -1, and unless an abort is pending call the chapter script entry taken from the per-chapter function pointer table at 0x00060074 indexed by the chapter number. Restore 0x00060158, clear 0x00060131, and call 0x00030cc0 with the chapter number and 0.

Parameters: none.

Returns: the menu selection left over when the loop exited, which is 0 on a normal exit and 0 when the abort flag was already set on entry.
evidence: The function loads two named resources out of the "MISC_VFS" archive (string at 0x00060128): "ShopWin.Cel" (0x00061ef8) and "Village.cel" (0x00061f04), which fixes this as the village/town screen. It keeps a selection index in a local, draws a cursor at coordinates taken from two parallel six-entry int tables at 0x00060174 (x: 138, 214, 253, 46, 54, 4) and 0x0006018c (y: 0, 74, 151, 135, 49, 160), and dispatches selections 1..5 through a jump table at 0x00031328 to five distinct facility handlers -- the classic Flame Dragon town hub. It is called only from main (0x00029220) and 0x0002a2b0, so it is a top-level phase driver, not a helper. It is game logic (fdps pool): it touches game globals such as the chapter number at 0x00069cf4 and the per-chapter script pointer table at 0x00060074, and contains no CRT or Miles AIL idiom. Calling convention is the binary default stack convention: the prologue is the standard four-push form PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP; MOV EBP,ESP documented for -4s in rebuild_info/build_flags.md, the epilogue is MOV ESP,EBP with a plain RET, and every call site pushes arguments and cleans up with ADD ESP,n. The function itself reads no parameters from [EBP+0x14] or above, so it takes none; Ghidra's param_1/param_2/unaff_EBX in the decompilation are invented.
open_question: The meaning of the five facility handlers (shop, inn, church, etc.) was not checked, and the exact semantics of the flags at 0x00060131, 0x00060150, 0x00060158 and 0x00069cd8 are unsettled. The non-zero return path is unreachable in practice as far as the local reasoning shows, so the return value's contract is unconfirmed.

name: fdps_load_field_chapter_resources
role: Releases the previously loaded field-phase chapter resources and loads the current chapter's text and shop tables out of Field.vfs, then re-reads every roster member's icon from ICON.CEL.
plate_comment:
Loads (and reloads) the per-chapter resources used by the field/village phase.

Algorithm:
1. If the cached chapter text buffer at 0x00060124 is non-NULL, free it.
2. sprintf a name with the format string "fdetxt%02d.txt" at 0x00061f10 using chapter index [0x00069cf4] + 1, load that member out of the archive named by "Field.vfs" (0x000600f8) via FUN_0002a140, and store the returned buffer in 0x00060124.
3. sprintf a name with "Shop%02d.dat" (0x00061f20) using chapter index [0x00069cf4] -- note: no +1 here, unlike the text file -- load it the same way and store the buffer in 0x00069d80.
4. If [0x00060150] is non-zero and the cached roster pointer [0x00069cd8] differs from the live roster base [0x00064108], free the stale roster copy.
5. Snapshot the live roster: [0x00060150] = roster count [0x00064114], [0x00069cd8] = roster base [0x00064108].
6. For i in 0 .. [0x00069cdc)-1, free the three parallel per-entry buffer arrays at 0x00069cb0, 0x00069c20 and 0x00069c98, then reset the entry count [0x00069cdc] to 0.
7. If the flag [0x00069cf0] is set, free the buffer held in [0x00060138] and clear the flag.
8. Open "ICON.CEL" (0x00061f34) in mode "rb" (0x00061f30) via the CRT fopen at 0x0004265e.
9. For each of the [0x00064114] roster records (stride 0x50 bytes from [0x00064108]), read the icon id at record offset +7 and pass it with the open stream to FUN_00023050, which decodes that icon.
10. Close the stream via the CRT fclose at 0x000428be.

Parameters: none. All inputs are globals: the chapter index at 0x00069cf4, the roster base/count at 0x00064108/0x00064114, and the cached-resource slots listed above.

Returns: nothing. The loaded buffers are published through the globals 0x00060124 (chapter text) and 0x00069d80 (shop table).
evidence: Four string literals pin the behaviour: "fdetxt%02d.txt" (0x00061f10) and "Shop%02d.dat" (0x00061f20) are both formatted with the chapter counter at 0x00069cf4 and then passed with "Field.vfs" (0x000600f8) to the archive reader FUN_0002a140, whose result is stored into two long-lived globals; "ICON.CEL" (0x00061f34) is opened with mode "rb" (0x00061f30) and iterated once per roster record. The repeated single-argument calls to FUN_0003d478 on previously stored pointers, each followed by ADD ESP,4, are the free() shape. The array walk uses a 0x50-byte stride over [0x00064108] bounded by [0x00064114], the same roster base/count pair the function snapshots, and reads a byte at record offset +7 as the icon selector. Callers are fdps_run_village_phase (0x00031210) and FUN_00035cc0, i.e. field/village scene entry, so this is game code (fdps pool), not CRT or vendor. Prologue is the standard four-push (EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP) form and every call site pushes arguments and cleans them with ADD ESP,n, matching the binary-wide -4s stack convention documented in rebuild_info/build_flags.md; the unaff_EBX and extra parameters in the decompilation are Ghidra guesses -- EBX is pushed and never read.
open_question: The text file uses chapter index + 1 while the shop file uses the raw index, so the on-disk numbering of fdetxt*.txt and Shop*.dat is offset by one; which of the two matches the chapter number shown in game is unsettled. The identities of the three parallel arrays at 0x00069cb0 / 0x00069c20 / 0x00069c98 and of the buffer at 0x00060138 guarded by the flag 0x00069cf0 were not investigated (out of scope for this ticket).

name: fdps_village_signboard_menu
role: Runs the village signboard (CanBan.cel) menu: loops reading the keyboard, moves a 5-entry selection cursor with the arrow keys, animates the highlight palette in sync with the vertical retrace, blits the composed frame to 0xA0000, and returns when Enter or ESC is pressed.
plate_comment:
Village signboard menu loop.

Algorithm:
1. Copies three 9-byte VGA DAC ramp tables (R at 0x31064, G at 0x3106d, B at 0x31076) into locals; they drive the pulsing highlight colour.
2. Clamps the global scene index at 0x000601a4 against the count at 0x00064114, then loads the signboard cel "CanBan.cel" from the "MISC_VFS" archive (FUN_0002a140). The handle is freed on exit.
3. Each iteration: draws the village backdrop (FUN_00030c50), reads a keyboard scancode (FUN_000567be, masked to 8 bits). Scancodes >= 0x7F are ignored. FUN_000357a0 acts as a hotkey/abort filter: when it returns non-zero the selection is forced to 5 and the selection-change handler FUN_00031f60 runs.
   - 0x4B (left) / 0x48 (up): plays "Beep.wav" (FUN_0002a1f0), selection = (selection + 4) % 5, calls FUN_00031f60.
   - 0x4D (right) / 0x50 (down): plays "Beep.wav", selection = (selection + 1) % 5, calls FUN_00031f60.
   - 0x1C (Enter) / 0x39 (Space): sets the exit flag.
   - 0x0F (Tab): advances the scene index at 0x000601a4 modulo the count at 0x00064114.
4. Picks an animation cell from the frame counter (frame/5 & 3, with 3 folded back to 1), resolves the sprite through the table at 0x00060138 offset by scene index * 0x30, allocates a 64000-byte off-screen page (FUN_0003d375) and fills it with the caller-supplied background image (FUN_0003d514, 320x200).
5. Blits the animated figure (FUN_000568db) at the position given by the x table at 0x00060174 and the y table at 0x0006018C indexed by the current selection, then draws the signboard text twice through FUN_0002dba0 (once for entry 6, once for the current selection, i.e. the highlighted line).
6. Waits for vertical retrace on port 0x3DA (bit 3), then writes DAC entries 0xF0..0xF4 through ports 0x3C8/0x3C9 using the ramp tables phase-shifted by (frame/3) % 5, waits for retrace to end, copies the off-screen page to 0xA0000, spins until the timer tick at 0x00069D64 changes, and frees the page.

Parameters:
  background - pointer to a 64000-byte (320x200) background image copied into the off-screen page every frame.
  selection  - in/out pointer to the current menu selection (0..4, or 5 when the hotkey filter fires); updated in place and read by the caller after return.

Returns:
  Nothing. The cel handle and the off-screen page are released before returning.
evidence: String evidence is decisive: the loop loads "CanBan.cel" (0x61f40) from the archive name "MISC_VFS" (0x60128) and plays "Beep.wav" (0x61f4c) on every cursor move. The only caller is fdps_run_village_phase @ 00031210, placing it in the village/menu subsystem. Arrow-key scancodes 0x48/0x4B/0x4D/0x50 wrap a selection modulo 5, 0x1C/0x39 terminate the loop, and the selection indexes cursor x/y tables at 0x00060174 / 0x0006018C. Ports 0x3DA (retrace), 0x3C8/0x3C9 (DAC write index/data) and the 0xA0000 / 64000-byte page flip are unambiguous mode-13h VGA presentation, so this is game logic (fdps pool), not CRT. Both parameters arrive on the stack at EBP+0x14 and EBP+0x18 with no incoming register arguments and the function returns with a plain RET, so the caller cleans the stack: __cdecl.
open_question: The meaning of selection value 5 and of the predicate FUN_000357a0 (some hotkey/abort filter applied to the scancode) is not settled from this function alone. The frame counter local at EBP-0x24 is read before it is first assigned, so the first frame uses whatever was on the stack; this looks like an original-source defect rather than a decompiler artifact and should be checked against the caller when 00031210 is written.

name: fdps_village_item_menu
role: Village-phase item screen: loads the "Item.cel" background from MISC.VFS onto a freshly allocated 320x200 surface, then runs a five-entry menu loop dispatching to the item sub-screens until the player backs out.
plate_comment:
Village item screen driver.

Algorithm:
1. Copies a 5-dword menu descriptor table from DAT_00031180 into a local array (the menu entry ids 0x24, 0x14, 0x15, 0x04, 0x10).
2. Loads asset "Item.cel" from container "MISC.VFS" (FUN_0002a140), allocates a 64000-byte (320x200) surface (FUN_0003d375), publishes it in DAT_00063fb4, blits the cel into it with pitch 0x140 (FUN_0002dba0), then frees the cel (FUN_0003d478).
3. Runs the screen transition FUN_00031780(surface, 0x9f, 0x63, 1), presents the surface (FUN_00032570), restores the 0xa8208 region (FUN_00032370) and draws the header text (message id 0x1f4 via FUN_0001ff60).
4. Loops: FUN_000323e0(menu_table, 5, &selection) reads a selection; a jump table at 0x35948 dispatches case 0 (redraw plus message id 4), case 1 -> FUN_00033b80(surface, 0), case 2 -> FUN_00034000(surface), case 3 -> FUN_00034210(surface), case 4 -> FUN_00033f80(surface). After each entry the screen is re-presented and message id 0x1f5 redrawn; selection == -1 leaves the loop.
5. On exit runs the closing transition FUN_00031780(surface, 0x9f, 0x63, 0) and frees the surface (FUN_0003d478).

Parameters: none. State comes from the globals DAT_000643c4 / DAT_00060124 (text sources) and the menu table at DAT_00031180.

Returns: nothing.
evidence: Only caller is fdps_run_village_phase @ 00031210, so this is a village-phase sub-screen. The single string pair it references is s_MISC_VFS_00060128 ("MISC.VFS") and s_Item_cel_00061fa4 ("Item.cel"), naming the screen's own background asset. The 0xfa00 (64000) allocation and the 0x140 pitch passed to the blit and text calls are a mode-13h 320x200 surface. The body is a canonical menu loop: a 5-entry table copied to the stack, FUN_000323e0(table, 5, &selection), a CS-relative jump table at 0x35948 with five arms, and -1 as the exit sentinel. Pool is fdps because it consumes game asset containers and game UI helpers; no CRT or Miles entry points are touched apart from the allocator/free pair. Prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5, args pushed and cleaned by the caller with ADD ESP, and 'MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP' epilogue match the -4s stack convention recorded in rebuild_info/build_flags.md, hence __cdecl; the function itself reads no stack parameters ([EBP+0x14] is never touched), so it takes none.
open_question: The meaning of the five menu entries is not settled: the table holds opaque ids (0x24, 0x14, 0x15, 0x04, 0x10) and case 0 invokes no handler, only a redraw plus message id 4 from DAT_00060124, which may be a stub or an unavailable-option notice. Whether the screen is item management or an item shop cannot be decided without naming FUN_00033b80 / FUN_00034000 / FUN_00034210 / FUN_00033f80, and the message ids 0x1f4 / 0x1f5 / 4 have no resolved text source yet.

name: fdps_run_church_screen
role: Runs the village church facility screen: loads and displays the Church.cel backdrop, then loops on a 4-entry menu dispatching to three church service handlers until the player cancels.
plate_comment:
Village church facility screen (one of the village sub-screens dispatched from fdps_run_village_phase).

Algorithm:
1. Copies a 16-byte menu descriptor {0x24, 0x12, 4, 0x10} from the read-only table at 0x00031194 onto the stack; the fields read as x=36, y=18, item_count=4, line_height=16.
2. Opens resource "Church.cel" out of container "MISC.VFS" (FUN_0002a140), allocates a 64000-byte (320x200) screen buffer (FUN_0003d375), publishes the buffer pointer in the global at 0x00063fb4, decodes the cel into the buffer (FUN_0002dba0, stride 0x140), then frees the cel data (FUN_0003d478).
3. Presents the backdrop with FUN_00031780(buffer, 0x9f, 0x63, 1) - a fade/transfer centred on (159, 99) with the enable flag set - and does an initial page/cursor update (FUN_00032570) plus a full-width copy of the 0x000A8208 region (FUN_00032370) and a text/dialog draw (FUN_0001ff60, id 0x200).
4. Main loop: while the selection variable is not -1, run the menu widget FUN_000323e0(descriptor, 4, &selection) and switch on the result via the jump table at 0x00035b84:
     case 0 - no handler; only toggles the display twice and redraws through the global at 0x00060124 with id 7.
     case 1 - FUN_000345a0(buffer)
     case 2 - FUN_00034210(buffer)
     case 3 - FUN_00033f80(buffer)
   After the handler, selection == -1 leaves the display enabled and exits the loop; otherwise the backdrop and the id 0x201 text are redrawn and the loop repeats.
5. On exit, FUN_00031780(buffer, 0x9f, 0x63, 0) fades the screen back out and the 64000-byte buffer is freed.

Parameters: none. The function reads nothing above the frame pointer; all state comes from the resource files and the globals at 0x00063fb4, 0x000643c4 and 0x00060124.

Returns: nothing.
evidence: Two literal strings settle the identity: the function passes "MISC.VFS" (0x00060128) and "Church.cel" (0x00061fb0) to the resource loader at 0x0002a140, so the backdrop it puts up is the church. Its single caller is fdps_run_village_phase, which places it as one of the village facility screens, matching the shape of the code: load backdrop, allocate a 320x200 buffer, loop a 4-entry menu widget, dispatch three handlers, fade out and free. Pool is fdps because it drives game-specific resources and screen flow; there is no CRT or Miles signature anywhere in it. Calling convention is __cdecl: every call site pushes its arguments on the stack and the caller restores ESP with ADD ESP,n afterwards, and this function itself takes no arguments (the param_1/param_2/unaff_EBX in the decompilation are Ghidra guesses - no stack slot above EBP is ever read).
open_question: Menu case 0 calls no handler at all, only a display toggle and a redraw through the global at 0x00060124 with id 7; whether that entry is a disabled/unimplemented church service or a purely visual sub-state could not be settled from this function alone. Which concrete church service each of 0x000345a0 / 0x00034210 / 0x00033f80 implements (revive, save, load, ...) is also unresolved here, as is the meaning of the message ids 0x200 / 0x201 / 7 passed to FUN_0001ff60.

name: fdps_run_bar_shop
role: Runs the village bar/tavern screen: loads BarShop.cel from MISC.VFS into a 320x200 backbuffer, fades in, then loops over a 4-entry menu dispatching to the bar's option handlers until the player leaves.
plate_comment:
Village bar/tavern screen.

Algorithm:
1. Copies a 4-entry menu descriptor table from 0x000311a4 (0x24, 9, 10, 8) into a local array.
2. Loads "BarShop.cel" out of the "MISC.VFS" container (FUN_0002a140), allocates a 64000-byte (320x200) backbuffer via the CRT allocator, decodes the cel into it (FUN_0002dba0, pitch 0x140), publishes the buffer in the global at 0x00063fb4, then frees the raw file image.
3. Fades the screen in (FUN_00031780 with flag 1), starts the screen's audio/entry hook (FUN_00036460), shows the cursor, uploads the palette at 0xa8208 and prints the bar greeting (FUN_0001ff60, text id 0x200).
4. Loops: FUN_000323e0 drives the 4-entry menu and returns the picked index in a local; a switch dispatches index 0..3. Index 0 prints a canned message (text id 6). Index 1 enters FUN_000241e0. Index 2 enters FUN_00024490 and, when it returns 1, calls FUN_00031540(1) and ends the loop. Index 3 asks a confirmation (text id 0x1f0) via FUN_00017990; on a zero answer it sets the byte flag at 0x000643eb, prints text id 0x1f1, delays ~300 ticks and ends the loop.
5. Each iteration that does not end the loop hides the cursor, reprints the greeting (text id 0x201) and restores the palette; the sentinel -1 in the selection variable terminates the loop.
6. On exit fades out (FUN_00031780 with flag 0) and frees the backbuffer.

Parameters: none.
Returns: nothing.
evidence: The function's only string evidence is decisive: it calls the VFS loader with "MISC.VFS" (0x00060128) and "BarShop.cel" (0x00061fbc), so this screen is the bar/tavern. Its single caller is fdps_run_village_phase, which places it as one of the village facility screens. The body is a textbook screen driver: 64000-byte 320x200 buffer, cel decode at pitch 0x140, fade-in/fade-out pair with flags 1 and 0, a 4-entry menu table copied from .data, a switch on the selected index and a -1 sentinel to leave. Pool is fdps because the logic is game-specific and the only runtime helpers used are the allocator/free/delay thunks. Convention is __cdecl: the prologue is the -4s stack-convention prologue (PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP, MOV EBP,ESP) documented in rebuild_info/build_flags.md, and every call pushes arguments and is followed by ADD ESP,n in this function.
open_question: Which real-world bar action each of the four menu indices maps to (rumor, recruit, quest, leave) is not settled -- the handlers at 0x000241e0, 0x00024490 and 0x00017990 were not read, and the text ids 6/0x1f0/0x1f1/0x200/0x201 have not been resolved to strings. The meaning of the global byte flag set at 0x000643eb on the index-3 path is also unknown.

name: fdps_run_weapon_shop
role: Runs the village weapon-shop screen: loads the Weapon.cel full-screen background into a 320x200 offscreen buffer, then loops on a 5-entry menu dispatching to the shop sub-screens until the player leaves.
plate_comment:
Village weapon-shop screen driver.

Algorithm:
1. Copies the 5-entry menu descriptor table at 000311b4 (ids 0x24, 0x14, 0x15, 0x04, 0x06) into a local array.
2. Loads resource "Weapon.cel" out of the container "MISC.VFS" via FUN_0002a140, allocates a 64000-byte (320x200) offscreen buffer via the CRT allocator at 0003d375, publishes the buffer pointer to the global at 00063fb4, decodes the cel into the buffer with FUN_0002dba0 (pitch 0x140), then frees the loaded cel image.
3. Plays the screen-open transition FUN_00031780(buffer, 0x9f, 0x63, 1) centred on 159,99, presents the buffer with FUN_00032570(buffer, 0), blits the overlay at 000a8208 with FUN_00032370 and draws the header text (entry 0x1fe of the table pointed to by the global at 000643c4) with FUN_0001ff60 into 000aa3d4.
4. Loops: FUN_000323e0 runs the 5-item menu selector and writes the chosen index into a local; index 0 blanks and redraws the panel and prints message 5 of the table at 00060124; indices 1..4 call the sub-screens FUN_00033b80(buffer, 1), FUN_00034000(buffer), FUN_00034210(buffer) and FUN_00034420(buffer). After each iteration the selection is re-tested: -1 leaves the loop after a final present, otherwise the panel and prompt text (entry 0x1ff) are redrawn and the loop repeats.
5. On exit plays the closing transition FUN_00031780(buffer, 0x9f, 0x63, 0) and frees the offscreen buffer.

Parameters: none. All state comes from the module globals and the embedded menu table.

Returns: nothing.
evidence: The function reads no incoming stack slots and every call site pushes its arguments and cleans up with ADD ESP, so it is a no-argument __cdecl routine. It is called from exactly one place, fdps_run_village_phase at 00031210, which places it in the village facility menu family. The only string evidence in the function is the pair pushed to FUN_0002a140: "MISC.VFS" at 00060128 and "Weapon.cel" at 00061fc8, and the loaded data is decoded into a freshly allocated 64000-byte buffer at a pitch of 0x140, i.e. a full 320x200 background image for a weapon-related screen. The body is a textbook screen driver: open transition, present, menu selector over a 5-entry table, jump table at 000360b8 to four sub-screens, redraw, close transition, free.
open_question: The five menu entry ids (0x24, 0x14, 0x15, 0x04, 0x06) and the text ids 0x1fe/0x1ff/5 were not resolved to labels, so the individual shop commands (buy / sell / equip / etc.) and the exact identity of sub-screens 00033b80, 00034000, 00034210 and 00034420 are unconfirmed; the name rests on the Weapon.cel background plus the village caller, not on any decoded menu label.

name: fdps_run_secret_menu
role: Runs the village-phase "Secret" screen: loads Secret.cel from MISC.VFS into a freshly allocated 320x200 backbuffer, fades in, then loops on a six-entry hotspot menu dispatching to five sub-screen handlers until the user exits.
plate_comment:
Village-phase Secret screen menu loop.

Algorithm:
1. Copies a 6-entry menu descriptor table from 0x000311c8 (values 0x24, 0x14, 0x15, 0x04, 0x06, 0x10) into a stack copy at [ebp-0x24]; the loop mutates the copy so the table stays pristine.
2. Loads "Secret.cel" out of the "MISC.VFS" container (0x0002a140), allocates a 64000-byte (320x200) backbuffer via 0x0003d375, publishes the pointer to the global at 0x00063fb4, decodes the CEL into the buffer with pitch 0x140 (0x0002dba0), then frees the raw CEL data (0x0003d478).
3. Fades the screen in through 0x00031780 with centre (0x9f, 0x63) and direction 1, presents the buffer (0x00032570, mode 0), refreshes the 0x140-wide overlay at 0xa8208 (0x00032370), and draws the prompt with message id 0x202 (0x0001ff60, using the global at 0x000643c4).
4. Loops while the selection is not -1: 0x000323e0 reads a selection from the 6-entry table into the local, a jump table at 0x000362f8 dispatches cases 0..5 -- case 0 presents mode 2 then mode 0 and draws message id 8 with the global at 0x00060124, cases 1..5 call 0x00033b80 (with sub-mode 2), 0x00034000, 0x00034210, 0x00034420 and 0x00033f80 respectively, each taking only the backbuffer. Selections above 5 fall through to the tail.
5. Tail of each iteration: if the selection is -1 the screen is presented in mode 1 and the loop exits; otherwise it is presented in mode 0, message id 0x1f5 is drawn and the overlay at 0xa8208 is refreshed, then control returns to the top of the loop.
6. On exit, fades out with 0x00031780 (centre 0x9f, 0x63, direction 0) and frees the backbuffer.

Parameters: none. The function reads no incoming arguments; Ghidra's param_1/param_2/unaff_EBX are decompiler artefacts.

Returns: nothing. The selected backbuffer pointer is also left in the global at 0x00063fb4 while the screen is live.
evidence: Standard four-push prologue and stack-argument/caller-cleanup call sites (every CALL is followed by ADD ESP,n) match the documented -4s default in rebuild_info/build_flags.md, so __cdecl with no register arguments. Pool is fdps: it references the game's own VFS container string "MISC.VFS" at 0x00060128 and the asset name "Secret.cel" at 0x00061fd4, allocates exactly 64000 bytes (the 320x200 mode 13h frame) and blits with pitch 0x140. Its only caller is fdps_run_village_phase (0x00031210), which places it in the village-phase menu tree; the 6-entry table copied from 0x000311c8 plus the 6-way CS-relative jump table at 0x000362f8 make the menu-loop shape unambiguous. The fade-in/fade-out pairing of 0x00031780 (direction 1 on entry, 0 on exit) around the loop is the usual screen-enter/screen-leave bracket.
open_question: What the six menu entries actually are is not settled: the descriptor values 0x24/0x14/0x15/0x04/0x06/0x10 and the five handlers (0x00033b80, 0x00034000, 0x00034210, 0x00034420, 0x00033f80) are still unnamed, so the name records only that this is the Secret.cel screen and not which village facility it represents. Message ids 0x202, 0x1f5 and 8 were not resolved to text.

name: fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range
role: Walks a closed index range of the global 0x50-byte object records and rewrites the low nibble of each record's byte field at offset 0x34, leaving the high nibble untouched.
plate_comment:
Sets the low nibble of the byte at offset 0x34 for every record in a closed index range of the global 0x50-byte object table.

Algorithm:
  i = first_index
  while (i <= last_index) {
      rec = object_at(i);            /* FUN_0002d210: *(char**)0x00069cd8 + i * 0x50 */
      rec[0x34] = (rec[0x34] & 0xF0) | value;
  }
  The high nibble of rec[0x34] is preserved; only the low nibble is replaced.
  The loop is inclusive of last_index, so first_index == last_index touches exactly
  one record. If first_index > last_index nothing is written.
  All three observed call sites pass value = 0, i.e. they clear the low nibble.
  Only the low byte of the third stack slot is read (register DH).

Parameters:
  [EBP+0x14] int first_index  - first object index, inclusive
  [EBP+0x18] int last_index   - last object index, inclusive
  [EBP+0x1C] unsigned char value - value merged into the low nibble of field 0x34

Returns:
  Nothing. Arguments are passed on the stack and removed by the caller (ADD ESP,0xC).
prototype: void fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range(int first_index, int last_index, unsigned char value)
evidence: Disassembly is a single inclusive counting loop over [EBP+0x14]..[EBP+0x18]; each iteration calls FUN_0002d210(i), whose whole body is 'IMUL EAX,[EBP+0x14],0x50; ADD EAX,[0x00069cd8]' - a pure index-to-record accessor over a global array of 0x50-byte records that 60+ functions use. The loop body reads rec[0x34], masks with 0xF0 and ORs in the byte argument, so exactly the low nibble of that field is written. No registers carry arguments (first argument sits at the first stack slot after the four saved registers and the return address), and both call sites push three dwords right-to-left then execute ADD ESP,0xC, so the convention is __cdecl, not the Watcom register default. Call sites: fdps_title_demo @0002acd7 passes (0, 0xB, 0) and FUN_0003b150 passes (n+0xC, n+0xC, 0), (n+0x1D, n+0x1D, 0), (n+0x2E, n+0x2E, 0) with n = DAT_00069ce8 < 0x12. Pool is fdps because the code touches a game-owned global record table and matches no CRT or Miles AIL routine.
open_question: The meaning of the 0x50-byte record table at *0x00069cd8 and of the low nibble of its byte field 0x34 is not established; the accessor FUN_0002d210 is still unnamed, so the name is structural rather than semantic. The subsystem cannot be pinned down: the table is reached from the title demo as well as from dozens of unnamed functions in the 0x10000-0x25000 range. All observed callers pass 0, so whether non-zero values are ever written is unknown.

name: fdps_vfs_find_entry
role: Linear-searches an archive directory table for the entry whose 13-byte name field matches the requested name, returning the entry index or -1.
plate_comment:
Look up a named entry in an archive directory table.

Algorithm:
The entry count is the single byte at the start of the directory block (dir[0]).
For each index i from 0 to count-1 the routine copies 13 (0xd) bytes from
dir + i*0x1a + 0x11 -- the name field of a 26-byte directory entry -- into a
16-byte stack buffer via the 3-argument copy helper at 0x000435bc, passes the
caller-supplied name through the helper at 0x000435f3 (which returns a string
pointer), and compares the two with the compare helper at 0x00042fe0. A zero
result means a match: the loop stores i and returns it. If the loop runs off
the end without a match the result stays at its initial -1.
The search index is kept in a local and returned unchanged; there is no early
exit other than the match, and the comparison is done on the raw stored name
with no case folding of the table side.

Parameters:
  name - pointer to the name being looked up; passed through the helper at
         0x000435f3 before comparison (stack slot EBP+0x14)
  dir  - pointer to the directory block: byte 0 is the entry count, entry i
         has stride 0x1a and its 13-byte name field at +0x11
         (stack slot EBP+0x18)

Returns:
  Zero-based index of the matching directory entry, or -1 when no entry
  matches.
evidence: Both arguments are read from stack slots above the saved registers (EBP+0x14, EBP+0x18) and the function returns with a plain RET, so the caller cleans the stack: stack-based cdecl, not the Watcom register default. The body is a textbook table lookup: count byte at dir[0], stride 0x1a from IMUL EAX,[EBP-8],0x1a, a 13-byte (PUSH 0xd) name field at +0x11 copied into a 16-byte stack buffer, a compare whose zero result selects the index, and a -1 sentinel initialised before the loop. Its only caller is fdps_vfs_load_file @ 00039bd0, which fixes the subsystem as the archive/VFS layer and the return value as a directory index; the name is derived from that role, and the pool is fdps because the routine encodes the game's own directory record layout rather than any library contract.
open_question: What the single-argument helper at 0x000435f3 does to the caller's name (case folding, path stripping, or returning a pointer into a scratch buffer) was not established, so whether the lookup is case-sensitive is unsettled. The three callees at 0x000435bc, 0x000435f3 and 0x00042fe0 are unnamed; if 0x000435bc/0x00042fe0 turn out to be CRT strncpy/strcmp the wording of the plate comment should say so.

name: fdps_vfs_open
role: Opens a .VFS container file, reads its entry table into a freshly allocated in-memory handle that also stores the entry count and the container path, then closes the file and returns the handle.
plate_comment:
Opens a VFS container and builds its in-memory directory handle.

Algorithm:
  1. fopen(path, "rb"). Return NULL if it fails.
  2. fseek to offset 7, fread a u32 entry_count.
  3. fseek to offset 5, fread a u16 table_offset (later sign-extended when used as a seek target, so the usable range is 0..0x7FFF).
  4. Allocate 0x11 + entry_count * 0x1A bytes for the handle. If the allocation fails, still close the file and return NULL.
  5. memset the first 0x11 bytes of the handle to zero, store entry_count at offset 0, and memcpy strlen(path) bytes of the container path to offset 4 (the zeroed header leaves it NUL terminated for names up to 12 characters).
  6. fseek to table_offset and fread entry_count entries of 0x1A bytes each into handle+0x11.
  7. fclose and return the handle.

The container magic "VFS", the version word, the 24-byte signature, the duplicated per-entry size and the reserved byte are never examined, so a non-VFS file is not rejected here.

Parameters:
  path - NUL terminated container file name, opened through the C runtime, no directory search of its own.

Returns:
  Pointer to the allocated container handle {u32 entry_count; char path[13]; entry table of entry_count * 0x1A bytes}, or NULL if the file could not be opened or the handle could not be allocated.
evidence: The disassembly opens the argument at [ebp+0x14] with fopen(path, "rb") -- the literal "rb" is at 0x6201c -- then seeks to 7 for a 4-byte count and to 5 for a 2-byte offset, allocates count*0x1a+0x11, zeroes 0x11 bytes, stores the count at +0, copies the path string to +4, and reads count*0x1a bytes into +0x11 before fclose. That is exactly the VFS container layout already established in resource_info/vfs.md (header 35 bytes, u16 table offset at 0x05, u32 entry count at 0x07, 26-byte entries), and that document already attributes the container open to 0x39ab0. Six game-side callers including fdps_load_global_resources put it in the fdps pool, file_io subsystem. The prologue 'PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP; MOV EBP,ESP' with the first argument at [ebp+0x14] and 'MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP' epilogue is the -4s stack-convention signature recorded in rebuild_info/build_flags.md, and every callee here is invoked with pushes plus caller ADD ESP, so the convention is __cdecl, not __watcall.
open_question: The exact element type of the returned handle is described but not typed as a struct here; callee 0x0003d375 is the allocation wrapper and 0x42xxx are the CRT file routines, none of which were inspected under this ticket.

name: fdps_vfs_load_file
role: Looks up a named entry in an open VFS archive descriptor, allocates a buffer for it and reads the entry's bytes from the archive file, returning the buffer or NULL on any failure.
plate_comment:
Loads one named entry out of a VFS archive into a freshly allocated buffer.

Algorithm:
1. Calls the VFS name lookup helper at 00039990 with (name, vfs) to get the entry index; if it returns -1 prints "Can't find the string: %s" and returns NULL.
2. Copies 13 bytes of the archive path stored at vfs+4 into a local buffer (strncpy) and opens it with fopen(path, "rb"); on failure prints "Can't open the source VFS_file: %s" and returns NULL.
3. Reads the entry's byte length from the directory record at vfs + 0x1e + index * 0x1a (record field +0) and asks the allocator at 0003d375 for that many bytes; on failure prints "Can't allocate memory for VFS_file: %s(%dbytes)", closes the file and returns NULL.
4. Reads the entry's file offset from field +9 of the same record, fseek(fp, offset, SEEK_SET), fread(buf, length, 1, fp), then fclose(fp).
5. Returns the allocated buffer (NULL on any of the error paths above).

Directory layout implied by the arithmetic: a 0x1e byte header (archive path string at +4) followed by 0x1a byte records, each holding the entry length at +0 and the entry offset at +9.

Parameters:
  name - entry name to look up inside the archive; also used in the error messages.
  vfs  - pointer to the loaded VFS descriptor (header plus directory records).

Returns: pointer to the newly allocated buffer holding the entry's contents, or NULL if the entry was not found, the archive could not be opened, or the allocation failed. The caller owns the buffer.
evidence: Both arguments arrive on the stack ([EBP+0x14], [EBP+0x18] after PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP) and every call site inside the function uses PUSH + ADD ESP,n, so the convention is caller-cleaned __cdecl. The three format strings read from 0x62020/0x62054/0x62078 name the subsystem outright: "Can't allocate memory for VFS_file: %s(%dbytes)", "Can't open the source VFS_file: %s", "Can't find the string: %s", and 0x6201c is the literal "rb" passed as the fopen mode. The body is the textbook lookup/open/alloc/seek/read/close sequence over a fixed 0x1a byte directory record, and the callers include fdps_load_global_resources, confirming this is game-side resource loading rather than CRT or AIL code.
open_question: The exact field layout of the 0x1e byte VFS header and of the 0x1a byte record beyond length(+0) and offset(+9) is not settled here; the 13 byte archive path at vfs+4 suggests an 8.3 DOS filename field but that was not cross-checked against the on-disk format.

name: fdps_cd_alloc_dos_buffers
role: Allocates the two 512-byte DOS real-mode memory blocks used as the MSCDEX request header and data transfer buffers, caching their segment and flat linear addresses in globals.
plate_comment:
Allocates the DOS real-mode communication buffers used by the CD-ROM (MSCDEX) driver layer.

Algorithm:
1. Zero the 12-byte struct SREGS at 0x00069df0 with memset.
2. Fill the input REGS at 0x00069dc8 with AX = 0x0100 and BX = 0x0020, then call int386x(0x31, in, out, sregs). DPMI function 0100h allocates 0x20 paragraphs (512 bytes) of DOS memory below 1MB; the returned AX is the real-mode segment and DX the protected-mode selector (the selector is discarded).
3. Store the first block's real-mode segment as a word at 0x00069e54 and its flat linear address (segment << 4) at 0x00069de8. Under DOS/4GW the first megabyte is identity mapped, so segment << 4 is directly dereferenceable.
4. Repeat the identical DPMI 0100h call for a second 512-byte block; store its segment shifted left 16 bits at 0x00069da8 (pre-packed seg:0000 real-mode far pointer for the MSCDEX request header transfer address field) and its flat linear address (segment << 4) at 0x00069da4.

The input REGS block is not re-initialised before the second call because int386x leaves the caller's input structure untouched.

No error handling: a failed DPMI allocation leaves the carry flag set and garbage in AX, and the resulting addresses are used unchecked by the CD driver functions.

Parameters: none.

Returns: nothing. Results are published through the globals at 0x00069da4, 0x00069da8, 0x00069de8 and 0x00069e54.
evidence: Disassembly shows two identical int386x-shaped calls (push segregs, push outregs, push inregs, push 0x31, call 0x00043657, add esp,0x10) with the input REGS preloaded AX=0x0100 / BX=0x0020, which is DPMI INT 31h function 0100h 'Allocate DOS Memory Block' for 0x20 paragraphs. The returned AX (real-mode segment) is converted to a flat linear address by << 4 and to a packed far pointer by << 16, the classic DOS/4GW real-mode transfer buffer idiom. The sole caller is fdps_cdrom_detect, and every reader of the two resulting linear addresses (0x00069de8, 0x00069da4) is a CD driver function including fdps_cd_stop_audio, so the buffers belong to the MSCDEX interface. Callees are CRT only (memset at 0x00042cd0, int386x at 0x00043657, Watcom stack-probe helper at 0x0004361a), so the function body itself is game code. No parameters are set up by the caller and none are read; the decompiler's param_1/param_2/unaff_EBX are artifacts of it mis-modelling the CRT callees.
open_question: The DPMI selector returned in DX is discarded, so the blocks can never be freed through DPMI 0101h; whether any later code frees them was not checked. The exact split of roles between the two buffers (which one is the MSCDEX request header and which the data transfer area) needs the CD command builders at 0003bfa5 / 0003c0c8 to confirm.

name: fdps_cd_device_request
role: Issues the MSCDEX "Send Device Request" call (INT 2Fh, AX=1510h) against the pre-filled CD-ROM request header by simulating a real-mode interrupt through DPMI INT 31h AX=0300h.
plate_comment:
Sends the currently prepared MSCDEX request header to the CD-ROM device driver.

Algorithm:
Clears the SREGS block at 0x00069df0 (12 bytes) and the DPMI real-mode call structure at 0x00069e22 (0x32 bytes). Fills the real-mode structure with EAX=0x1510 (MSCDEX Send Device Request), ECX = the CD-ROM subunit number held in the byte at 0x00069dfe, EBX=0 and ES = the real-mode segment of the request header held in the word at 0x00069e54, so that the driver receives ES:BX pointing at the request header. It then fills the protected-mode input REGS block at 0x00069dc8 with EAX=0x0300 (DPMI Simulate Real Mode Interrupt), BL=0x2f (interrupt 2Fh), BH=0, ECX=0 (no words copied from the protected-mode stack) and EDI = 0x00069e22, sets SREGS.es to DS, and calls int86x(0x31, &inregs, &outregs, &sregs). If the carry flag in the output REGS (0x00069dc4) is set, it prints "DEVICE REQUEST FAILED!!!" and returns anyway; the MSCDEX status word in the request header is not inspected here.

Parameters:
None. Every input is a file-scope global: the request header itself and its real-mode segment at 0x00069e54, and the CD-ROM subunit number at 0x00069dfe. Callers fill the request header before calling.

Returns:
Nothing. Failure is only reported on stdout; the caller must read the request header status field itself.
evidence: The only string reference is s_DEVICE_REQUEST_FAILED____0006223c = "DEVICE REQUEST FAILED!!!\n", printed when the output REGS carry flag is set. The constant 0x1510 loaded into the EAX slot of the real-mode structure is the MSCDEX "Send Device Request" function of INT 2Fh, and 0x0300 with BL=0x2f in the protected-mode REGS is the DPMI Simulate Real Mode Interrupt service for INT 2Fh. Offsets confirm the layout: 0x00069e22 is the DPMI real-mode call structure (EBX at +0x10 = 0x69e32, ECX at +0x18 = 0x69e3a, EAX at +0x1c = 0x69e3e, ES at +0x22 = 0x69e44), 0x00069dc8 is a Watcom union REGS (EAX +0, EBX +4, ECX +8, EDI +0x14 = 0x69ddc), 0x00069dac is the output REGS whose cflag sits at +0x18 = 0x00069dc4, and 0x00069df0 is a 12-byte struct SREGS with ES first. The four-argument cdecl call at 0x00043657 (ADD ESP,0x10 after PUSH 0x31/out/in/sregs) is int86x. All seven callers are the CD subsystem, one of which is already named fdps_cd_stop_audio, so the pool is fdps and the subsystem is cd. The entry PUSH 0x14 / CALL 0x0004361a is the Watcom stack-overflow probe with the exact worst-case frame (16 bytes of outgoing arguments plus the return address), not a real parameter, so the function takes no arguments and the unaff_EBX and param_N in the decompiler output are artifacts.
open_question: Which caller writes the real-mode segment word at 0x00069e54 and the subunit byte at 0x00069dfe, and whether the request header lives in a DOS-memory block allocated once at CD init, was not traced.

name: fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info
role: Issues an MSCDEX/CD-ROM device-driver IOCTL Input request with control-block code 0x0A (Read Disk Info) and caches the lowest track, highest track, lead-out MSF address and driver status word into globals.
plate_comment:
Reads the CD-ROM table-of-contents summary via the MSCDEX device driver.

Algorithm:
Builds a 26-byte (0x1a) CD-ROM device driver request header on the stack: header length 0x1a, subunit 0, command code 3 (IOCTL Input), media descriptor 0, transfer address taken from the real-mode buffer pointer at 0x00069da8, transfer byte count 7, starting sector 0, volume ID pointer NULL. Next it zero-fills a 7-byte IOCTL control block and sets its first byte to 0x0A (Read Disk Info). Both blocks are copied down into the DOS-addressable low-memory staging buffers whose linear addresses are held in 0x00069de8 (request header) and 0x00069da4 (IOCTL control block), then the driver is invoked through the request dispatcher at 0003bb7d. Afterwards both blocks are copied back up from low memory and the reply is distributed: the 6 payload bytes are mirrored to 0x00069e16, the lowest track number to 0x00069e06, the highest track number to 0x00069e07, the 4-byte lead-out address is split into its three MSF components at 0x00069e08/09/0a by 0003bc3f and converted to a single frame/LBA count at 0x00069e0b by 0003bc78, and the driver status word from offset 3 of the request header is stored to 0x00069e20.

Parameters:
None. All input and output travel through file-scope globals and the low-memory staging buffers pointed to by 0x00069da4, 0x00069da8 and 0x00069de8.

Returns:
Nothing. Results are observed through the globals listed above; 0x00069e20 holds the raw device driver status word for error checking by the caller.
evidence: The stack block matches the documented MSCDEX CD-ROM device driver request header field for field: byte 0 = 0x1a header length, byte 1 = subunit, byte 2 = 3 (IOCTL Input), byte 0x0d = media descriptor, dword 0x0e = transfer address, word 0x12 = transfer count 7, word 0x14 = starting sector, dword 0x16 = volume ID pointer. The 7-byte transfer buffer is the IOCTL Input control block for code 0x0A (Read Disk Info), whose reply layout is exactly [0]=0x0A, [1]=lowest track, [2]=highest track, [3..6]=lead-out track address in MSF -- which is precisely how the returned bytes are split at 0003c07c onward. The only caller is fdps_cdrom_detect, confirming the CD subsystem. Calls at 000435bc are a 3-argument memcpy and 00042cd0 a 3-argument memset (both stack-arg, caller-cleaned, CRT pool); 0004361a is the Watcom __STK stack-probe prologue. Convention is the binary-wide stack default (-4s) per rebuild_info/build_flags.md, consistent with every callee here taking pushed arguments cleaned up by ADD ESP.
open_question: The purpose of the redundant memcpy at 0003c024 (copying the IOCTL control block back up from low memory immediately before the driver call, before any reply exists) is unexplained; it is harmless but must be reproduced verbatim for byte-level fidelity of the call sequence.

name: fdps_cd_stop_audio
role: Builds a 13-byte MSCDEX CD-ROM device-driver request header for command 0x85 (Stop Audio), dispatches it through the shared driver-request helper, and saves the returned status word.
plate_comment:
Stop CD audio playback.

Algorithm: Reserves a 16-byte local scratch area and fills the first three bytes with a DOS CD-ROM device driver request header: length = 0x0D (13 bytes), subunit = 0, command code = 0x85 (Stop Audio Play). The header is copied into the real-mode-addressable request buffer pointed to by DAT_00069de8 with a 13-byte memcpy, the driver request dispatcher at 0003bb7d is invoked with no further arguments, then the same 13 bytes are copied back from the buffer into the local scratch area. The status word at header offset 3 is stored into the global DAT_00069e20, which holds the result of the most recent CD driver request.

Parameters: none.

Returns: nothing. The driver status word is left in the global at 00069e20.
evidence: The disassembly writes the literal byte triple 0D 00 85 to a stack buffer and then transfers exactly 0x0D bytes to and from the pointer in DAT_00069de8, which is the exact layout and length of a DOS CD-ROM (MSCDEX) device driver request header for command code 133 = Stop Audio Play; the word read back from offset 3 is the request header's status field. Six sibling functions in the 0003bf..0003c7 range call the same dispatcher 0003bb7d, i.e. a family of CD driver request wrappers. It is called from main and from five game-side functions (scene/chapter transitions), which fits stopping background CD music, so the pool is fdps game logic rather than CRT. No arguments are read and nothing is returned in EAX, so the default Watcom register convention applies trivially.

name: fdps_cdrom_detect
role: Startup CD-ROM probe: runs the MSCDEX installation check (INT 2Fh AX=1500h), records how many CD-ROM drive letters exist and which letter is the first one, then initialises the CD subsystem and issues one device request, returning 0 when MSCDEX is absent, 1 on success and 2 when that request leaves the status word 0x810C.
plate_comment:
CD-ROM presence check, called once from main during startup. main sign-extends the
result and aborts with "Fatal error: CDROM is not install!!!" unless it is exactly 1.

Algorithm:
  1. PUSH 0x10 / CALL __CHK (0004361a) - Watcom stack probe for the 16 bytes this call
     chain needs. Not a parameter.
  2. Fills the input union REGS at 00069dc8: AL=0 (00069dc8), AH=0x15 (00069dc9),
     BX=0 (00069dcc), i.e. AX=1500h - the MSCDEX installation check.
  3. int386(0x2f, &in_regs at 00069dc8, &out_regs at 00069dac) via 00043268.
     On return the output block holds BX at 00069db0 (number of CD-ROM drive letters)
     and CX at 00069db4 (index of the first CD-ROM drive letter, 0 = A:).
  4. If BX == 0 no CD-ROM redirector is loaded: return 0 immediately.
  5. Otherwise publishes the result to the CD subsystem globals: the drive count word
     goes to 00069dfc and the low byte of the first-drive-letter index to 00069dfe.
  6. If the flag at 00069e54 is still zero, calls the one-time CD initialiser at
     0003bade, then always calls 0003bfa5, which leaves a 16-bit status word at
     00069e20.
  7. Returns 2 if that status word is 0x810C, otherwise 1.

Parameters:
  None. The decompiler's param_1/param_2/unaff_EBX are artifacts: param_1 is the
  0x10 stack-probe immediate, and nothing in the body reads an incoming register or
  a stack slot.

Returns:
  0 - no MSCDEX / CD-ROM redirector installed (INT 2Fh AX=1500h returned BX=0).
  1 - CD-ROM found and the device request completed with a status other than 0x810C.
  2 - CD-ROM found but the device request left status 0x810C at 00069e20.
  Only 1 is accepted by main; both 0 and 2 end the program.
evidence: The INT 2Fh call is unambiguous in the disassembly: byte [00069dc9] (AH) is set to 0x15, byte [00069dc8] (AL) to 0, word [00069dcc] (BX, offset +4 of the input union REGS) to 0, and 00043268 is called with the stack arguments 0x2f, 00069dc8, 00069dac followed by ADD ESP,0xc. 00043268 is already identified in this walk as int386(intno, in_regs, out_regs). AX=1500h with BX=0 is the MSCDEX installation check; it returns the number of CD-ROM drive letters in BX and the first drive letter in CX. The code reads exactly those two fields out of the output block: 00069dac+4 = 00069db0 (EBX) is tested for zero and copied as a word to 00069dfc, and 00069dac+8 = 00069db4 (ECX) has its low byte copied to 00069dfe. Purpose confirmed from the caller side: main (00029220) is the only caller, and per its own verdict it prints "Fatal error: CDROM is not install!!!\a\n" / "Check your CDROM please!!!\n" and exit(1) whenever this function returns anything but 1, and pairs it with a shutdown call to 0003c4a7. That makes this game code, not library code, hence the fdps_ prefix and the cd subsystem. Calling convention: the module default is the stack convention (-4s) per rebuild_info/build_flags.md, this function takes no arguments at all, and the only non-default signals listed there are absent - the PUSH imm / CALL __CHK prologue is explicitly excluded as a cc signal. Return type short rather than int is inferred from main sign-extending the result with CWDE before comparing it against 1. All the globals touched (00069dac..00069e54) lie inside the BSS range 00063930..0006a3bc cleared by the Watcom startup code.
open_question: What the magic status word 0x810C at 00069e20 actually means was not settled - determining that requires reading 0003bfa5, which is a separate ticket. If 00069e20 is the status field of an MSCDEX device request header then 0x810C decodes as error|done with error code 0x0C, but that could not be confirmed from this function. Also unresolved: whether the flag at 00069e54 is a plain "CD subsystem already initialised" latch. The return type is recorded as short on the strength of main's CWDE; int is the alternative reading.

name: fdps_cd_audio_is_idle
role: Issues an MSCDEX device request through the CD request builder at 0003c34f and reports whether the request header status word has the busy bit clear, i.e. whether CD audio playback has stopped.
plate_comment:
Query whether the CD-ROM drive has finished the current audio playback.

Algorithm:
  1. Watcom stack-overflow probe: PUSH 4 / CALL __STK at 0004361a (compiler
     prologue, not a real argument to this function).
  2. Calls the CD request builder at 0003c34f, which fills a DOS device driver
     request header and submits it via fdps_cd_device_request (0003bb7d).
  3. Tail-jumps into the shared epilogue at 0003c6d0, which loads the 16-bit
     request header status word at 0069e20, clears the low byte (error code
     bits), masks AH with 0x02 (status bit 9 = BUSY) and returns SETZ of the
     result. So the value is 1 when the drive is no longer busy and 0 while it
     is still busy.
  The neighbouring function at 0003c6bc falls through into the same epilogue
  after issuing a different request; 0003c6d0 is a shared tail, not a callee in
  the source.

Parameters:
  none. The pushed 4 belongs to the Watcom stack-check helper.

Returns:
  16-bit flag in AX: 1 when the request header BUSY bit (0x0200) is clear
  (audio idle / command complete), 0 while the drive reports busy.
evidence: Only caller is fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll (00030c50), which polls to restart background music when a track ends, so the return value is a playback-finished predicate. The single real callee 0003c34f calls fdps_cd_device_request (0003bb7d), placing this squarely in the already-named CD-ROM/MSCDEX subsystem, hence pool fdps. The PUSH 4 / CALL 0004361a pair is the Watcom stack probe: 0004361a is called at the entry of many functions in this region with different constants (8 at 0003c6bc, 4 here, 0x30 at 0003c6f9) and pops its own argument (no ADD ESP follows, and the shared RET at 0003c6e7 would otherwise be unbalanced), so it is CRT, not a game call. Raw bytes at 0003c6d0 decode as MOV AX,[0069e20] / XOR AL,AL / AND AH,2 / MOVZX / TEST / SETZ / MOVZX AX,AL / RET, which is the classic DOS device driver request header status test on bit 9 (BUSY) after masking off the low error-code byte. No arguments arrive on the stack for this function itself, so __watcall.
open_question: The exact MSCDEX request code that 0003c34f builds was not read (that function is a separate ticket), so it is not proven that the polled request is specifically the audio-status IOCTL rather than a generic device-status request; the busy-bit semantics and the caller make audio-idle the reading, but the name could need narrowing to fdps_cd_request_not_busy if 0003c34f turns out to be generic.

name: fdps_cd_play_track
role: Starts CD audio playback of one track: stops whatever is playing, selects the requested track, resolves its start/end sector positions into two globals and issues the play command.
plate_comment:
Starts CD-DA playback of a single track.

Algorithm:
1. Calls the argument-forwarding thunk at 0004361a with the constant 0x0c (the thunk swaps the pushed value into EAX, calls 0004362d and returns popping its argument, so ESP is unchanged on return).
2. Calls fdps_cd_stop_audio to halt any track currently playing.
3. Sign-extends the 16-bit track argument at [ESP+4] and passes it to FUN_0003c0c8, which selects/queries the requested track (caller cleans the 4-byte argument).
4. Calls FUN_0003c803, the only writer of the globals at 00069dec and 00069de4; it derives the playback start and end positions for the selected track (00069de4 is written on two paths, i.e. the end position is conditional).
5. Pushes 00069de4 then 00069dec and calls FUN_0003c452, so that routine receives (value_at_00069dec, value_at_00069de4) - the start and end positions - and performs the actual play request. The 8 bytes of arguments are cleaned by this function.

Parameters:
  track - 16-bit track index, passed on the stack and read with MOVSX from [ESP+4].

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX is not set deliberately; the value left in it comes from the last call.
evidence: Subsystem is certain: the function sits in the 0003c0c8-0003c891 CD cluster, its second call is the already-named fdps_cd_stop_audio at 0003c4a7, and one of its three callers is the already-named fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll at 00030c50. The stop-then-select-then-play ordering plus the pair of position globals (written only by FUN_0003c803, read only here, handed straight to FUN_0003c452) is the standard MSCDEX play-audio-from-to sequence, which makes 'play one track' the role. Convention is __cdecl by disassembly: the sole argument is read as word ptr [ESP+4] after a callee-cleaning thunk (RET 0x4) restores ESP, the function returns with a bare RET leaving the argument for the caller, and it cleans its own outgoing arguments with ADD ESP,0x4 / ADD ESP,0x8. Pool is fdps - no CRT or Miles AIL signature anywhere in the chain, and the executable has no import table.
open_question: The meaning of the constant 0x0c passed through the thunk at 0004361a is unresolved - it could be a delay, a device/driver selector or a mode code; 0004362d was not read. The exact split between FUN_0003c0c8 (track select/query) and FUN_0003c803 (position computation) is inferred from the write xrefs to 00069dec/00069de4 rather than read directly, and the argument order of FUN_0003c452 (start,end vs end,start) is assumed from the push order.

name: crt_malloc
role: Public cdecl malloc entry point: a five-instruction thunk that forwards its single stack argument to the Watcom near-heap allocator core at 0003d383 and returns the resulting block pointer in EAX.
plate_comment:
Watcom C library malloc.

Algorithm: Loads the caller-pushed size from [ESP+4], re-pushes it, calls the near-heap allocator core at 0003d383 (which rounds the request up to a 4-byte multiple with a 12-byte minimum, rejects zero and sizes >= 0xFFFFFFD5, walks the heap list at DAT_00060388/DAT_0006038c/DAT_00060390, and falls back to heap expansion), then pops the argument and returns. The thunk itself performs no bookkeeping; the allocator's return value is left untouched in EAX. Because the callee also clears the out-of-memory flag DAT_00069ead, no error handling happens here.

Parameters: size - number of bytes requested, passed on the stack (cdecl); the caller removes it.

Returns: pointer to the allocated block, or NULL when the size is zero, out of range, or the heap cannot satisfy the request.
evidence: Body is MOV EDX,[ESP+4] / PUSH EDX / CALL 0003d383 / ADD ESP,4 / RET, so the argument arrives on the stack and this function cleans its own forwarded copy while the caller cleans the original - verified at the call site 000296bd, where fdps_load_global_resources does PUSH 0xA00 / CALL 0003d375 / ADD ESP,4 / MOV [00064108],EAX, i.e. a byte count in and a stored pointer out. The callee 0003d383 is unmistakably the Watcom near-heap allocator: zero-size and size >= 0xFFFFFFD5 rejection, (size+3) & ~3 rounding with a 12-byte floor, a free-list walk over DAT_00060388/0006038c/00060390 with per-block +0x14 size fields, and heap-expansion retries via 000442d0 / 000444a1. That callee is also reached directly from three other CRT routines (000430a1, 000556a9, 0005600f - the calloc/realloc/strdup family), which is exactly the layering of malloc over _nmalloc in the Watcom 10.0a C library. Around 90 distinct game functions across every subsystem call this thunk, matching a general-purpose allocator rather than any game-specific routine, so the pool is crt and the name is crt_malloc.
open_question: In the flat 32-bit model Watcom aliases malloc and _nmalloc onto the same code, so this thunk could equally be the _nmalloc public entry; the disassembly cannot distinguish them and the distinction does not affect the rebuild.

name: crt_free
role: Public C library free(): forwards the caller's heap pointer to the internal near-heap release routine that locates the owning mini-heap and returns the block to the free list.
plate_comment:
Watcom C library free().

Algorithm: Loads the single stack argument from [ESP+4], pushes it and calls the internal near-heap release routine at 0003d486, then pops the argument. The internal routine walks the mini-heap segment list starting at the heap-begin pointer (DAT_00060388) until it finds the segment whose range contains the pointer, hands the block plus the owning segment to the free-list insert helper (FUN_00043d94), updates the largest-free-block-before-rover cache (DAT_00060390) when the segment is not the rover segment (DAT_0006038c), and clears the heap-state flag at DAT_00069ead. This wrapper adds nothing beyond the stack-to-stack call, which is the usual free()/__nfree() split in the Watcom runtime.

Parameters: void *ptr - pointer previously returned by the matching allocator; behaviour for a pointer outside every mini-heap segment is whatever the internal routine does, no validation happens here.

Returns: nothing.
evidence: Body is a five-instruction forwarder: MOV EDX,[ESP+4] / PUSH EDX / CALL 0003d486 / ADD ESP,4 / RET. The target 0003d486 is textbook Watcom __nfree: it iterates the mini-heap chain from __nheapbeg (DAT_00060388) via the next field at offset 8, breaks on the segment containing the pointer, calls the block-release helper FUN_00043d94(ptr, DS, segment), and then does the __MiniHeapRover / __LargestSizeB4Rover comparison (DAT_0006038c, DAT_00060390) against the segment's largest_blk field at offset 0x14 - a sequence that only exists in the Watcom heap. 0003d486 additionally has six other CRT-internal callers (realloc/heap maintenance range 000430a1-000556a9), while 0003d478 is called from ~95 distinct game functions spread across battle, village, shop, savegame, title and resource-loading code, which is the caller profile of the public free() rather than of any game-specific routine. Pool crt follows from the heap implementation being runtime code, not FDPS code. Convention is __cdecl because the argument arrives on the stack at [ESP+4] and the function ends in a plain RET, leaving cleanup to the caller; this matches the binary-wide -4s stack calling convention recorded in rebuild_info/build_flags.md.
open_question: The exact identity of the byte flag cleared at DAT_00069ead (a heap-state or heap-dirty flag inside the runtime) is not settled, but it lives in the callee, not in this function.

name: AIL_shutdown
role: Public Miles AIL API entry point that logs the call "AIL_shutdown()" to the AIL debug log and then invokes the internal shutdown routine that tears down the audio driver stack.
plate_comment:
Miles Sound System AIL API entry point: AIL_shutdown().

Algorithm:
The function is the standard Miles API wrapper generated for every public AIL
entry point. It increments the global API nesting depth counter at 0x00069e6c
on entry and decrements it on exit. If the debug log is enabled (0x00069e80
non-zero) and either this is the outermost API call (depth == 1) or nested
logging is enabled (0x00069e84 non-zero), and the "inside interrupt/DOS-unsafe"
guard at 0x00044f42 returns zero, and the log-line prologue helper at 0x0003d676
succeeds, then the literal text "AIL_shutdown()\n" at 0x000623a5 is written to
the log file handle held in 0x00069e7c via the printf-style writer at 0x00045183
(cdecl, two stack arguments cleaned by the caller).
The real work is then performed by the internal shutdown routine at 0x00045af9,
which takes no arguments. Afterwards the same log-enable test is repeated and,
if it passes, the log stream at 0x00069e7c is flushed through 0x000428be.
The function has no early exits and always falls through to the depth decrement.

Parameters:
None.

Returns:
Nothing.
evidence:
The only string reference is the literal "AIL_shutdown()
" at 0x000623a5, which sits in a dense block of Miles AIL API name strings ("AIL_set_preference(%d,%d)
", "Result = %d
", "AIL_get_..."). The body is the textbook Miles API-wrapper shape: nesting-depth counter, log-enable flag, nested-log flag, log file handle, an interrupt-safety guard, a fprintf-style write of the API name, the real implementation call, and a stream flush. The function itself takes no parameters and returns nothing, matching AIL_shutdown's upstream signature. Pool is ail because the code and its string live in the linked-in Miles library, and the name uses upstream Miles casing per the project naming rules. Only two callers, both in the game's own code, consistent with a shutdown API called from teardown paths.
open_question: The internal worker at 0x00045af9 and the helpers 0x0003d676 / 0x00044f42 / 0x000428be were not inspected, so the exact teardown steps and the precise meaning of each global (0x00069e6c depth, 0x00069e7c handle, 0x00069e80 / 0x00069e84 log flags) are inferred from the wrapper shape rather than read directly.

name: crt_exit
role: Watcom C runtime `exit()`: runs the first two runtime finalizer hooks, then tail-calls the `_exit` stage with the same status code, terminating the program.
plate_comment:
C runtime exit().

Algorithm:
  Calls two runtime finalizer hooks indirectly through the function-pointer
  slots at 0x000603a0 and 0x000603a4, then pushes its own status argument and
  calls the next termination stage at 0x00042e29 (_exit), cleaning the argument
  off the stack afterwards.

  The three adjacent slots 0x000603a0 / 0x000603a4 / 0x000603a8 form the
  runtime's finalizer hook table. exit() runs slots [0] and [1]; the _exit
  stage at 0x00042e29 runs slots [1] and [2] and then jumps into the cstart
  termination tail at 0x00043527, which pops the status into EAX and reaches
  INT 21h AH=4Ch. In this build all three slots are statically initialised to
  0x00042e0e, a bare RET stub, i.e. no finalizer module was linked in, so the
  hooks are effectively no-ops.

  The trailing RET is unreachable: control never comes back from 0x00042e29.
  This function does not return.

Parameters:
  [ESP+4]  int status - process exit code, forwarded unchanged to _exit and
           ultimately to the DOS terminate call.

Returns:
  Does not return.
evidence:
Body is 7 instructions: CALL [0x000603a0]; CALL [0x000603a4]; MOV EDX,[ESP+4]; PUSH EDX; CALL 0x00042e29; ADD ESP,4; RET.

Caller context is decisive. FUN_0004df4c is Watcom's __CMain: it computes the stack size from DAT_00060438, calls the init-routine chain at 0x00054dbc, then does MOV EDX,[0x0006a3b8]; PUSH EDX; MOV EBX,[0x0006a3b4]; PUSH EBX; CALL 0x00029220 (argv/envp pointers -> main); ADD ESP,8; PUSH EAX; CALL 0x00042e0f. That is literally `exit( main( argc, argv, envp ) )`, which fixes this function as exit() and 0x00029220 as main. __CMain itself is reached from the cstart stub at 0x00043522 (the INT 21h AH=30h / DPMI "DX"/"CB"/INT 31h startup block at 0x00043310).

Callee chain confirms termination: 0x00042e29 calls hooks [0x000603a4] and [0x000603a8], pushes the same status, and JMPs to 0x00043527, which does POP EAX and falls into 0x0004354d -> PUSH EAX; ... ; POP EAX; MOV AH,0x4C; INT 0x21 (DOS terminate-with-return-code). So the status pushed here ends up as the DOS exit code.

Data evidence: read_memory at 0x00060398 gives 00 00 00 00 | 01 00 00 00 | 0e 2e 04 00 | 0e 2e 04 00 | 0e 2e 04 00, i.e. slots 0x603a0/0x603a4/0x603a8 all hold 0x00042e0e, and 0x00042e0e disassembles to a single RET. No code anywhere writes those three slots (get_xrefs_to shows only the two READ references from 00042e0f and the two from 00042e29), so they are link-time-initialised finalizer hooks left at the empty default. Neighbouring slots in the same block are cstart's own globals (0x000603ac is written by the DOS/4G startup at 0x00043398, 0x000603b0 stores the GS selector at 0x000433e3), placing this table squarely in the runtime data area.

Caller count also fits exit(): 11 callers = __CMain (0x0004df4c), main itself (0x00029220), and 9 scattered game functions (0x000177d0, 0x00017ca0, 0x0001a4c0, 0x00023e20, 0x00029400, 0x00029660, 0x0002a140, 0x0002a240, 0x0002e640) — the shape of fatal-error bail-outs, not of a game-logic helper.

No strings are referenced; none are expected for this routine.
open_question: The exact upstream Watcom names of the three finalizer hook slots (0x000603a0 / 0x000603a4 / 0x000603a8) cannot be recovered from this binary — all three hold the same empty RET stub, so nothing distinguishes them here.
